Job Description: 

About the Group

Intel Foundry is a systems foundry dedicated to transforming the global semiconductor industry by delivering cutting-edge silicon process and packaging technology leadership for the AI era. With a focus on scalability, AI advancement, and shaping the future, we provide an unparalleled blend of an industry-leading technology, a rich IP portfolio, a world-class design ecosystem, and an operationally resilient global manufacturing supply chain.


Intel Foundry will be differentiated from other foundries with a combination of leading-edge packaging and process technology, committed capacity in the US and Europe, and a world-class IP portfolio that customers can choose from, including x86 cores, graphics, media, display, AI, interconnect, fabric and other critical foundational IP's, along with Arm and RISC-V ecosystem IP's. Foundry Services will also provide access to silicon design services to help our customers seamlessly turn silicon into solutions, using industry standard design packages. Come join us and do something wonderful.


The Aerospace, Defense, Government (ADG) - The Senior DFT Logic Design Engineer provides technical support to Intel Foundry Services customers on our PDKs, DFT/DFM insertion, ATPG validation methodology and flows.

The successful candidate will:

  • Collaborate with internal teams across Intel and external stakeholders such as foundry customers' design teams, IP providers, and EDA vendors on issue resolution.
  • Create content, application notes and deliver technical training/presentations.
  • Drive quality of ASIC DFT/DFM and ATPG validation methodology, capability/flow and documentation for block level and SOC level.
  • Support and provide Tool/Flow/Methodology on customer issues and challenges for successful customer tape-outs, and to increase customer satisfaction.

Core Competencies

  • Customer-oriented attitude and mindset.
  • Self-driven and results-oriented, capable of effectively working multiple tasks.
  • Team player - effective team-work skillset to drive and find solutions for customer design implementation issues/challenges.
  • Analytical problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication skills, as well as experience in collaboration, listening and providing feedback.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Ability to obtain a US Government Security Clearance.
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical / Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or in a STEM related field of study.
  • 3+ years of experience with advanced CMOS processes (16nm and below).
  • 3+ years of experience in implementing ASIC DFT/DFM insertion (MBIST, LBIST, SCAN, JTAG, ...) at ASIC design block level and at full chip level. Performing ATPG validation and DFT timing and DFT signoff at SOC level.

title: Senior Analog Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.

Business group

Intel Integrated Photonics Solutions (IPS), part of the Data Center Group, is a leader in silicon photonics integration. Our team drives innovation through advanced technology and scalable, high-volume manufacturing of silicon photonics products. We are committed to developing next-generation optical connectivity solutions that enable continued data center bandwidth growth through smaller form factors, co-packaged optics, and data rates scaling from 400G today to 3.2T and beyond.
 

The Role and Impact

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Analog Design Engineer to join our growing team and help accelerate the development of industry-leading silicon photonics solutions. As a Senior Analog Design Engineer, you will contribute to the Silicon Photonics Solutions Group's mission of transforming data center connectivity and strengthening Intel's leadership in networking technologies.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • The architecture, design, implementation, and validation of high-speed analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in advanced optical interconnect products.
  • You will collaborate closely with cross-functional design teams to deliver innovative solutions from concept through production.
  • Define circuit architectures and develop designs that meet power, performance, and functionality requirements for next-generation optical interconnects.
  • Lead block-level design and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver key integrated circuit components.
  • Architect, design, and validate high-speed, low-voltage, low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits.
  • Work closely with digital design teams to ensure successful integration and product execution.
  • Plan and execute design activities while balancing performance, schedule, and quality objectives.
  • Guide to the development of post-silicon test and characterization plans.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive design documentation, including design specifications, reviews, and technical reports.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences. 


Minimum Qualifications:
M.S. degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field with 3+ years of industry experience or PhD & 0 years in the following:

  • Hands-on experience designing high-speed circuit blocks such as amplifiers, drivers, equalizers, PLLs, phase interpolators, and clock and data recovery (CDR) circuits for data rates of 32 Gbps and above.
  • Experience designing inductors, transmission lines, transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs), and optical modulator drivers.
  • Strong expertise in high-speed serial link design and analog CMOS/BiCMOS circuit design using deep-submicron process technologies.
  • Experience with full-chip integration, ESD design considerations, and verification methodologies.



Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with optical communication systems.
  • Experience developing 400G, 800G, and 1.6T optical links.
  • Experience with package design and test setup development.
  • Experience designing precision analog circuits such as ADCs and DACs.
  • Experience with PAM4 and NRZ link architectures.
  • Strong understanding of mixed-signal design methodologies and flows.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

title: Quality And Reliability Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Manufacturing Quality and Reliability Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring Intel's manufacturing ramps transition seamlessly to high-volume production while maintaining exceptional product quality and reliability standards. You will evaluate materials, processes, and testing mechanisms, conduct quality audits, and implement improvements that directly enhance Intel's ability to deliver cutting-edge technology solutions. Your contributions will foster a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence, driving impact across manufacturing and customer satisfaction.

Business Group
You will join Intel's Foundry manufacturing quality and reliability team, an organization dedicated to upholding world-class standards across Intel's manufacturing operations. Collaborating across product engineering, manufacturing, and supplier engagements, the team ensures Intel's products consistently meet rigorous quality requirements while supporting Intel's broader mission of delivering innovative solutions that shape the future of technology.

Key Responsibilities
- Evaluate and qualify manufacturing ramps and processes to ensure compliance with quality and reliability standards.
- Develop systems for early detection and containment of manufacturing excursions while conducting risk assessments.
- Drive continuous process improvements and proactive quality programs in factories to promote a quality mindset.
- Conduct quality assessments, audits, and analyze reliability data to identify opportunities for improvement.
- Collaborate with product development teams to make recommendations for system, process, and product reliability enhancements.
- Manage excursion containment, change control, and supplier audits, driving supplier continuous improvement initiatives.
- Respond to customer-reported issues by providing engineering solutions to improve customer satisfaction and experience.
- Extract insights from data using statistical techniques and machine learning to evaluate product and system compliance.

- Proven ability to lead and motivate teams within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

title: Construction Tool Install Engineer (Contract)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) is at the heart of building the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing facilities. We are a team of passionate engineers, project managers, and construction professionals dedicated to delivering cutting-edge factories that power Intel's global technology operations. At Intel, we believe in pushing boundaries, fostering innovation, and creating a culture where safety, collaboration, and excellence are at the forefront of everything we do. Join us and be part of a team that is literally building the future of technology.

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Construction Tool Equipment Install Engineer to join our Project Execution Team at our Hillsboro, Oregon campus. In this role, you will serve as the primary Intel equipment owner from pre-design through SL2 Signoff, working closely with factory owners, suppliers, trade contractors, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure the seamless installation of semiconductor manufacturing tools and equipment. This is a hands-on, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of engineering, project management, and construction execution.

This is a fixed-term opportunity lasting approximately 12 months, with the potential for extension subject to the approval of both parties.

Key Responsibilities

  • Equipment & Delivery Management: Collaborate with factory owners and stakeholders to ensure tools, equipment, and kits are ordered and delivered in alignment with the Tool Install schedule. Track and resolve issues in a timely manner, escalating where required.

  • Stakeholder Representation: Represent the local FCS site in CTI and VF forums, acting as the primary point of contact for all equipment-related matters.

  • Financial Planning & Forecasting: Work with stakeholders to forecast equipment workload and funding requirements, ensuring alignment with FCS Financial Planning and Reporting Cycles. Ensure purchase orders and commitments are in place to meet program goals.

  • Systems & Configuration Management: Collaborate with EMS and Systems Owners to ensure systems accurately reflect equipment requirements and schedules. Drive systems and part number configuration, genealogy, and accuracy for RFT Order and Kits delivery.

  • Execution Planning & Coordination: Align all stakeholders to enable detailed execution planning supporting Tool Install Milestones. Lead planning and coordination meetings across multiple suppliers, trade contractors, and project stakeholders.

  • Supplier & Contractor Management: Work with suppliers to ensure business needs are understood and that equipment, materials, and resources are positioned to deliver services on time. Maintain awareness of commercial risks and contractor capacity to enable early course correction.

  • Compliance & Training: Ensure all stakeholders are trained, competent, and compliant with standard operating procedures and protocols.

  • Funding & Change Order Management: Request and process timely funding requests before work commences to prevent After-the-Fact Change Orders (ATFCOs).

  • Continuous Improvement: Review and incorporate cross-site learnings into Tool Install operations. Foster innovation by driving new methods and solutions through leveraging industry insights.

  • Safety Leadership: Build and champion a safety culture of caring across all business environments — from office settings to active construction sites — throughout the full project lifecycle.

  • Project Planning: Translate business and technical requirements into high-quality project plans that enable accurate and cost-effective delivery of scope.

  • Problem Resolution: Act as the primary Intel equipment owner from pre-design through SL2 Signoff, driving troubleshooting efforts to lean, decisive resolution to mitigate delays on assigned projects.

As a successful candidate, you must possess

  • Exceptional Communication: You can confidently manage discussions with executive leadership while also rolling up your sleeves to work through the details hands-on when needed.

  • Strong Leadership: You naturally champion a safety-first culture and inspire those around you to do the same, both on-site and in the office.

  • Collaborative Spirit: You thrive in a highly matrixed environment, building strong relationships with business partners and influencing outcomes without direct authority.

  • Decisive Problem-Solving: You have a talent for identifying challenges early, developing creative solutions, and driving decisions at pace.

  • Adaptability & Resilience: You remain calm under pressure, escalate constraints proactively, and help remove roadblocks to keep projects on track.

  • Innovation Mindset: You continuously look for ways to improve processes, challenge traditional practices, and bring fresh ideas to the table.

  • Planning & Organization: You are meticulous in your planning, ensuring all moving parts are aligned and that nothing falls through the cracks.

If you are passionate about semiconductor manufacturing, construction project execution, and making a tangible impact on the world's most advanced technology facilities, we want to hear from you!

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, architecture, or other related technical field with 1+ years of experience in project or program management, construction or tool install. Experienced may be gained through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training OR master’s degree in engineering, architecture or other related technical field.

Preferred Qualifications:

title: Install Qualification Operations Specialist (Contract)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Install Qualification Operations Specialist is responsible for driving key milestones enabling tool installation, readiness, and qualification within Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS). The role is responsible for equipment install execution from pre-design through design finish and set to SL2 signoff, ensuring safe delivery, accurate scope definition, efficient construction, and prompt vendor qualification.

This position requires five days per week onsite presence and close coordination with manufacturing, design, construction, OEMs, trade contractors, and supplier partners.

This is an onsite position in Hillsboro, Oregon.

Please consider that this is an Intel Contract position (3 years).



Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

Safety and Compliance:

  • Champion Intel's Culture of Caring and ensure safe behaviors across design and construction activities.
  • Enforce cleanroom, IP protection, and site protocols to maintain compliance with all applicable regulations and agency audits.


Install and Qualification Execution:

  • Own key tool installs milestones including set, rigging, placement, hook up, energization, and qual.
  • Support troubleshooting for Supplier Qual and Intel Qual to quickly resolve issues.
  • Drive micro schedule and pull plan development to support tool install milestones.
  • Manage decoupled construction paths SET/SL2 to accelerate readiness.
  • Coordinate testing and facility readiness (LSS, eFIT, TAB, networking, ESOPN)

Design and Scope Alignment

  • Load complete tool install scope in DAC prior to design engagement.
  • Participate in cross functional design reviews with CIT, TICE, Layout, OEMs, and module teams.
  • Validate OEM data and ensure alignment with Intel standards (SEED/EDS/UDS).
  • Support LSP creation, routing validation, POC assignments, and space management.
  • Reduce changes by minimizing DCNs, DCRs, and late-stage modifications.
  • Execution Planning and Stakeholder Coordination:
  • Lead multi supplier coordination meetings and execution planning sessions.
    Translate technical/business requirements into actionable plans and schedules.
  • Forecast equipment and resource needs.
  • Ensure readiness and prompt delivery of tools, prefac kits, global, and parts.
  • Coordinate equipment decon and demo activities.
     

Supplier and Vendor Management:

  • Manage OEMs and third-party vendors to achieve best-in-class qual durations.
  • Drive early vendor enablement and facility readiness using ESOPN. (Equipment sign- off per need).
  • Ensure clean handoff from construction completion to vendor qual finish.
  • Manage contracts, KPIs, and supplier scorecards in partnership with Procurement.

Operations and Continuous Improvement:

  • Oversee contractor and supplier activities in accordance with SLAs.
  • Monitor site operational budget and maximize efficiency.
  • Apply Lean principles to eliminate waste, reduce install durations, and improve quality.
  • Document and share lessons learned across modules and sites.

Business group The Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE) focuses on advancing Intel's hardware and software platforms through innovation and collaboration. Key Responsibilities - Drive customer enabling activities for Intel client platforms across Audio, Computer Vision, Camera, and other software ingredients. - Execute Platform POR features and ensure successful platform bring-up, validation, and customer adoption. - Debug and resolve complex platform issues spanning hardware, firmware, BIOS, operating systems, drivers, middleware, and applications. - Serve as a technical focal point for customer-reported issues, driving root cause analysis and resolution across internal and external stakeholders. - Partner with Microsoft and other OS vendors to investigate and resolve operating system, driver, and platform integration issues. - Collaborate with third-party ecosystem partners including Codec Vendors, Camera Vendors, ISVs, IHVs, ODMs, and OEM customers to drive feature integration and issue resolution. - Collect, analyze, and refine requirements for next-generation solutions and topologies. - Define proof-of-concepts (POCs) and technical evaluations for emerging platform technologies and customer use cases. - Develop technical collaterals, enabling guides, debug methodologies, knowledge repositories, and issue triage frameworks to accelerate customer adoption and support. - Manage Audio and multimedia validation labs, including debug equipment, test infrastructure, and platform readiness activities. - Drive cross-functional collaboration with firmware, BIOS, driver, validation, architecture, and platform engineering teams to resolve customer escalations. - Provide technical leadership during customer engagements, workshops, design reviews, and issue resolution meetings. - Evangelize and provide technical guidance on Intel tools and technologies to enable adoption across various domains.

title: RTL Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.

Life at Intel

As a CPU Logic Design Engineer, you will play a critical role in shaping Intel's next-generation, high-performance microprocessors. Leveraging your technical expertise, you will contribute to the design, development, and optimization of CPUs that drive innovative computing solutions across various industries. By developing cutting-edge logic designs and collaborating with a dynamic, cross-functional team, you will help Intel deliver world-class processors that meet the demands of modern computing applications, including energy-efficient performance and advanced functionality. Your work will directly impact Intel's mission to create world-changing technology and enrich the lives of every person on earth.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop logic design and register transfer level (RTL) coding for CPU components, such as cell libraries, functional units, and CPU IP blocks.
  • Participate actively in defining architecture and microarchitecture features to optimize CPU performance, power, and area.
  • Write RTL and employ strategies to meet power, performance, area, and timing goals while ensuring design integrity and readiness for physical implementation.
  • Review and refine verification plans and tests to ensure correct implementation of design features.
  • Resolve failing RTL tests and implement corrective measures to meet design specifications.
  • Document microarchitectural specifications (MAS) for CPU features and ensure their alignment with project goals.
  • Support SoC customers to achieve seamless integration of the CPU block into larger designs. 

A highly qualified candidate will exhibit the following behavior traits:

·       Demonstrated written and oral communication skills, particularly to an executive audience

·       Skilled at presenting complex information in a simple form.

·       Willingness to thrive in high stress, ambiguous environments, to climb very steep learning curves and rapidly distinguish what is important from what is not important.

As a CPU Design Verification Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring the reliability and functionality of Intel's next-generation CPUs. Mentor engineers in agentic software engineering and the responsible use of AI-assisted development tools.

title: Quantum Packaging Signal/Power Integrity (SI/PI) Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is the world's largest semiconductor company and a global leader in computing innovation. Our Quantum Computing Group represents Intel's bold venture into the next frontier of computing technology, leveraging our decades of semiconductor manufacturing expertise to develop silicon-based quantum processors. We're pioneering spin qubit technology in silicon quantum dots, combining cutting-edge quantum physics with Intel's unmatched manufacturing capabilities to create the world's first commercially viable quantum computers. Our collaborative approach spans Intel's research divisions and partnerships with leading academic institutions worldwide.

We are seeking an exceptional Quantum Packaging Signal/Power Integrity (SI/PI) Engineer to join our pioneering quantum computing team in Oregon. In this role you will be responsible for modeling and simulation of various packaging solutions from silicon redistribution layers to IC substrates within a multidisciplinary team. You'll play a crucial role in advancing Intel's silicon quantum dot technology while contributing to the development of scalable quantum systems that will revolutionize computing.

Key Responsibilities
- Modeling and simulation of packaging hardware including redistribution layers (e.g., interposers, RDLs), IC substrates, and silicon testchip routing
- Work closely with stakeholders to meet design requirements - requirements come from both theory and hardware teams. In some pathfinding projects, you will be asked to participate in creating requirements and novel packaging hardware.
- System-level modelling and simulation; end-to-end simulations to ensure designs meet system-level requirements
- Deliver and disseminate design milestones to stakeholders
- Communicate designs in presentations and relevant documentation
- Stay current with the latest developments in packaging technology and design techniques by attending conferences and reading papers

As a successful candidate, you must possess
- Excellent communication and presentation skills for technical and non-technical audiences
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving capabilities
- Collaborative mindset with ability to work effectively across diverse teams
- Adaptability to work in a fast-paced, innovative research environment
- Passion for pushing the boundaries of quantum technology development

Join Intel's Quantum Computing Group where we are building the future of quantum computing. If you're passionate about working at the forefront of quantum computing packaging and want to work with the resources and expertise of the world's leading semiconductor company, we want to hear from you. Apply today and discover your place in our world-changing work.

title: AI Software Development Engineer - Neuromorphic Computing
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

What if you could help define how developers program an entirely new class of AI hardware?

For nearly a decade, Intel's Neuromorphic Computing Lab, together with a global ecosystem of more than 250 research groups, has advanced architectures, algorithms, and software inspired by the brain's remarkable efficiency, scalability, and adaptability. Our Loihi research chips pioneered event-driven, sparse, and massively parallel neuro-inspired computing, contributing to more than 100 peer-reviewed publications and establishing the potential of this new approach.

Now we are taking the next step: transforming those breakthroughs into technologies for physical AI systems, such as robots and intelligent edge devices that must sense, decide, and act under tight latency and power constraints. This is an opportunity to join at a formative stage and help create the kernels, programming abstractions, and performance models for a new hardware architecture built around sparse, event-driven, and massively parallel computation. Your work will directly influence both the hardware and how developers use it. You will also help shape a software stack designed for an era in which engineers and AI agents build and optimize applications together.

Position Overview

As an AI Software Engineer in Neuromorphic Computing, you will turn new neuromorphic hardware capabilities into working, high-performance AI software and contribute to critical technical areas from design through delivery. You will build specialized kernels for current and next-generation neuromorphic hardware, explore optimization strategies that conventional processors cannot offer, and help shape the programming abstractions that expose those capabilities to developers.

Working alongside hardware architects, compiler engineers, and AI researchers, you will use performance and power models to influence design decisions before silicon is available and then validate those decisions using simulators, emulators, and hardware. Your work will span the full hardware-software lifecycle, from modeling a hardware feature to implementing the kernel that unlocks it and demonstrating measurable gains on real AI workloads. You will contribute to the training, porting, and optimization of end-to-end applications for Loihi-based systems while helping improve engineering quality across the team.

As part of Intel's CTO Office, you will join a vertically integrated incubation effort dedicated to bringing Intel's neuromorphic technology innovations to market. Our diverse team of engineers and researchers has pioneered sparse, event-based neuromorphic architectures across multiple generations and is now focused on commercializing the technology in future Intel and partner products.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:

  • Design and implement specialized AI kernels for neuromorphic hardware using custom DSLs and accelerator programming models such as CUDA and SYCL and help shape the programming abstractions for Intel's next-generation neuromorphic architecture.
  • Develop and optimize operations for convolutional networks, transformers, and generative AI workloads by applying techniques such as tiling, fusion, vectorization, parallelization, layout transformation, buffering, sparsity, and quantization.
  • Develop performance methodologies and improve kernel behavior in areas such as compute utilization, latency, throughput, memory bandwidth, data movement, synchronization, and scaling, turning architectural insights into measurable workload gains.
  • Build reference models, numerical validation tools, benchmarks, and analytical or simulation-based performance, power, and area models that guide hardware-software co-design; reconcile discrepancies across models, simulators, emulators, and hardware.
  • Collaborate with hardware, compiler, runtime, and application engineers to deliver maintainable code, tests, documentation, benchmarks, and performance-regression infrastructure.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • A PhD with no prior professional experience, a master's degree with 2+ years of relevant experience, or a bachelor's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field.
  • 4+ years of experience developing, debugging, and delivering maintainable software in Python and either C or C++, including performance-critical or systems-level code.
  • 2+ years of experience implementing and optimizing numerical, machine-learning, or high-performance computing kernels using parallel programming and either an accelerator programming model, such as CUDA, SYCL, or OpenCL, or a domain-specific language, such as Triton.
  • 2+ years of experience developing, training, or evaluating AI algorithms and machine-learning models using a framework such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.
  • 2+ years of experience establishing numerical correctness and measuring performance using reference implementations, automated testing, benchmarking, profiling, or performance-regression infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications:

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Experience developing or optimizing workloads based on convolutional networks, transformers, generative AI, or other models relevant to edge and physical AI systems.
  • Experience with compiler technologies or domain-specific language development, such as MLIR, LLVM, TVM, Triton, or related toolchains.
  • Experience with hardware performance modeling, architecture simulators, performance, power, and area (PPA) analysis, or hardware-software co-design.
  • Advanced experience with optimization techniques including kernel fusion, tiling, vectorization, quantization, sparsity, layout optimization, or double buffering.
  • Experience developing software for spatial, dataflow, neuromorphic, or other emerging AI accelerator architectures.
  • Experience contributing to collaborative or open-source software projects using code review, continuous integration, documentation, and testing practices.

We are excited to welcome passionate and driven individuals who want to shape the future of AI technology. Your expertise will be invaluable in driving Intel's success and delivering transformative solutions to the world.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

Key Responsibilities:


• Photomask and Reticle Operations: Oversee photomask incoming quality control, pellicle integrity, reticle qualification protocols, and reticle lifecycle management across advanced EUV and DUV toolsets.

• Advanced Pellicle Development: Drive next gen EUV pellicle development, material optimization for enhanced transmission, stability, defect mitigation and overall yield improvement. Optimize reticle usage, inspection and disposition strategies over life cycle.

• Cross-Functional Process Integration: Partner closely with Scanner/Litho teams, Reticle Design, Thin Films, Etch, and Yield Enhancement engineering teams to diagnose patterning excursions and accelerate technology transitions.

Education: M.S. with 8+ years of foundry experience or Ph.D. of Foundry experience in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Optics, Microelectronics, or a related semiconductor engineering discipline.

• Photomask and Reticle Expertise: In-depth knowledge of mask fabrication, mask metrology, aerial image modeling, pellicle technology, reticle degradation mechanisms, and mask defect inspection platforms.


• Lithography Toolset and Process Knowledge: Proven proficiency across DUV (ArFi / 193nm immersion) and EUV exposure systems (ASML Twinscan / NXE platforms), track integration, and advanced CD metrology.


• Analytical and Statistical Mastery: Advanced proficiency with Statistical Process Control (SPC), Design of Experiments (DOE), yield analytics platforms, JMP, Python, or MATLAB for complex data modeling and multivariate analysis.

title: Intel Foundry Advanced Device Development Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

Logic Technology Development (LTD) develops and delivers Intel's leading-edge silicon process technologies for both Intel products and Intel Foundry customers. LTD is responsible for creating process technologies that meet targets for performance, power, area, yield, reliability, cost, and schedule while ensuring they can be successfully transferred into high-volume manufacturing.

About the Role

This position is in the Logic Technology Development (LTD) team working in one of the most advanced semiconductor cleanroom facilities in the world. You will be designing, executing, and analyzing experiments necessary to meet engineering specifications for their process.

The Advanced Device Development Engineering Manager is responsible for leading scientific research device group enabling the manufacture of innovative device architectures

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead a team of device engineers to develop a high-volume capable process technology that meets performance, yield, and reliability requirements for both internal and foundry products. This includes both physical and electrical data analysis, as well as extensive interaction with other technology development teams (integration, module, design/modeling and reliability)
  • Set priorities of a team embedded in programs targeted for foundry offerings to get results across boundaries, ensure an inclusive work environment, develop employee careers and manage team performance.
  • Work closely with LTD core program integration and device organization to ensure the high-quality Process-Design Kit (PDK) is delivered to design enablement team. It includes extensive Silicon-to-Simulation (or model-hardware correlation) analysis/target projection, layout effect validation and electrical monitors to product parametric correlation.
  • Collaborate closely with LTD foundry technology engineering group to ensure the customer achieves leadership product performance and derives maximum value from Intel's advanced manufacturing technologies.
  • Define robust test structures and test programs to validate advanced design rules and reliably extract key device parameters.
  • Use Statistics, Data Mining, and other data analysis techniques to collect, explore, and extract insights from Electrical-test, yield, and fab data to define future development direction.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Experience in advanced node semiconductor industry in one or more of the following:
    • Semiconductor materials
    • Fabrication
    • Device physics
    • Electrical characterization of Semiconductor Devices (transistor, diode, etc.)

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Advanced Transistor Device Structures and Device Physics.
  • Process monitoring Test structures design and layout experience.
  • Device and circuit simulation.
  • Statistical Process Control (SPC) or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles and engineering analysis tools.
  • Expertise in database structures, research methods, machine learning, analytics packages (i.e., JMP, MATLAB, Octave), scripting languages (i.e., JSL, Perl, TCL), or programming languages (i.e., Python, SQL, C/C++)
  • Expertise in agentic AI and orchestrated LLM workflows, machine learning, deep learning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), knowledge engineering, and dataflow pipeline architectures.

Qualifications:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Material Science, or scientific field of study directly related to Semiconductor.
  • Ph.D. with 10+ years of experience in advanced node semiconductor industry OR Masters with 15+ of experience.

title: Senior CPU Silicon Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Join Intel's architecture team as a Senior CPU Silicon Analysis Engineer. In this role, you will be central to in-depth studies of CPU designs, providing critical data-driven guidance for future CPU roadmap decisions. You will own silicon bring-up, maintenance, and a wide range of measurements to characterize processor behavior across power, performance, and physical operating conditions. Your findings will directly influence architectural decisions at the highest levels of Intel's CPU development organization.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and operate lab infrastructure for systematic silicon characterization, including bring-up, maintenance, and debug of pre-production and production platforms
  • Plan and execute measurements across a broad range of metrics including performance, IPC, power, dynamic capacitance, leakage, voltage-frequency curves, and microarchitectural telemetry
  • Design and execute structured measurement campaigns to characterize silicon behavior under a variety of operating conditions, workloads, and thermal/power envelopes
  • Analyze and interpret silicon data to identify power/performance gaps, anomalies, and opportunities relative to architectural expectations and roadmap targets
  • Collaborate with architecture, benchmarking, backend design, and simulation teams to correlate lab results with pre-silicon models and design data, and to drive root cause analysis of discrepancies
  • Develop tooling, scripts, and automation to streamline data collection, processing, and reporting pipelines
  • Communicate findings clearly through technical reports and presentations to engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

To Be Successful in This Role, You Should Demonstrate

  • A methodical, detail-oriented approach to lab work and data analysis, with the discipline to maintain accuracy across complex, multi-dimensional data sets
  • Strong collaborative instincts and the ability to work effectively across architecture, design, and simulation teams to drive alignment and root cause resolution
  • Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to translate technical findings into actionable insights for both engineering peers and leadership audiences

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline with 8+ years of relevant industry experience, OR a Master's Degree in a related discipline with 6+ years of relevant industry experience
  • Hands-on experience with silicon lab environments, including platform bring-up, debug, and instrumentation
  • Experience collecting and analyzing silicon power and performance metrics such as IPC, Frequency, Cdyn, leakage, and microarchitectural telemetries
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash, or similar) for test automation and data analysis
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to draw actionable conclusions from complex, multi-dimensional silicon data sets

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience characterizing CPU silicon across a range of designs and operating conditions
  • Familiarity with EMON/PMU-based performance profiling and OS-level performance tooling
  • Understanding of CPU microarchitecture sufficient to interpret performance counter data and correlate measurements to architectural behavior
  • Exposure to backend design concepts such as voltage-frequency corner selection, leakage-frequency tradeoffs, and process library characteristics

  • Background in silicon-based benchmarking and performance characterization of processor designs

title: HPC System Architecture
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The HPC System Architect is the senior technical lead responsible for defining the next generation of Intel's leading-edge high-performance computing systems. Reporting directly to Nic Dube, Corporate Vice President and General Manager of Data Center Systems and Solutions, this position owns forward-looking HPC system architecture from concept through committed definition.

You will work directly with Intel's CPU and GPU teams to architect the systems that follow today's products - shaping silicon requirements, and defining system-level architecture for the large-scale, scale-out clusters that characterize production HPC. The role spans full-system definition: compute node design, memory and I/O balance, scale-out fabric and topology, and the software stack that determines delivered application performance at scale.

You will engage directly with the customers that set the leading edge of HPC - DOE national laboratories and their exascale and post-exascale programs, financial services institutions, oil and gas operators, and major academic and government research computing centers - translating their workload and facility requirements into system architectures Intel can build, and Intel's roadmap into system concepts they can commit to.

Responsibilities

  • Own system-level architecture for next-generation HPC clusters: node definition, CPU and GPU configuration, memory bandwidth-to-capacity balance, I/O and parallel storage architecture, and scale-out fabric and topology.
  • Define scale-out interconnect architecture - fabric selection, network topology, bisection bandwidth and blocking ratios, collective and communication performance, and resilience at thousands-of-node scale.
  • Partner with the CPU and GPU teams to define product requirements for future HPC systems, bringing system-level and workload evidence into silicon definition while requirements remain open.
  • Build performance models that project delivered application throughput at scale on unreleased silicon and use them to drive configuration and roadmap decisions.
  • Lead architecture co-design and benchmark definition with leadership HPC customers, including acceptance criteria for standard and customer-proprietary application suites.
  • Drive HPC requirements into Intel's CPU, GPU, platform, and software roadmaps across DCG and the product and design organizations.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies for next-generation HPC systems, including advanced memory, Ultra Ethernet and other scale-out fabric standards, optical interconnect, and heterogeneous accelerator integration.
  • Produce reference architectures and system specifications that platform teams, OEM and ODM partners, and system integrators can build to.
  • Grow and lead HPC architecture capability within the team, providing technical direction and mentorship to architects and engineers.

Successful Candidate Profile

  • Deep expertise in HPC system architecture at cluster scale, spanning CPU and GPU configuration, memory subsystem design, scale-out interconnect, and parallel storage.
  • Demonstrated experience defining systems around unreleased silicon and influencing CPU or accelerator requirements from a system and workload perspective.
  • Fluency with HPC workload characteristics and performance analysis, including quantitative reasoning about scaling behavior, communication patterns, and bottlenecks at scale.
  • Working knowledge of the HPC software stack - MPI, OpenMP, GPU programming models, schedulers, and math and communication libraries.
  • Proven credibility with sophisticated technical customers in high-stakes procurement and co-design settings.
  • Strong understanding of the competitive HPC landscape, including alternative CPU and accelerator architectures, fabric options, and system vendor positioning.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, effective with both deep technical audiences and executive stakeholders.
  • Comfort with high ambiguity and a track record of driving clarity in undefined technical areas.
  • Willingness to travel domestically and internationally for customer engagements and technical conferences.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in HPC, data center, or server system architecture, design, or engineering.
5+ years of experience in a customer-facing or externally-facing technical role.
Demonstrated experience defining or deploying large-scale compute clusters.

Preferred Qualifications
Master's degree or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
Experience defining next-generation systems in partnership with CPU or GPU product and design teams.
Experience supporting DOE national laboratory or comparable large-scale public-sector HPC procurements.
Domain experience in a definitional HPC vertical: financial services, oil and gas and seismic processing, weather and climate, computational chemistry or biology, or manufacturing and CAE.
Hands-on experience with scale-out fabrics including InfiniBand, Ultra Ethernet, or other high-performance interconnect.
Experience with system-level performance modeling and workload characterization at scale.
Experience with converged HPC and AI system design.

title: Software Engineering - PhD Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact


Intel is seeking a highly motivated Software Research Intern (PhD) to join the TCAD Process Reliability Modeling team within Intel Foundry. This internship offers an opportunity to work on advanced computational software solutions supporting semiconductor technology development. The selected candidate will contribute to cutting-edge software applications and solution methodologies like chip-package interactions, thermal transport and thermal management, thin films development and patterning.


The internship is designed for PhD students interested in applying software engineering and research expertise to solve complex engineering challenges while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across Intel. 

Business Group


The Intel Foundry Technology organization is focused on driving semiconductor process innovation and enabling future technology nodes. Within the LTD-TD TCAD team, engineers and researchers develop advanced simulation, modeling, and software solutions used to accelerate technology development. The team fosters a collaborative environment where software, mathematics, physics, and engineering intersect to solve challenging technical problems.

Key Responsibilities


  • Design, develop, and optimize software solutions for engineering and research applications. 
  • Develop simulations capabilities using numerical methods like finite element, level sets, or related techniques. 
  • Develop modeling-based methodologies to solve device and interconnect process, module and reliability problems.
  • Establish criteria and methods to determine proper inputs and validate results. 
  • Collaborate with software engineers, researchers, and domain experts to deliver scalable and maintainable solutions. 
  • Document technical solutions and present findings to project stakeholders.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


  • Must be a full-time student pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Material Science, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering or a semiconductor-related field.
  • Must have a minimum of a 3.0 GPA in college courses to date.
  • 1+ year experience programming in C/C++/Python or equivalent.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and software development skills.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience with using TCAD or atomistic simulation tools to study thermo-mechanical and chip/package interactions, thermal transport, thin film deposition processes, patterning, material chemical interactions or circuit performance.
  • Hands on experience development and/or using finite element or equivalent solvers for solutions of physical systems.
  • Experience with physics-based modeling, AI/machine learning methodologies for the analysis of solid mechanics, thermal management, reliability and manufacturing process of microprocessors devices.

This is your opportunity to develop your expertise, gain hands-on experience, and make a meaningful impact within a collaborative environment that drives the future of technology. We look forward to seeing how your skills and passion will contribute to our innovative team.

title: Senior Advanced Packaging Defect Inspection Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Advanced Packaging Technology Development (APTD) Metrology Group at Intel sits at the heart of our most critical technology development and pathfinding programs. As packaging architectures grow increasingly complex, the role of metrology has evolved far beyond traditional inspection and measurement — it has become a strategic enabler of technology progress, yield learning, and program decision-making confidence.


We are seeking a Senior Module Development Engineer who combines deep hands-on expertise in next-generation metrology equipment with a broad, current awareness of where the semiconductor metrology industry is heading.


The ideal candidate brings the technical credibility to work at the equipment level and the strategic clarity to translate industry knowledge into a forward-looking roadmap that keeps our capabilities ahead of program demand. This requires genuine engagement with the global metrology landscape — staying current with advances in measurement science, emerging equipment capabilities, and evolving industry standards — and applying that knowledge with sound judgment and determine which capabilities are worth pursuing and when.


This engineer will be embedded in our most advanced development and pathfinding programs from their earliest stages — ensuring that measurement strategies are defined, equipment is ready, and metrology coverage is in place before process flows are locked and before gaps can become program risks. A critical dimension of this role is the end-to-end qualification of new metrology equipment — taking ownership from initial tool installation and acceptance testing through process validation and full fab readiness — ensuring every new tool meets the performance and capability standards our programs require.


This engineer will also serve as a key technical resource for fab support, and ensuring the metrology tool fleet consistently operates at the highest level of performance and availability. The ability to move fluidly between strategic roadmap work and hands-on fab problem solving is essential — and is what makes this role both uniquely challenging and uniquely rewarding.


This is a role that demands technical depth, industry awareness, and the ability to lead with influence across a wide range of partners — from process integration and module engineering to advanced process control, AI and automation, and senior program leadership. The ideal candidate resolves complex process challenges with the same confidence and credibility they bring to presenting a technology investment case to senior leadership.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Drive technology development and enablement across both high-volume manufacturing and future technology nodes — delivering process integration and equipment solutions that meet desired device specifications and performance targets
  • Lead the design and development of technically sophisticated metrology and inspection processes  including material selection, parameter optimization, equipment configuration, and system design to enable new product architectures and functional requirements
  • Define and own the metrology group's long-range technology roadmap translating a deep understanding of industry trends, emerging measurement technologies, and program requirements into a clear, prioritized strategy that keeps our capabilities ahead of demand
  • Perform pathfinding activities in support of process and hardware development enabling the manufacturing of innovative device architectures and developing roadmaps for technologies that support future program needs.
  • Conduct process technology feasibility studies through theoretical simulations and practical engineering methods providing early, evidence-based assessments of new measurement approaches before committing to full qualification Evaluate and qualify next-generation metrology and inspection equipment end-to-end — from installation and acceptance testing through process validation and full fab readiness — ensuring every new tool meets the performance and capability standards our programs require.
  • Serve as the primary technical resource for fab support — providing engineering disposition on process excursions, driving resolution of metrology-related program holds, and maintaining the tool fleet at the highest level of performance and availability.
  • Recommend and implement equipment and process modifications that improve production efficiency, optimize output, and enhance manufacturing techniques for both existing and next-generation products.
  • Partner with key equipment and materials suppliers to develop and implement enabling elements of the technology — building direct technical relationships that go beyond standard supplier engagement to actively co-shape next-generation tool capabilities and roadmaps.
  • Remain current on relevant industry process, materials, and metrology trends — developing a forward-looking view of future technology needs and partnering with the vendor ecosystem to build a cost-sensitive, capability-driven roadmap that pushes the industry forward.
  • Lead metrology module development across multiple concurrent advanced packaging programs — taking full ownership from first wafer through process sign-off, including recipe development, specification setting, SPC strategy, and sampling plan definition.
  • Design and implement rapid inline feedback mechanisms that compress the time between experiment execution and actionable insight — directly accelerating cycles of learning across TD and pathfinding programs.
  • Collaborate with AI, machine learning, and advanced process control teams to develop intelligent monitoring and excursion detection strategies — evolving from threshold-based alarms toward predictive, context-aware process control.
  • Represent the metrology group in cross-functional program reviews — communicating metrology readiness, capability status, and risk with clarity and credibility to integration, process, and senior program leadership teams

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research and relevant previous job and/or internship experience.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in materials science, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, physics, chemistry, or related STEM field with 4+ years of relevant experience.
  • OR master’s degree in the same fields with 2+ years of relevant experience.
  • OR PhD in the same fields.
  • Relevant experience in any of the following:
    • Expertise in semiconductor processing, wafer-level assembly, or cleanroom environments.
    • Proficiency in process development methodologies, statistical process control, and manufacturing process improvement.
    • Technical expertise in module engineering or fab process/hardware technology development.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD and 3+ years of experience in relevant field and any of the below:
    • Strong metrology fundamental understanding and development experience.
    • Strong collaboration skills with cross-functional teams, including yield and operations.
    • Demonstrated skills to leverage data analysis tools for process optimization and continuous improvement.
    • Experience with packaging processes, equipment automation development, or project management.
    • Passionate about advancing Intel's strategic goals and driving meaningful industry advancements.
    • Experience in Python, Dashboard Creation, and Scripting
    • Direct experience engaging with metrology equipment vendors at a technical roadmap level as a co-development partner

As a System Integration Engineer, you will work across the firmware and hardware elements of the 200G/400G/800G/1.6T Ethernet PHY subsystem. title: Senior Hardware Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Central Engineering Group (CEG) team delivers best-in-class Ethernet products and is at the heart of Intel's transformation from a PC company to a company that powers the cloud and billions of smart, connected computing devices. CEG's compelling Ethernet products move the world's data and are the foundations of cloud service and telecommunications data centers. You will be exposed to High-Speed I/O protocols such as PCIeGen6-7, DDR5-6, and PAM4 Ethernet 224Gb, which are a part of our Ethernet Infrastructure Processing Unit (Intel IPU) and Foundation NIC (FNIC) Ethernet product lines. We propose a dynamic and flexible workplace position, working directly with highly capable design, system, and pre/post-silicon teams within the organization. Most of the team's engineers have 10+ years of experience, and we are looking for a highly skilled multidisciplinary engineer with proven experience in electrical and system engineering to lead the hardware design of our next division projects' challenges and be part of Ethernet networking's accelerated growth. The role requires high-frequency signal and power integrity and a good understanding of RF circuits and electromagnetic wave propagation. It includes learning the specifications of each interface and the required design limitations that should be verified. You will lead a team of developers and develop yourself digital and analog circuit boards for use in HW-Engineering products. In this position, your responsibilities include but are not limited to developing board design from schematic through leading the Silicon power-on hardware enablement and debug and may interface with other board design and test module development teams to drive innovation initiatives. Join an enthusiastic team of engineers in Intel's Central Engineering Group (CEG), within the Custom ASICs Development Group (CADG), focused on enabling and integrating the next generation of programmable Infrastructure Processing Units (IPUs) and Foundation Network Interface Card (FNIC) product lines. As a System Integration Engineer, you will work across the firmware and hardware elements of the 200G/400G/800G/1.6T Ethernet PHY subsystem. title: AI Hardware Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Job

Intel is seeking exceptional Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and AI/ML students to join an AI Hardware Engineering internship focused on the future of AI inference and AI infrastructure with hardware/software co-design expertise. 


This internship approaches AI infrastructure as a hardware/software co-design challenge. The intern will analyze how model architecture, inference behavior, memory movement, data-center constraints, and software stacks influence end-to-end customer outcomes, including throughput, latency, time-to-first-token, tokens per second, power consumption, utilization, total cost of ownership, and deployability. 


The successful candidate will be technically hands-on, capable of independent research and analysis, and comfortable working within a highly technical team of researchers and engineers addressing complex AI hardware and infrastructure challenges. 


What You Will Do 

  • Conduct technical research on the next generation of AI infrastructure, including CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, ASICs, memory systems, networking, storage, rack-scale architecture, power delivery, cooling, and cluster management. 
  • Analyze GenAI and agentic AI workloads to understand their hardware implications, including transformer architecture based inference, mixture-of-experts architectures, multimodal models, real-time interactive inference, and distributed serving. 
  • Evaluate the hardware behavior of AI inference pipelines, including the distinct demands of prompt processing/prefill and token generation/decode, memory capacity, memory bandwidth, KV-cache management, compute utilization, interconnect bandwidth, and latency. For example, cluster architecture around optimizing both prefill and decode through hardware, memory, and system co-design. 
  • Identify product and system gaps that may limit Intel's ability to serve AI customers effectively, including hardware capabilities, developer tooling, performance libraries, reference architectures, deployment models, observability, and ecosystem enablement.  

- Expertise in modern high-performance CPU, GPU, or AI accelerator architecture and hardware/software interactions. 

- Support Silicon HW programs through multiple phases of the silicon lifecycle, with end-to-end chip execution from concept to silicon. 

- Good understanding with firmware codebases, compilers, kernels, serving stacks and model architectures.    

- Familiar with driving silicon design for subsystems and/or top-level functions with ASICs and SOCs from an architecture specification to production silicon including memory subsystems and interconnects: scale up, scale out, scale across, power management , liquid cooling at rack scale level, deep system level observability & telemetry and dependent impact into Gen AI and LLM level performance/tco/execution KPIs 

  • Develop technical recommendations for what Intel should build, optimize, enable, partner on to meet AI customer requirements based on deep understanding of customer use cases, workload performance, and ML systems research. 
  • Benchmark and compare relevant AI hardware and infrastructure approaches across performance, power efficiency, cost, programmability, memory hierarchy, scalability, ecosystem maturity, and workload fit. 
  • Develop technical models, simulations, prototypes, or analysis tools to evaluate hardware/software trade offs for AI workloads. 
  • Investigate system bottlenecks across compute, memory, networking, storage, and software orchestration, and propose methods to improve end-to-end AI workload performance. 
  • Work with Intel technical teams and external ISVs to collect data on model requirements, inference bottlenecks, deployment challenges, hardware optimization opportunities, and customer priorities. 
  • Engage with AI software ecosystem partners, including model providers, inference-engine developers, cloud providers, framework teams, and ISVs, to understand how their stacks interact with underlying hardware. 
  • Good understanding of modern AI software layers, including PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, model serving, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, Kubernetes, and Neocloud design efficiencies.  
  • Present findings through architecture diagrams, benchmark analyses, technical reports, design recommendations, and executive-ready presentations. 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, AI/ML, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Strong foundation in computer architecture, operating systems, distributed systems, parallel computing, AI/ML systems, high-performance computing, or systems software.
  • Familiarity with generative AI models and inference concepts, including transformers, attention, token generation, model serving, quantization, batching, KV cache, long-context workloads, and latency-throughput trade-offs.
  • Experience programming in one or more of the languages - C, C++, Rust, CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL, or a comparable low-level or performance-oriented language.
  • Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Coursework, research, or project experience in computer architecture, VLSI, digital design, ASIC/FPGA systems, compilers, kernel development, GPU programming, distributed systems, high-performance computing, or AI systems.
  • Experience using profiling, tracing, or benchmarking tools to evaluate CPU, GPU, accelerator, network, memory, storage, or software performance.
  • Familiarity with AI hardware platforms such as Intel Xeon processors, Intel GPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, TPUs, custom AI accelerators, FPGAs, or domain-specific inference ASICs.
  • Understanding of memory hierarchies and performance concepts, including cache behavior, DRAM, HBM, memory bandwidth, memory capacity, latency, data locality, DMA, and data movement.
  • Experience with inference frameworks or runtimes such as vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch, Triton, or Ray.
  • Familiarity with AI systems infrastructure such as Linux, containers, Kubernetes, distributed storage, RDMA over Ethernet, InfiniBand, CXL, PCIe, NVMe, UALink/eSUN based interconnects, silicon photonics and cluster-management software.
  • Some experience with simulation, modeling, emulation, RTL, FPGA prototyping, firmware, driver development, or low-level debugging.
  • Some experience contributing to open-source systems, ML infrastructure, compiler, kernel, framework, or performance-engineering projects.

title: Senior Thin Films Metals Deposition Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Group
Manufacturing Development Customer Engineering (MDCE) is a new organization within Intel Foundry Technology Manufacturing focused on improving process capability for Intel's technology nodes from initial product qualification to high volume manufacturing with the vision of making technology ramp a competitive advantage for Intel foundry. This team is responsible for transferring new technologies into high-volume manufacturing, driving process optimization and continuous improvement, resolving complex yield and manufacturing issues, partnering closely with technology development and factory teams to ensure robust, predictable silicon delivery.

About the Role

MDCE Metals Deposition Engineer is responsible for enabling best-in-class process performance and manufacturability for advanced metals deposition modules across Intel 18A, Intel 3, and Intel 12nm technology nodes. This role sits at the intersection of Technology Development (TD), High Volume Manufacturing (HVM), and Customer Engineering, driving module readiness from early development through full HVM ramp and sustaining.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

  • Leadership and Trust: Strong leadership, resourcefulness, and the ability to manage extremely sensitive information.
  • Competency, Performance: A high performer with a track record of significant accomplishments.
  • Experience Expertise: Cross-functional team leadership is a plus, significant expertise spanning multiple technology nodes and modules driving improvement to yield, performance, variation.
  • Technical and Business Acumen: A combination of technical capability, business acumen, and executive expertise to drive results across multiple groups and disciplines.
  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interpret and present technical information clearly to various audiences.
  • Initiative and Perseverance: Strong self-initiative, persistence, and the ability to navigate ambiguity and drive clarity in key areas.
  • Detail Orientation: Ability to gather, analyze, and interpret data to drive results.
  • Pressure Handling: Willingness to handle high degrees of task and deadline pressure in a dynamic environment while remaining focused.
  • Industry Knowledge: Deep knowledge of technology development and manufacturing strategies, products, processes, fab structure, and transfer methodology. Demonstrated ability to understand and interpret industry trends, create and drive strategies, work independently, simultaneously manage diverse and extensive assignments while remaining organized and productive.
  • Cultural Change: Demonstrated results in driving organizational culture change through workplace of choice efforts.

Job Responsibilities Include but Are Not Limited To:

  • Strategic Alignment and Customer-first Execution: Align organizational goals with technical vision, formulate technical strategies to deliver cutting-edge solutions, and demonstrate relentless execution to meet customer needs on time.
  • Synthesis of Diverse Information: Ability to gather diverse inputs, uplevel to the right strategic response.
  • Problem Solving: Own the resolution of technical challenges and integrate solutions across multiple groups (including technology development and high volume manufacturing) Demonstrated ability to perform data driven root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methods and common data/analytics tools.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with direct and extended technology development (TD) and manufacturing (TFSM) members and Business Groups to achieve common goals.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Engage and interface with internal and external stakeholders, including Integration, Device, Yield, Defect Metrology, Quality and Reliability, and suppliers. Establish strong working relationships.
  • Industry Trends: Stay updated on relevant industry direction setting technologies.
  • Rapid Execution: Conceptualize strategies and put them into motion swiftly to meet challenging schedules.
  • Team Management: Define goals for the team, remove roadblocks, and facilitate timely delivery of process solutions. Own the outcome, surface and resolve issues quickly.
  • Work Together, in Person: Work together with team members in person to enable faster decision making and problem resolution

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or a related engineering/science field.
  • 6+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor manufacturing, process development, or technology development.
  • 4+ years direct experience in metals deposition modules.
  • Hands-on experience with thin film deposition technologies in at least one of the following areas: Frontend or middle-of-line, Backend metals / interconnect or other critical conductive or barrier/liner films supporting logic technologies.
  • 3+ years of experience with one or more deposition technologies: PVD, CVD, and/or ALD for metals, conductive films, or barrier/liner stacks.
  • Experience with integration and module interactions (e.g., Deposition with CMP, lithography, etch, clean) and impact of deposition on device performance and yield.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or a related engineering/science field.
  • Experience in advanced technology nodes (e.g., 10nm class and below), ideally with exposure to Intel 18A, Intel 3, Intel 4/7, or comparable leading-edge foundry nodes.
  • 5+ years of direct experience in a metals deposition module such as Contact/MOL metals (e.g., W, Co, Ru, liners/barriers), BEOL / Cu interconnect (e.g., Cu/Co/Ru/W, caps, barriers, seed), advanced liners/barriers/adhesion layers or conductive films in logic nodes.
  • Experience with interconnect and MOL physics (RC performance, via/contact resistance, electromigration, reliability mechanisms) and their linkage to metals deposition and integration.
  • Proven experience driving process development, optimization, and transfer to HVM.
  • Experience supporting technology ramp or technology transfer from TD to HVM, including POR definition, process window characterization, and tool matching.
  • Hands-on ownership of metals deposition equipment (e.g., multi-chamber PVD/CVD/ALD platforms) including qualification, matching, and release to production.
  • Experience collaborating with equipment and materials suppliers on hardware changes, chamber design, or chemistry changes to improve yield, cost, or reliability.
  • Cross-functional leadership experience including experience leading or contributing to cross-site and cross-functional task forces for yield excursions, defect reduction, or technology ramp and demonstrated ability to work closely with factory teams, module and technical program stakeholders to implement metals deposition solutions in HVM.
