title: Sr. Director, Networking Hardware Product Management
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Sr. Director of Product Management serves as the senior product owner for Intel's Infrastructure Processing Unit (IPU) and Ethernet controller and adapter portfolio, with end-to-end responsibility for product vision, strategy, definition, positioning, and lifecycle management across Data Center, Enterprise, Edge, and Embedded markets. This role leads a team and reports directly to the General Manager of the Business Unit.

Defines and drives long-range product and portfolio strategy based on customer requirements, market dynamics, competitive intelligence, technology trends, and Intel business priorities. Translates these insights into differentiated product requirements, multi-year roadmaps, investment priorities, and new product opportunities that strengthen Intel's networking portfolio and support business growth.
Owns new product definition from concept through execution, partnering closely with architecture, engineering, design, manufacturing, test, quality, operations, sales, and marketing. Collaborates with platform and system architects to evaluate emerging technologies and customer use cases, assess technical and business tradeoffs, and influence future silicon, platform, and system capabilities.

Leads and develops a high-performing product management team responsible for executing the portfolio strategy. Sets clear priorities and expectations, establishes ownership and accountability, develops product management capabilities and technical expertise, and coaches team members to deliver business and customer outcomes. Builds organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, and effective deployment of resources against the highest-priority opportunities.
Serves as a key interface to strategic customers and ecosystem partners, developing a deep understanding of current and emerging networking requirements and translating those needs into actionable product strategy. Influences internal technology roadmaps and investment decisions based on customer insights, competitive dynamics, and long-term market opportunities.
Defines product positioning, value propositions, and competitive differentiation for Data Center, Enterprise, Edge, and Embedded applications. Partners with sales, marketing, and communications teams to develop go-to-market strategies, enable customer adoption, and successfully launch products worldwide.

Owns the complete product lifecycle from cradle to grave, including product introduction, ramp, sustaining, optimization, technology transitions, modifications, upgrades, and end-of-life decisions. Evaluates portfolio performance, customer adoption, market opportunity, and competitive positioning to inform ongoing investment and lifecycle decisions.
Leads complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning multiple organizations and geographies, establishing priorities, and driving alignment where successful outcomes require significant technical and business tradeoffs. Communicates product vision, strategy, roadmap, investment rationale, and business implications to executive leadership, customers, and other key stakeholders.
Uses deep networking technology expertise, extensive industry knowledge, customer insight, and business acumen to anticipate market transitions, identify new opportunities, and influence Intel's long-range networking strategy. Operates with a high degree of autonomy and serves as a recognized product and market authority for the portfolio.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent relevant industry experience.
• 12+ years of experience in product management, product strategy, engineering, architecture, technical marketing, or a related role within the semiconductor, networking, data center, or infrastructure technology industry.
• 5+ years of experience leading product strategy, product definition, or lifecycle management for complex hardware or hardware/software products.
• Demonstrated technical knowledge of Ethernet and networking technologies, including network interface controllers (NICs), Ethernet controllers/adapters, infrastructure processing units (IPUs/DPUs/SmartNICs), or related data center networking technologies.
• Demonstrated experience translating customer, market, and competitive requirements into product strategy, product requirements, and multi-year roadmaps.
• Experience managing products through multiple stages of the product lifecycle, including new product definition, development, launch, production, sustaining, and end-of-life.
• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives across engineering, architecture, operations, sales, marketing, and other business functions.
• Experience engaging directly with strategic customers and/or ecosystem partners and translating technical requirements into product and business decisions.
• Demonstrated ability to communicate and influence effectively across technical, business, and executive-level audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
• Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline and/or MBA.
• 15+ years of semiconductor, networking, data center, or infrastructure industry experience.
• Deep knowledge of Ethernet networking, data center architectures, NICs, IPUs/DPUs/SmartNICs, accelerators, or related silicon and platform technologies.
• Experience defining or managing networking silicon, adapters, boards, or platform-level products.
• Experience developing product strategies for Data Center, Cloud, Enterprise, Edge, and/or Embedded markets.
• Experience working directly with hyperscalers, cloud service providers, OEMs, ODMs, enterprise customers, or other strategic ecosystem partners.
• Demonstrated experience developing business cases, assessing market opportunities, influencing investment decisions, and driving product portfolio strategy.
• Experience developing product positioning, competitive strategy, go-to-market plans, and customer adoption strategies for highly technical products.
• Track record of influencing senior executives and leading across complex global organizations without direct authority.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. title: Partner Marketing Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Partner Marketing Manager, you will lead and drive impactful co-marketing initiatives with Intel's strategic partner Microsoft, ensuring alignment with Intel's brand strategies and delivering measurable business results. You will evaluate market trends and competitive programs, manage multi-region campaigns, and guide partners in utilizing Market Development Funds (MDF) effectively. Your expertise will play a critical role in developing metrics to analyze marketing spend and return on investment, empowering Intel and its partners to collaboratively achieve success in the marketplace.
In this role, you will work alongside the Global Field Sales, Business Groups, global and regional marketing, and sales counterparts that are at points of influence throughout the world. You will work directly with partners at Microsoft and build relationships, from mid-level to the most senior managers within their marketing and sales organizations.
This role is responsible for driving strategic decisions that align Microsoft and Intel's global GTM strategies and regional execution engines that materially and measurably contribute to business growth across all segments. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As a Memory Electrical Validation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in optimizing and validating electrical performance for memory IO interfaces. You'll focus on ensuring compliance with industry standards, analyzing margins for stable operation, debugging electrical issues, and driving system-level improvements. Your expertise will directly contribute to delivering high-quality, reliable products that meet production goals while advancing Intel's innovative memory solutions.

Business group
The Silicon and Platform Engineering (SPE) Group leads Intel's efforts in designing, developing, and validating advanced silicon and platform technologies. This team is committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that drive Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry. By joining SPE, you'll be part of a collaborative environment that tackles challenging problems and powers Intel's success in creating transformative technologies for the future.

Key Responsibilities
- Define electrical validation strategies for memory IO interfaces to ensure optimized electrical performance and alignment with production goals.
- Validate circuit analog performance, signal integrity compliance, and system-level margins against industry standards.
- Analyze, debug, and optimize Memory Reference Code (MRC) requirements to improve margins and overall product quality.
- Collaborate on multidisciplinary research for testing, validation, and optimization of memory IO and mixed-signal architectures.
- Develop procedures and designs for validation processes, systems margin evaluation, and test infrastructure.
- Debug functional and triage failures to identify root causes and resolve electrical issues.
- Test electrical interactions between design features using advanced validation infrastructure.
- Prepare validation specifications, evaluate intellectual property (IP), and generate detailed test reports.

- Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- Demonstrated ability to analyze, design, and optimize validation procedures and test infrastructure.

- Passion for delivering innovative solutions and driving continuous improvement.

title: GPU Software Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As a GPU Software Development Engineer, you will focus on enabling and optimizing Intel's GPUs by developing, backporting, and validating software solutions that span the stack-from firmware and device drivers to APIs and the application layer. You will play a critical role in designing, debugging, and improving GPU kernel drivers and graphics software on Linux platforms across diverse kernel environments and enterprise distributions, ensuring seamless integration and performance. Your contributions will directly support Intel's innovations in graphics and data center technologies.


Business Group:

The Data Center Group (DCG) drives Intel's leadership in computing innovation, with a focus on delivering high-performance solutions for data-centric markets. This group develops technologies that power advanced workloads in cloud computing, AI, and graphics acceleration. By joining DCG, you'll collaborate with experts dedicated to enabling cutting-edge GPU solutions that advance Intel's broader mission to shape the future of technology.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Develop and validate GPU kernel drivers and graphics software solutions, contributing to the full development lifecycle from design and implementation to testing and release across Linux platforms, including contributions to the open-source graphics software community where applicable.
  • Debug, optimize, and enable Linux DRM/KMD drivers - including root cause analysis of kernel panics, regressions, deadlocks, race conditions, and memory corruption across diverse hardware and software environments.
  • Design and implement new driver features, enhancements, and optimizations within the Linux DRM/KMD subsystem, collaborating closely with hardware and firmware teams to enable new GPU capabilities.
  • Adapt and backport upstream Intel GPU drivers (DRM/KMD) to LTS, enterprise, and customized customer kernel environments, designing and maintaining compatibility layers and out-of-tree packaging solutions such as DKMS.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams - spanning firmware, KMD, user-space runtime, and compute/graphics stacks - to ensure robust integration, compatibility, and stability across the full GPU software stack.
  • Partner with validation and DevOps teams to expand multi-kernel test matrices, regression suites, and automated build pipelines that catch compatibility breaks early.
  • Ensure high code quality and adherence to Linux kernel coding standards through active participation in design and code reviews, spanning both upstream driver development and backported driver deliverables.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.
    5+ years of hands-on experience in large-scale software product development with deep focus on Linux kernel and system software engineering.
  • Expert-level C programming with deep understanding of Linux kernel internals, driver architecture, memory management, concurrency, locking primitives, and interrupt handling.
  • Proven experience developing and debugging Linux DRM/KMD drivers and device driver debugging mechanisms.
  • Hands-on experience backporting Linux kernel patches and drivers across kernel versions, with practical understanding of kernel API/ABI drift and compatibility wrapper construction.
  • Proficiency in Linux kernel debugging tools such as ftrace, perf, kdump/crash, kgdb, GDB, dynamic debug, and interpreting stack traces and lockdep reports.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electronics/Electrical Engineering.
  • Deep experience with Linux DRM/KMS subsystem, GPU memory management (TTM, GEM), DMA-BUF, and modern graphics/compute software stacks.
  • Experience with out-of-tree module frameworks (DKMS, Kbuild backport frameworks) and multi-kernel distribution packaging (RPM, DEB).
  • Experience triaging and resolving kernel regressions caused by upstream changes in core subsystems such as schedulers, memory allocators, power management, and PCIe buses.
  • Experience supporting customer-specific or enterprise Linux distributions such as RHEL, SLES, or Ubuntu LTS, including kernel validation and issue resolution in production environments.
  • Active patch submissions or contributions to the open-source Linux kernel or DRM/graphics community.

Join us to work on impactful projects that shape the future of GPU technology and advance Intel's mission of delivering world-changing innovations.

title: Product Failure Analysis Engineer - SCAN Design for Test
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that enriches the lives of every person on earth. As a global leader in semiconductor innovation, we design and manufacture the world's most advanced chips — powering everything from personal computers and smartphones to data centers, AI systems, and autonomous vehicles. Our Oregon campus is one of our most important engineering hubs in the world, home to thousands of brilliant engineers who are shaping the future of technology. We believe that diversity of thought, background, and experience makes us stronger — and we're committed to building a workplace where everyone can do their best work.

We are seeking an experienced Product Failure Analysis Engineer - SCAN Design for Test who is excited by the opportunity to help enable the success of Intel Foundry's leading-edge 18A technology. The ideal candidate brings 6-12 years of semiconductor experience with deep expertise in DFT, ATPG, scan diagnosis, and post-silicon debug, along with a proven track record of solving complex silicon issues in advanced process technologies.

In this role, you will play a critical part in accelerating the ramp and quality of Intel Foundry products by driving root-cause analysis of silicon failures, partnering across design, test, technology development, and manufacturing organizations to quickly identify and resolve product and process issues. Your technical leadership will directly contribute to improving product quality, yield, reliability, and time-to-market for next-generation foundry customers.

The successful candidate will have hands-on experience utilizing both logical diagnosis techniques (ATPG, scan diagnosis, fault isolation) and physical failure analysis methodologies (FIB, SEM, TEM, laser-based techniques, or equivalent) to isolate defects and determine corrective actions. Strong collaboration skills are essential, as you will work closely with DFT architects, design engineers, validation teams, process integration engineers, yield engineers, and high-volume manufacturing organizations.

Beyond issue resolution, we are looking for an engineer who can help shape the future of failure analysis and silicon debug by developing innovative methodologies, automation frameworks, and diagnostic capabilities that improve debug efficiency and accelerate root-cause identification across Intel Foundry's advanced technology portfolio..

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead Failure Analysis: Utilize state-of-the-art lab equipment — including FIB tools, probe tools, and automated systems — to isolate microscopic silicon circuit failures and identify root causes with precision and speed.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with test and validation engineers, circuit designers, wafer fabrication process engineers, and high-volume manufacturing teams to resolve quality issues, develop temporary mitigations, and implement permanent remedies.
  • Advance Debug Technologies: Develop new debug tools, methodologies, and technologies that push the boundaries of silicon debug, contributing to breakthrough innovations in semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Ensure Design for Debug: Evaluate and resolve component engineering and physical design issues, ensuring products incorporate the necessary design-for-debug features to enable deep silicon isolation capabilities.
  • Support Continuous Improvement: Provide expert input on failure analysis investigation areas and design process improvements, ensuring products consistently perform to specification.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • A collaborative spirit — you thrive in cross-functional environments and build strong relationships across teams.
  • Intellectual curiosity — you love diving deep into complex problems and aren't satisfied until you've found the root cause.
  • Resilience and adaptability — you stay focused and effective even when working on the most challenging, ambiguous problems.
  • Clear communication — you can translate highly technical findings into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences.
  • Ownership mentality — you take pride in your work and hold yourself accountable for delivering results.
  • Innovation mindset — you're always looking for better ways to do things and aren't afraid to challenge the status quo.

Ideal Background:

  • 6+ years of semiconductor industry experience in Product Engineering, Failure Analysis, Silicon Debug, DFT, Yield Engineering, or Post-Silicon Validation.
  • Deep expertise in DFT architectures, ATPG, scan diagnosis, and fault modeling.
  • Experience debugging complex silicon issues on leading-edge technology nodes.
  • Strong understanding of failure analysis workflows and physical debug techniques.
  • Demonstrated success driving cross-functional investigations from problem identification through corrective action.
  • Experience developing automation and debug methodologies that improve diagnosis accuracy and turnaround time.
  • Passion for advancing semiconductor technology and contributing to the successful deployment of Intel Foundry 18A products.

If you're passionate about silicon engineering and want to work on technology that matters, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and take the next step in your career at Intel.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research and relevant previous job and/or internship experience.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related STEM discipline with 6+ years of hands-on experience, OR master's degree with 4+ years, OR PhD with 2+ years.
  • Hands – on experience with the following:
    • Expertise in Design for Test (DFT) tools and techniques, SCAN ATPG methodology, and Scan Chain Diagnosis.
    • In fault isolation techniques including ATPG pattern generation, fault modeling (stuck-at, transition, path delay, bridging), and Scan architecture (SSN).
    • Experience with Siemens Tessent, Synopsys TestMAX/TetraMAX, Verdi, DVE, simulation and diagnosis tools
    • Experience developing debug automation and analysis tools using Python, Perl, or TCL

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 6+ years of experience:
    • JTAG and validation/debug research methodologies.
    • Developing innovative debug tools and methodologies in a research-driven environment.
    • In foundry, fabless semiconductor, or high-volume manufacturing environments supporting customer product bring-up, yield ramp, or production qualification.

title: Senior Construction Manager - Site Logistics (Contract Position)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Organization

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) as we deliver some of the world's largest and most advanced semiconductor manufacturing facilities. FCS manages a global portfolio of capital projects that includes new wafer fabrication facilities, fab expansions and conversions, process tool installations, infrastructure upgrades, and progressive-build programs. 


Our projects involve complex stakeholder environments and large contractor workforces consisting of general contractors, architecture and engineering firms, specialty trade partners, and equipment suppliers. Collectively, the portfolio represents billions of dollars in annual capital investment and plays a critical role in enabling Intel's growth and technology roadmap. 


Position Overview

The Senior Construction Manager - Site Logistics is a key leader within the Project Execution organization, responsible for planning, coordinating, and optimizing site-wide construction logistics, labor forecasting, workforce coordination, and operational readiness across multiple capital projects. 


Reporting to the Director of Construction, this role provides leadership and oversight for integrated site logistics activities supporting projects with contractor populations ranging from 100 to 1000 workers. The successful candidate will collaborate across project teams, construction managers, suppliers, operations organizations, and external stakeholders to ensure safe, efficient, and predictable project execution. 


This role serves as a central coordination point for site logistics strategy, trade labor planning, contractor integration, and construction operations while driving innovation, productivity improvements, and best-in-class safety performance. 


Location: Albuquerque, New Mexico (On-site) 


Key Responsibilities 


Site Logistics and Construction Operations 

  • Lead site-wide logistics planning and execution to support multiple concurrent construction and tool installation projects. 
  • Drive safe, efficient, and coordinated construction operations while minimizing operational disruptions. 
  • Develop and implement logistics strategies for workforce access, material flow, laydown areas, site services, transportation, and critical infrastructure coordination. 
  • Partner with construction and project management teams to optimize site utilization and project delivery performance. 

Labor Planning and Workforce Coordination 

  • Own trade labor forecasting, workforce planning, and contractor resource alignment across active projects. 
  • Develop and present labor forecasts and staffing plans to construction leadership, trade organizations, and labor stakeholders. 
  • Monitor trade headcount demand, workforce availability, and project labor requirements to ensure delivery commitments are met. 
  • Coordinate labor requirements across multi-prime, design-build, and general contractor delivery models. 

Program Integration and Stakeholder Management 

  • Serve as a key interface between Construction Management, Tool Install, Facilities Operations, Finance, Design, Procurement, and Supply Chain organizations. 
  • Lead site-wide indirect planning, coordination, tracking, and reporting activities. 
  • Drive alignment among project teams, suppliers, and stakeholders regarding logistics priorities, resource constraints, and schedule requirements. 
  • Facilitate executive-level discussions while maintaining detailed understanding of project execution needs. 

Contractor and Supplier Leadership 

  • Build and maintain strategic partnerships with contractors, suppliers, and service providers. 
  • Drive continuous improvement in contractor performance, safety, schedule reliability, productivity, and cost management. 
  • Identify and implement innovative construction methods, technologies, and operational practices that improve project outcomes. 

Process Excellence and Innovation 

  • Own and drive site logistics governance processes, planning frameworks, and reporting mechanisms. 
  • Champion Lean construction principles and operational excellence initiatives. 
  • Evaluate and implement innovative logistics, planning, and construction solutions to improve efficiency and scalability. 
  • Promote sustainability initiatives and support environmental and certification objectives where applicable. 

Safety and Culture 

  • Lead and reinforce Intel's Culture of Caring across all phases of project execution. 
  • Ensure compliance with safety requirements and foster a proactive safety culture among contractors and project teams. 
  • Drive continuous improvement in safety performance, operational excellence, collaboration, and employee engagement.

title: Defect Characterization Low Yield Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

As a Low Yield Analysis (LYA) Engineer within Intel Foundry's Defect Characterization organization, you will drive root cause identification and yield improvement strategies for advanced packaging assembly and substrate technology development programs. You will lead complex technical investigations, develop innovative characterization methodologies, and collaborate across manufacturing, quality, process integration, design, and module technology development organizations to resolve critical yield challenges.


This role requires a strong sense of ownership, urgency, technical leadership, and customer focus. The successful candidate will independently drive investigations, influence technical decisions, mentor team members, and deliver measurable business impact through yield improvement and defect characterization excellence.

Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end investigations to identify and resolve complex yield, defect, and quality issues.
  • Serve as a technical owner for major factory, platform, or technology development programs.
  • Define characterization strategies, learning plans, and root cause methodologies for critical technical challenges.
  • Utilize advanced analytical techniques including Optical Microscopy, SEM/EDS, EBSD, CSAM, FTIR, Raman, FIB, ion milling, and mechanical cross-sectioning to identify failure mechanisms.
  • Correlate characterization results with electrical data, defect inspection data, process history, and manufacturing information to establish root cause.
  • Consolidate and analyze large data sets using statistical methods and coding tools to identify yield limiters and emerging trends.
  • Develop and implement tools, dashboards, automation, and analytical methodologies that improve learning velocity and analysis efficiency.
  • Drive corrective actions and influence process improvements across manufacturing, integration, quality, and technology organizations.
  • Lead cross-functional task forces and technical reviews to address high-priority yield and reliability issues.
  • Present technical findings, recommendations, and risk assessments to engineering and management teams.
  • Mentor engineers and technicians while promoting best-known methods and organizational learning.
  • Support future capability development through equipment strategy, methodology development, and characterization roadmap planning.
  • Effectively manage multiple high-priority investigations while balancing customer commitments, factory priorities, and business needs.

Behavioral traits

  • Demonstrated success managing multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing or development environment.
  • Communicate findings verbally and through reports to yield engineers, LYA analysts, and other customers.
  • Work in a collaborative manner with a variety of different individuals in a fast paced, technical environment.
  • Experience independently driving technical investigations and root cause analysis activities.
  • Independently own open-ended technical problems, proactively drive actions across organizations, and deliver measurable business impact through root cause identification and implementation of corrective actions.
  • Problem-solving, analytical, and troubleshooting skills.
  • Verbal and written communication skills to communicate technical findings to diverse audiences.
  • Operate effectively in ambiguous environments and drive technical issues to closure with minimal direction.

This role is lab-based and on-site required.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum qualifications and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Chemistry and Physics or related field with 3+ years of relevant semiconductor industry or failure analysis lab experience OR PhD in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Chemistry and Physics or related field.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience working in a lab environment with hands-on experience with failure analysis and characterization techniques such as Optical Microscopy, SEM/EDS, CSAM, FTIR, Raman, TEM, EBSD, XRD or similar methodologies.
  • Experience with mechanical cross-sectioning, planar grinding, ion milling, focused ion beam (FIB), and advanced sample preparation techniques.
  • Advanced knowledge of semiconductor packaging, assembly, substrate manufacturing, or related process technologies.

  • Track record of mentoring engineers and technicians and contributing to organizational capability development.
  • Experience developing new characterization techniques, analytical workflows, or problem-solving methodologies.

title: E-Core CPU Design Automation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

E-core (formerly known as ATOM), Intel's most efficient CPU Technology team is looking for a highly motivated and technically savvy experienced individual to join our team as Design Automation Engineer. Intel has a vision to create and extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person. We are designing future generations of high-performance E-core CPUs using the most advanced and innovative process technologies. If you are looking to grow and develop your skillsets while being surrounded by highly motivated and knowledgeable teammates, then this is the organization for you.


E-Core CPUs are the industry-leading performance-per-watt CPU that helps:

  • Power the latest Intel laptops, desktops, and high-end gaming platforms.
  • Drive 5G communications by serving as the base station that delivers essential data from your electronic devices across the world at maximum bandwidth.
  • Create Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning devices.
  • Enable a full virtual learning experience for students using the latest Google Chromebooks.

As a CPU Physical Design Automation Engineer in the E-core CPU group, you will be responsible for:

  • Developing, debugging, and supporting tools, flows, and methodologies covering backend physical design methodologies and flow automation for high-performance blocks and full chip level using RTL2GDS standard cell level design techniques.
  • Performing analysis of either synthesis, place and route, floor planning or signoff for static timing analysis on timing paths, formal equivalence verification, power consumption, electrical rule checking, and circuit reliability to identify key issues.
  • Working closely with design teams to understand and debug tool issues and constraints.
  • Working with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a high-speed, low-power synthesizable CPU.
  • Creating documentation and helping with guidelines/specs.
  • Communicating with other team members to solve problems and following solutions through to completion. Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Leverage AI capabilities to enhance daily operational efficiency and design productivity.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering and/or Electrical/Electronic Engineering and 1+ years of relevant working experience OR Master's Degree in Computer Engineering and/or Electrical/Electronic Engineering

  • Fresh Graduate is welcome to apply.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 1+ years of experience in VLSI, design automation algorithms, and transistor-level design.

  • 1+ years of experience using industry standard Engineering Design Automation (EDA) VLSI tools/flows from vendors such as Synopsys, Cadence and/or Mentor Graphics for performing synthesis, place-and-route, extraction, timing/power analysis and functional verification.

  • 1+ years' experience with Python, Perl, and/or Tcl scripting languages.

  • 1+ years of relevant working experience in microprocessor or other high speed design backend design.

  • Experience with timing closure methodology for worst-case corner (static timing analysis / STA, statistical variation analysis, spice circuit simulation, ERC, noise analysis flows, cross talk, OCV effects, budget constraints)

descriptionHtml:

As a Senior CPU Circuit Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and developing custom digital circuits for CPUs, including memory. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to optimize power, performance, area, timing, and yield goals, while ensuring the functionality and reliability of CPU circuits. Your expertise will directly contribute to the creation of cutting-edge processors that shape Intel's technological leadership.


Business Group

As part of this group, you will join a collaborative team dedicated to developing world-class CPUs that address the needs of diverse computing markets and support Intel's broader mission of technological excellence.

descriptionHtml:

The Role and Impact

Intel is seeking a collaborative and community-focused professional to help strengthen relationships with the public and private sector in Ohio, with a primary focus on the Columbus, New Albany, Johnstown, and Licking County region. The Government and Public Affairs, Community Engagement Manager will support Intel's efforts to advance education, workforce development, economic opportunity, and community impact through strategic engagement with schools, nonprofits, civic organizations, neighbors, and other community stakeholders.

Working in close partnership with the Ohio Director of Government Affairs, this role will help build trust, foster meaningful partnerships, and manage community investment initiatives that support Intel's long-term presence and success in Ohio. Business group

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Shift 5: (Day shift compressed work week) 6 AM-6 PM (Sunday-Tuesday and alternating Wednesdays).
Shift 7: (Day shift compressed work week) 6 AM-6 PM (Thursday-Saturday and alternating Wednesdays).

About the Role
Join Intel's Foundry Technology Manufacturing business unit and play a key role in shaping the future of semiconductor packaging. As a Module Engineer, you will develop and optimize assembly processes and equipment, applying innovative concepts to enable Intel's next-generation foundry packaging platform technologies. You will work at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing, and technology development to deliver world-class packaging solutions for our foundry customers.

What You Will Do

  • Design and develop assembly processes and equipment, applying novel engineering concepts to advance Intel's foundry packaging roadmap and platform technologies.
  • Optimize manufacturing efficiency for foundry packages, developing processes that meet rigorous quality, reliability, cost, yield, productivity, and manufacturability requirements specific to foundry customer needs.
  • Define process and equipment specifications using Design of Experiments (DOE) and data analysis principles, documenting innovations and improvements through technical white papers.
  • Develop and maintain equipment used to evaluate silicon and package technologies under simulated field conditions, including thermal cycling, heat, humidity, and dynamic mechanical stress testing.
  • Ensure physical package designs are manufacturable within foundry process flows, and oversee the full cycle of package manufacturing processes, procedures, and production flows.
  • Establish material specifications for contract assemblers and raw material vendors, partnering closely with supplier quality and procurement teams to enforce process compliance and vendor performance standards.
  • Create new reliability screening techniques, acceleration methods, and quality tools to enable early detection of potential packaging quality and reliability risks within the foundry manufacturing environment.
  • Define reliability requirements aligned to foundry customer needs, and influence design decisions, material selection, and process development based on a fundamental understanding of failure mechanisms.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives using statistical methods and experimental design to innovate, troubleshoot, and enhance equipment and process performance.
  • Serve as a technical resource for foundry packaging challenges, responding to customer and partner requests and providing consultation on process improvements.
  • Drive standardization across product qualification frameworks, manufacturing quality systems, and methodologies, while actively engaging with packaging technology development and partner engineering teams to assess process maturity and mitigate risks to key product milestones.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description:

Intel's Central Engineering Group (CEG) focuses on enhancing engineering execution and expanding market opportunities through internal product development and external ASIC design services. As an IP Design Verification Engineer, you will play a crucial role in ensuring the functional accuracy and reliability of clock generator IPs, such as PLL and FLL, within Intel's innovative product development lifecycle. title: Packaging Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Surface Mount Technology Development (SMTD), part of Intel's Assembly Technology Development (ATD) packaging team, cater to Intel's customer product assembly needs and certify Surface Mount Technology (SMT) manufacturing for new Central Processing Unit (CPU), Chipset, System on Chip (SoC) BGA packages, and Socket Technology. The Surface Mount Technology Development Lab in Kulim, Malaysia, offers SMT manufacturing, provides expertise in technology development, enabling next-generation product roadmaps through innovative solutions in circuit board technology, assembly processes, and materials.


In this role, you will be a Packaging Module Development Engineer focuses on process, equipment, materials technology development for SMT processes and Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs). Your responsibilities will include developing SMT process solutions and recommendations for Intel's integrated circuit (IC) packages and Sockets, as well as advancing new technologies to support Intel's SMT and PCB roadmap.

What you will do:

As a Packaging Module Development Engineer, you will be tasked with developing and validating board assembly process solutions to meet Intel's next-generation product requirements.


Your responsibilities will include creating SMT process solutions for Intel IC packages and sockets, identifying and addressing root causes of defects in SMT process development, and publishing Critical to Function (CTF) parameter recommendations and manufacturability guidelines for Intel's customers to adopt.


You will also be responsible for SMT Process Development. Design and optimize SMT processes, including stencil design, solder paste selection, reflow profiling, and inspection criteria to ensure high yield and reliability.

  • Materials Characterization: Evaluate and select materials such as solder pastes, fluxes, underfills, and adhesives to enhance assembly performance and reliability.
  • Process Integration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate new SMT processes into existing manufacturing lines, ensuring compatibility and scalability. Influence IC package and PCB design based on a deeper understanding of SMT, and manufacturing processes in internal and external strategic forums.
  • Failure Analysis: Conduct root cause analysis of assembly defects and implement corrective actions to improve process robustness.
  • Technology Roadmap: Contribute to the development of technology roadmaps for SMT and PCB advancements, focusing on miniaturization, higher interconnect densities, and improved thermal and electrical performance.
  • Prototype Testing: Oversee the assembly and testing of prototype boards, utilizing advanced equipment such as X-ray inspection and automated optical inspection (AOI).
  • Data Analysis: Utilize statistical tools and software to analyse process data, identify trends, and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Documentation and Training: Develop detailed process documentation and provide training technicians to ensure consistent implementation of new technologies.

Qualifications:

  • Possess a Bachelor's degree with 3+ years of experience or Master's degree with 3+ years of experience or Ph.D. degree with 2+ years of experience in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering or Physics or related STEM fields.
  • Experiences required are Semiconductor integrated circuit (IC) assembly OR Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA SMT) in process and equipment related such as reflow, pick and place, dispensing of paste, adhesive with good understanding of material interaction with assembly processes or use condition.
  • Proficiency in statistical tools and methods (e.g., SPC, DOE) for process optimization.


The candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits and/or skills:

  • Discipline, Experimenters.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and the ability to excel under tight timelines and schedules.

We invite you to become part of a dynamic team that values innovation, collaboration, and the pursuit of excellence. Your expertise will drive transformative advancements in technology, ensuring Intel continues to lead in delivering exceptional products that shape the future of the semiconductor industry.

title: Chassis IP Senior Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is seeking an experienced Logic Design engineer for the Intel Chassis Group, which is chartered to deliver the chassis for SoCs within Intel. The role involves logic design of component and foundation IPs which can be used to build an SoC chassis. The ideal candidate will have strong design and Verilog skills and some background in protocol conversion bridges for AMBA/CXL protocols. Understanding of concepts such as QoS, access control, flow control, debug, RAS, security and error handling is a plus.

Key Responsibilities
- Develop logic designs, register transfer level (RTL) coding, and simulations required for functional units, IP blocks, and subsystems.
- Define and implement architecture and microarchitecture features for the interconnect IP block and sub-system which includes high-performance data plane and control plane routers, switches, arbiters, protocol conversion bridges, debug/trace components, and clock and power controls.
- Perform rigorous quality checks and optimization of RTL designs to improve IP power, performance, area, and timing, ensuring delivery of high-quality IP.
- Evaluate design trade-offs across area, bandwidth, timing, and reliability to achieve balanced and efficient IP functionality.
- Support Sub-system/SoC customers with high-quality IP integration and verification workflows.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with a minimum of 10 years of experience in logic design and RTL development.
- Proficiency in Verilog/System Verilog and RTL coding.
- Expertise in AMBA (CHI, AXI, AHB, APB) and PCIe/CXL protocols.
- Experience with Lint/CDC/RDC tools and methodologies.
- Strong understanding of power, performance, Timing and area optimization strategies in complex designs.

Preferred Qualifications
- 5+ years of experience designing network components such as routers, switches, arbiters, or protocol conversion bridges.
- Knowledge of debug/trace networks, flow control, and hashing methodologies.
- Experience working with leading-edge semiconductor nodes.

- Proven ability to collaborate across geographically distributed teams and adapt to multi-time zone working environments.

title: AI Frameworks Engineer - Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact


Intel is building the open software stack that makes large language models run fast on Intel GPUs. As an intern, you will join the engineering team that develops and optimizes LLM inference frameworks. You will work in vLLM and in the GPU kernel libraries beneath it with experienced engineers who will review your code and mentor you. This is a hands-on engineering internship, not a side project. You will write and test kernels, measure where performance goes, and see your changes land in open-source projects used across the AI industry.

Our internships usually last 12-24 months, and you will work with us part-time alongside your university degree. All applicants must be current university students and must remain students for the length of the internship. Candidates must be based in Poland on the internship start date and for its full duration.

Key Responsibilities


- Develop and optimize AI framework software for LLM inference on Intel GPUs, under the guidance of senior engineers, with contributions going upstream to open-source projects such as vLLM.
- Implement, port, and tune compute kernels (e.g., Triton, SYCL) for core transformer building blocks such as attention, sampling, normalization, mixture-of-experts, and quantization.
- Run benchmarks and profile inference workloads to find performance bottlenecks, measure them, and report findings to the team.
- Write and extend unit tests, correctness checks, and performance regression tests so that framework and kernel code stays reliable as upstream moves.
- Investigate and debug failures across the stack, from Python framework code down to kernel behaviour on the hardware.
- Collaborate with framework, compiler, and kernel engineers across global teams, and take part in code review and technical discussion with the open-source community.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


No professional experience is required.

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, AI, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field. Student status is required for the whole internship, preferably for the next two years and for at least 12 months.
- Good Python programming skills.
- Understanding of deep learning and neural networks, including the basics of transformer architecture and LLM inference. 
- Familiarity with Linux environments from a user perspective.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
- Eagerness to learn, an open mind, and the ability to work in a team.
- Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in English.

Preferred Qualifications


- Hands-on experience with PyTorch.
- Exposure to GPU programming (Triton, CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL, or similar), for example through coursework or personal projects.
- Working knowledge of C or C++.
- Experience testing and debugging Python code, including unit testing.
- Familiarity with vLLM or another LLM inference serving framework.
- Contributions to open-source projects, or a public portfolio of code (e.g., GitHub).
- Coursework or interest in computer architecture, parallel programming, or numerical methods.

Bring your passion for AI, your curiosity, and your engineering drive to Intel, and help shape how the next generation of AI workloads runs on Intel hardware.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

Logic Technology Development (LTD) is Intel Foundry's advanced technology engine, responsible for inventing, developing, and industrializing the process technologies that power future semiconductor products. From breakthrough device architectures and materials innovation to production-ready manufacturing solutions, LTD transforms research into customer-ready technologies that enable industry-leading performance at scale.

About the Role

The Lithography Overlay Principal Engineer is responsible for overlay control innovation, defining key technology roadmaps, and leading complex technical projects to establish Intel's overlay leadership.

As a lithography overlay expert and technologist, you will be responsible for customization and addition of new features to base technologies to use in high volume manufacturing. Your expertise will focus on all aspects of improving overlay control.

Responsibilities:
LTD Principal Engineers are responsible for leading scientific research enabling the manufacture of innovative device architectures but not limited to:

  • Lead scientific research enabling the manufacture of innovative device architectures coupled with the realization of these architectures.
  • Designing, executing, and analyzing experiments necessary to meet engineering specifications for their process.
  • Participate in the development of intellectual property.
  • Integrate the many individual steps necessary for the manufacture of complex microprocessors.

  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and researchers, fostering a culture of continuous learning and development.

  • Broad experience in logic technology development, enhancement, and customization

title: E-core CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We created the Intel Atom Processor (E-Core), a disruptive technology that enables a broad range of devices including entry PC's, smartphones, modems, 2 in 1 laptops, micro-servers, and other Internet-of-Things IoT devices. You will be part of a team, participating in the design of a future generation high performance Intel Atom microprocessor.


This role requires an engineer with strong analytic and problem solving skill, an ability to communicate well, and willing to share and discuss issues. You will work on implementation of CPU Core blocks from synthesis through post-layout verification and tapeout. You will develop the custom constraints for driving synthesis and Auto-Place and Route APR tools to implement and optimize the design to meet aggressive timing and power goals. You will work closely with micro-architecture, RTL, and custom circuit teams to converge the design to project targets.

The responsibilities will be tailored to the candidate's skills and expertise and will include several of the following, but not be limited to:

  • Logic synthesis and place and route for CORE IP blocks.
  • Performing floor-planning and routing studies and implementation
    Block/sub-system level timing analysis.
  • Work on low power techniques and power reduction in sub-system.
  • Physical verification closure of block/sub-system.
  • Scripts writing for data analysis and recipe creation.
  • Strong analytical ability, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and at various levels of abstraction.
  • Strong communication and team work skills.
  • Capable of working in a high performing team to deliver the results required from the organization.

Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.

title: CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone.

Life at Intel


As a member of Intel's CPU development team, you will have a front seat in designing the latest core IP to power cutting edge compute processors across client, server, IOTG and AI. We innovate state of the art microprocessor architecture on the most advanced and latest process technologies with a focus on power efficiency. Our core designs are present in nearly all segments of Intel's compute roadmap.

Job responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Performs physical design implementation of custom CPU designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing.
  • Conducts all aspects of the CPU physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis.
  • Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking. Analyzes results and makes recommendations to improve current and future CPU microarchitectures closely collaborating with logic, circuit, architecture, and design automation teams.
  • Possesses CPU specific expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, structured placement, routing, synthesis, and DFT.
  • Works intimately with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a highspeed, low power synthesizable CPU.
  • Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area. Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.

4+ years of experience in each of the following:

  • Experience performing CPU level timing analysis and optimization, ensuring designs meet functional and performance requirements.

title: Compiler Engineering Graduate Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Us in Shaping the Future


At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.


The Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.


Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.


Responsibilities
• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.


Success in This Role

• Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.

• Clear written and verbal communication.

• Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.

• Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.

• Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area.

• Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems.

• Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions.


Preferred Qualifications

• Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.

• Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information.

• Research or development experience involving CPU/GPU architectures, heterogeneous computing, AI/ML compilation, HPC, parallel programming, or performance optimization.

• Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.

• Tile-base programming model knowledge

• GPU Compute kernel writing experience

• Experience contributing to open-source software or working in a large collaborative codebase.

• Publications, technical reports, patents, open-source contributions, or other evidence of advanced technical work.

title: LLM & Agentic AI Performance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


Join Intel's Data Center AI organization and help shape how LLM and Agentic AI workloads perform on Intel platforms.

Our team operates at a unique intersection of core performance optimization, AI frameworks, and customer-facing AI solutions. We bridge the gap between teams that deeply understand silicon and benchmarking and teams building real-world AI solutions, turning performance insights into software optimizations that developers and customers can use.

In this role, you will own end-to-end performance characterization and optimization of LLM and Agentic AI workloads, from Python-level frameworks and inference runtimes down to Linux, system architecture, and hardware performance counters.

This is not simply a benchmarking role. Benchmarking tells us what the number is. Your job is to understand why the number is what it is, identify the hardware or software bottleneck, and determine what needs to change to remove it.

Your work will translate into code contributions, framework optimizations, best-known configurations (BKCs), customer-ready solutions, and insights that help influence future Intel hardware and software.

If you enjoy working across the complete AI stack, from agent frameworks and LLM serving engines to NUMA, memory bandwidth, cache behavior, and silicon counters, this role provides an opportunity to work at that intersection.


About the Team:


The AI Solutions and Toolkit Engineering team is part of Intel's Data Center organization, focused on enabling modern AI workloads and solutions on Intel platforms.

We work across the AI ecosystem, collaborating with AI framework and runtime developers, performance and optimization teams, hardware architects, open-source communities, and solution engineering teams.

Our goal is to take deep platform capabilities and performance insights and translate them into practical, optimized AI solutions that developers and customers can deploy.

The team works across areas including LLM inference, Agentic AI, AI frameworks and runtimes, workload optimization, open-source software, and datacenter AI systems.



Key Responsibilities:


·   Characterize and optimize LLM and Agentic AI workloads across the complete software and hardware stack.

·   Identify performance bottlenecks across AI frameworks, inference runtimes, operating systems, memory, compute, and platform architecture.

·   Design and develop hardware-aware and hardware-agnostic optimizations for AI frameworks and runtimes.

·   Optimize LLM inference techniques including KV-cache management, attention, continuous batching, and quantization.

·   Work hands-on with serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, or equivalent technologies.

·   Analyze host and accelerator performance using tools such as VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, and roofline modeling.

·   Debug complex performance issues spanning Python frameworks, native code, Linux, runtime libraries, and hardware.

·   Convert performance findings into software changes, upstream contributions, BKCs, and reusable optimization guidance.

·   Collaborate with open-source communities to upstream and integrate performance improvements.

Translate silicon-level findings into actionable recommendations for framework developers, while bringing application and framework insights back to Intel platform and silicon teams.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:


·   BE +10 years / M.Tech +8 years in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.

·   Significant hands-on experience in performance engineering, systems optimization, or workload characterization on server-class platforms.

·   Demonstrated ability to identify complex performance bottlenecks and deliver measurable performance improvements.

·   Strong programming skills in Python and C++, or equivalent systems programming experience in C/Rust.

·   Strong understanding of server architecture including cache hierarchy, memory bandwidth, NUMA, interconnects, and system-level performance behavior.

·   Hands-on experience with Linux performance and system technologies such as affinity, huge pages, cgroups, eBPF, ftrace, perf, or equivalent tools.


Preferred Qualifications:


·   Deep understanding of LLM inference, including KV-cache, paged attention, continuous batching and quantization such as INT8, INT4, or FP8.

·   Hands-on experience modifying or optimizing AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, OpenVINO, or equivalent.

·   Experience building, profiling, or optimizing Agentic AI systems using technologies such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP-based frameworks, or similar platforms.

·   Experience with hardware counter-level performance analysis using VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, or roofline modeling.

·   Contributions to significant open-source projects, including upstream code contributions.

·   Ability to communicate across abstraction layers, translating silicon-level findings for software developers and application-level requirements for hardware architects.


Why Join This Team?


This role gives you the opportunity to work across boundaries that few engineering positions span:


Agentic AI & LLMs → AI frameworks → inference runtimes Linux → server architecture → silicon


You won't be limited to measuring performance or optimizing an isolated component. You'll help connect the entire stack, identify where the real bottlenecks are, implement improvements, and make those optimizations available to developers and customers.

The result is tangible: better AI performance today, stronger software solutions for customers, and insights that can influence tomorrow's Intel platforms.

title: GPU Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join a leading technology company at the forefront of innovation in graphics processing and semiconductor technology. We are committed to pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in the world of computing, delivering cutting-edge solutions that power the future of digital experiences. Our team is composed of talented professionals who are passionate about technology and dedicated to excellence. We are seeking a skilled and experienced GPU Validation Engineer to join our dynamic team. This role requires regular onsite presence to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams and fulfill essential job responsibilities.


As a GPU Validation Engineer, you will define, develop, and perform functional validation for Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), focusing on the interaction of GPUs with media, display, and system-level features.

You will apply various hardware and software tools and techniques to ensure comprehensive validation coverage and achieve performance, power, and area goals.

  • Publishes GPU validation reports summarizing all validation activities performed, reviews results, and communicates to relevant teams.
  • Works with architecture, design, verification, board, platform, and manufacturing teams to maintain and improve debug, validation test strategy, methodologies, and processes for graphics interfaces and to meet desired product specifications.

title: Pre-Si Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact


Join Intel's cutting-edge team as a Formal Verification Engineer, where you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the quality and reliability of our next-generation IP and SoC designs. Your work will directly contribute to the delivery of innovative, high-performance solutions that drive Intel's success and leadership in the semiconductor industry.


As part of a collaborative and dynamic environment, you will work alongside architects, RTL developers, and physical design teams, applying state-of-the-art formal verification tools and methodologies to tackle complex architectural and microarchitectural challenges.


This is a unique opportunity to make a significant impact while advancing Intel's mission to shape the future of technology.



Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct formal verification of IP and SoC microarchitecture using advanced tools and methodologies based on model checking and equivalence checking algorithms.
  • Develop comprehensive formal verification test and coverage plans, including defining verification scope, strategy, and techniques.
  • Create abstraction models, carve boundaries for design, and track, verify, and apply abstraction techniques to ensure design convergence.
  • Develop and review formal proofs to implement the verification plan while continuously improving verification methodologies.
  • Perform convergence on designs by combining formal verification techniques with abstraction and simulation methods.
  • Identify and implement corrective measures to resolve failing tests, ensuring robust design functionality.
  • Collaborate closely with architects, RTL developers, and physical design teams to enhance the verification of complex architectural features.
  • Document and maintain test plans, driving technical reviews with design and architecture teams.
  • Maintain and improve the existing formal verification infrastructure and methodology.
  • Apply advanced understanding of modeling architectures, binary decision diagrams (BDD), and data flow graphs (DFG) to resolve design complexity, particularly on arithmetic pathways.
  • Utilize formal tools to prove protocols and architectures, simplifying and modeling problems with technical precision.

The ideal candidate should show the following behavioral traits:


  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communication skills.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's or BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related specialized field.
  • 6+ years of experience working with:

    • Formal verification tools and methodologies, such as model checking, equivalence checking algorithms, and abstraction techniques.
    • System Verilog, test content development, and test planning.
    • CPU architecture fundamentals, cache coherence, and CXL coherence.

title: Intel Foundry Senior Customer Quality Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

As a Customer Quality and Reliability Engineer within Intel Foundry, you will take a hands-on leadership role in ensuring that Intel Foundry meets and exceeds industry benchmarks for semiconductor manufacturing quality, reliability, and customer responsiveness.

In this role, you will act as a primary advocate for external customers across Intel Foundry partner organizations and Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) services. By spearheading incident and excursion management, facilitating customer audits, driving structured problem-solving, and developing next-generation quality systems, you will directly influence operational excellence and strengthen collaborative relationships with our global customers.

Business Group

Intel Foundry is dedicated to delivering industry-leading, world-class semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging solutions to global customers. The Customer Quality Engineering (CQE) team plays a mission-critical role in this vision by safeguarding manufacturing quality and product reliability, driving cross-site continuous improvement, and aligning internal processes with rigorous industry standards. Our team partners closely with customers and internal engineering groups to ensure Intel Foundry is recognized as a trusted, world-class manufacturing partner.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary customer advocate and technical interface for customer quality inquiries, representing customer interests across Intel Foundry and external OSAT partner organizations to deliver timely, collaborative solutions.
  • Direct end-to-end incident and excursion management processes for customer materials, driving structured root-cause investigations, material disposition, and preventative corrective actions.
  • Lead and support structured problem-solving initiatives utilizing rigorous methodologies such as 8D, RMA, and Change Notification Management (PCNs).
  • Facilitate and support customer quality audits, ensuring comprehensive compliance with international industry standards including ISO9001 and IATF16949.
  • Drive continuous improvement by designing, deploying, and standardizing next-generation quality management systems, collateral, and structured business processes across foundry and OSAT operations.
  • Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to track, analyze, and report key performance indicators (KPIs), conducting regular quality reviews to continuously enhance customer satisfaction.
  • Champion cross-functional collaboration internally to advocate for customer quality requirements and drive service, process, and yield improvements throughout manufacturing, assembly, and test operations.

Qualifications:

Candidates must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. The experience listed below may be obtained through schoolwork, classes and project work, internships, military training, and/or work experience.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field with 4+ years of hands-on experience in quality, reliability, or semiconductor manufacturing processes; OR
  • Master’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field with 3+ years of hands-on experience in quality, reliability, or semiconductor manufacturing processes; OR
  • PhD in Engineering or a related technical field with 1+ years of hands-on experience in quality, reliability, or semiconductor manufacturing processes.
  • 1+ years of experience in the following:
    • Quality and reliability systems, excursion management, and structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., 8D, root cause analysis).
    • Proficiency working with quality management standards and audit frameworks (such as ISO9001 and IATF16949).
    • Technical familiarity with silicon process technology, advanced packaging, or foundry manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across global time zones, including regular engagement during Asia workday hours.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Comprehensive technical knowledge of silicon technology, IC package technology, assembly process technology, advanced packaging architecture, and semiconductor industry standards.
  • Direct experience managing quality and reliability interfaces with external customers, foundries, and OSAT partners.
  • In-depth familiarity with industry manufacturing quality processes, including incoming/outgoing quality assurance (IQA/OQA), Product Change Notifications (PCNs), Manufacturing Baseline Process Specifications (MBPS), and FACR workflows.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving and negotiation capabilities, with a proven ability to balance customer requirements with internal business and operational priorities.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and cross-functional leadership skills in a dynamic, rapidly evolving business environment.

We are seeking collaborative, driven professionals who want to make a tangible impact by championing quality improvement, fostering customer trust, and advancing Intel Foundry's goal of delivering world-class semiconductor solutions. Join us to be part of a team committed to innovation, engineering excellence, and customer success.
