What We Do: Join the Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization, a powerhouse of process technology innovation driving Intel's IDM 2.0 strategy and enabling the success of our global foundry customers.


We are seeking a versatile Staff Engineer to be at the forefront of Intel's foundry transformation, serving as a pivotal technical partner who guides customers through the entire product development lifecycle. In this role, you will leverage multidisciplinary expertise spanning product/process integration, device engineering, and yield engineering to lead customers from pre-silicon evaluation and design tape-out through testing, validation, silicon qualification, and production ramp.This is a unique opportunity to apply broad technical leadership, solve complex challenges, face customers, and actively shape the future of the semiconductor industry in the AI era.


What You Will Do: We are seeking candidates with broad semiconductor expertise across foundry technology development. Depending on experience and business needs, responsibilities may include the following areas:


Product/Process Integration

  • Drive end-to-end Multi-Project Wafer (MPW) and New Product Introduction (NPI) execution across the full manufacturing flow, from front-end processing through far backend operations, ensuring quality and on-time delivery.
  • Serve as the primary customer-facing interface for silicon execution including wafer status, silicon health, technical issues, process changes, and execution alignment.
  • Own identification and resolution of customer-specific integration challenges.
  • Drive enablement of customer-specific requirements through effective cross-functional coordination.

Device Engineering

  • Serve as the primary customer interface for device performance, including manufacturing readiness reviews, performance roadmaps and projections, post-silicon characterization, model to hardware correlation, and resolution of customer-specific device issues.
  • Track device performance targets and process control capability while assessing alignment between silicon results and PDK expectations.
  • Drive device performance optimization through silicon learning, root-cause analysis, and cross-functional corrective actions to improve product readiness and close performance gaps.

Yield Engineering

  • Serve as the primary yield point of contact throughout the product lifecycle, from design tape-out through High Volume Manufacturing (HVM).
  • Develop predictive yield models to identify parametric and defect-related loss mechanisms and provide yield projections for test chips, shuttle vehicles, and production products.
  • Lead deep-dive investigations into yield signals and nonconformances, partnering with Process Integration, Device Engineering, and Defect Metrology teams to eliminate systematic yield losses. Perform root-cause analysis leveraging on state-of-the-art FI/FA.
  • Establish strong correlations between inline process metrics and end-of-line yield performance to improve process control and production predictability.

Benefits: Intel provides benefits that promote a healthy and enjoyable lifestyle, including comprehensive medical coverage, wellness programs, recreational activities, paid time off, employee discounts, and many additional benefits that help make Intel a Great Place to Work.Intel's future-of-work strategy is grounded in the belief that people are our most important asset. We are committed to a hybrid-first approach that provides flexibility while enabling strong collaboration and business success.


This position is not eligible for Intel Immigration Sponsorship.

title: Senior AI Developer Relations Advocate - Agentic Applications
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is transforming to meet the demands of a rapidly changing world. We design and deliver industryleading technology that powers data centers, enables AI, and drives the future of computing. Join a team building the software and platforms developers use to deliver performance at scale.

The Senior AI Developer Relations Advocate serves as the primary owner of the example applications developers copy when they build agentic and retrieval augmented generation solutions on Intel's current and future data center platforms.

This role builds and maintains production quality demos, blueprints, and workshop repositories on open libraries, including vLLM, SGLang, and Intel Inference Microservices, and on Open Source agent frameworks, including LangChain and MCP. The role treats every example as a product. Each one is pinned and reproducible, tested in CI from a clean machine, documented for a developer with no prior context, and runnable unmodified on Intel data center platforms.

The role leads flagship workshops and livecoding sessions at conferences, hackathons, and customer sites, and converts what developers hit in those rooms into fixes in the examples, the upstream libraries, and the product. Strong hands on Python engineering, depth in inference serving and agent frameworks, visible opensource engagement, and the ability to teach and present to developers live are essential.

Responsibilities:
• Own the agentic and retrieval augmented generation example applications for the AI software stack on data center platforms, including inference microservices and the agentic toolkit.
• Build and ship production quality demos, blueprints, and workshop repositories that developers can clone, run, and copy into their own projects.
• Build on open libraries and agent frameworks, including vLLM, SGLang, Intel Inference Microservices, LangChain, and MCP, and keep the examples current as those libraries and models change.
• Test every example in CI from a clean machine so it runs on a first attempt and stays reproducible.
• Lead flagship workshops, hackathons, and livecoding sessions at developer events and customer sites.
• Contribute upstream to the open libraries and agent frameworks the examples depend on.
• Convert what developers hit in workshops, issues, and customer engagements into fixes in the examples, the documentation, and the product.
• Partner with engineering, product, and developer advocates so each new capability ships with a working example application.

Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor's degree with 4 years of experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field or equivalent practical experience.
• Experience building agentic applications with agent frameworks and familiar with tool calling protocols such as LangChain and MCP.

title: Intel Foundry Module Development Engineer – Advanced Wet Etch and Cleans
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Shape the Atomic Frontier of Semiconductor Innovation

At Intel Foundry Technology and Development (TD), we don't just participate in technology development; we engineer physical reality at the angstrom scale. We are seeking visionary, research-driven Ph.D. graduates in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science, Electrochemistry, and Engineering to spearhead the next breakthrough in semiconductor manufacturing.

As a Wet Etch Module Development Engineer, you will operate at the intersection of fundamental chemical kinetics, interfacial surface science, and high-volume manufacturing engineering. You will pioneer atomic-layer selective etching, nanoscale surface cleans, supercritical and surface-tension-engineered drying, wet chemical formulations, and advanced single-wafer wet tool architectures to define the future of global computing.

What You Will Do:

  • Pioneer Next-Gen Process Architectures: Formulate and execute rigorous Design of Experiments (DOE) to invent, characterize, and validate novel wet etch, selective removal, and advanced chemical clean processes that power world-class transistor architectures (RibbonFET/GAA), backside power delivery networks (PowerVia), and high-density interconnect scaling
  • Lead Hardware and Module Co-Optimization: Collaborate with premier global semiconductor equipment suppliers and specialty chemical vendors to push single-wafer and batch wet processing capabilities beyond conventional fluid-dynamic and surface-tension limits, co-engineering custom dispense, megasonic, and chamber hardware solutions
  • Harness AI and Scientific Computing: Integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), chemical kinetics modeling, statistical physics, and data science (Python, MATLAB, JMP, ML frameworks) to accelerate chemical formulation screening, surface defectivity reduction, and line-yield enhancement
  • Drive High-Impact IP: Translate complex chemical, electrochemical, and surface phenomena into high-value patents, trade secrets, and proprietary wet processing solutions that sustain Intel Foundry's technological leadership
  • Scale Science to Global Manufacturing: Bridge early lab prototypes and coupon-level studies to 300mm fab-scale ramp, seamlessly deploying high-throughput, defect-free wet processes across Intel's worldwide mega-fabs using our industry-leading Copy Exactly (CE) methodology

Why Join Intel Foundry TD?

  • Access to Unparalleled Technology: Direct, hands-on access to the industry's most advanced 300mm cleanroom facilities, state-of-the-art single-wafer wet processing platforms, and cutting-edge analytical surface characterization suites
  • Academic Rigor Meets Global Impact: The intellectual curiosity and depth of doctoral research combined with the scale, capital resources, and execution speed of an industry leader
  • Accelerated Technical Leadership: Direct mentorship and collaboration with Intel Fellows and Senior Principal Engineers on an accelerated path toward technical distinction
  • Comprehensive Total Rewards: Top-tier Ph.D. compensation packages, sign-on bonuses, annual performance bonuses, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), equity/RSU grants, and full relocation assistance

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science and Engineering, Electrochemistry, Mechanical Engineering (Microfluidics/Transport Phenomena), Physics, or a closely related discipline (Degree completed or expected within 12 months)
  • 2+ years of hands-on experimental research experience (e.g., doctoral dissertation, advanced wet chemical synthesis/etching, aqueous/non-aqueous solution chemistry, electrochemistry, surface functionalization, thin-film interface phenomena, or cleanroom wet bench processing)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated deep expertise in chemical reaction kinetics, selective wet etching, interfacial surface chemistry, corrosion/passivation mechanisms, or surfactant-assisted cleaning/drying mechanisms (e.g., Marangoni drying, supercritical (CO2), Surface modification (SMT))
  • Hands-on experience with advanced thin-film, surface, and chemical characterization techniques (e.g., Ellipsometry, AFM, SEM/TEM, XPS, contact angle goniometry, FTIR, TXRF, or ICP-MS)
  • Experience with automated fluidic systems, wet processing instrumentation design, single-wafer spin hardware, or experimental fluid dynamics/mass-transfer troubleshooting
  • Demonstrated experience utilizing Python, MATLAB, JMP, or Machine Learning for design of experiments (DOE), multivariate statistical analysis, or process automation
  • Strong publication record, conference presentations, or filed patent applications demonstrating systematic problem-solving in experimental chemical and materials science

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description:

As an Analog Product Development Engineer, you'll play a pivotal role in ensuring the manufacturability and testability of cutting-edge analog and RF integrated circuits. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to design, develop, and validate advanced test solutions, driving complex test equipment and software programs to evaluate performance. Business group
The Intel Corporation team is dedicated to delivering innovative solutions that drive technology forward. Focused on creating and validating high-performance analog and RF integrated circuits, the group collaborates across disciplines to enhance product quality, optimize manufacturability, and ensure successful production ramp. title: CPU Senior Floor Plan Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact Defines the physical dimensions of the CPU IP with consideration for overall product costs such as die size optimization, die per reticle/good die per wafer maximization, and right technology selection as it pertains to metal layers and reuse strategy across different SKUs in a product family. Performs integration of all dies in a package and completes the relevant checks before tape out. Creates and physical database for the IP. Collaborates with architects to optimize the placement of IPs for latency as well as die area/aspect ratio. Creates specifications and collaterals for the IP blocks to execute the floorplan and automatic place and route (APR) at subsequent hierarchies. Collaborates with the clock design and logic design teams to deliver the physical block level floorplans for APR. Collaborates with the power delivery team on tradeoffs for metal allocation for signal and power. Business group You will join Intel Corporation's team focused on CPU design and development, contributing to the creation of groundbreaking technologies that enable world-class computing solutions. This group thrives on innovation, delivering high-performance designs that support Intel's mission to shape the future of technology through the creation of industry-leading products. Key Responsibilities In this role you will be responsible for all the aspects of Floorplan and pin placement activities. You will engage with Architecture, DFT and package to arrive at optimal chip planning early in the design cycle. You will work closely with physical design cluster leads to comprehend design challenges and arrive at optimal floorplan. You will play critical role in die size estimation and in evaluating Floorplan tools, methods and flows. Planning boundaries and pin densities to facilitate high confidence timing closure and routability. With your broad understanding of physical design you will play a critical role in identifying and solving multitude design issues at partition/cluster and full chip. Expertise with multiple aspects of ASIC integration including Floorplanning, Clock and Power distribution, global signal planning, I-O planning and hard IP integration.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or equivalent education, with 3+ years of hands-on experience OR Master's degree in a relevant field with 2+ years of hands-on experience. - Proven expertise in using Floor planning, APR flows, Physical Design Verification Flows using Synopsys or Cadence tools. - Proficiency in hierarchical design approach, top-down design, budgeting, timing and physical convergence. - Strong knowledge of submicron process nodes and layout verification methodologies such as LVS and DRC. - Experience at handling IP/partition/block with multiple voltage and clock domains, ESD strategies, mixed signal block integration, and advanced package technologies. Preferred Qualifications - Familiarity with scripting languages such as Tcl, Perl, or Python for automation in physical design workflows. - Effective communication skills for collaboration across multidisciplinary teams. - Proven ability to work in dynamic and cross-geographical environments. - Knowledge of feature feasibility studies and advanced design flow methodologies. Contribute to groundbreaking advancements in CPU design and innovation by joining Intel Corporation. Take the next step to shape the future of technology-apply now.

title: Senior GPU Driver and Graphics Performance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


The Role and Impact
Join our GPU Software Performance team and contribute to shaping the world of 3D graphics and GPU technologies. Our team is responsible for improving 3D graphics performance of Intel GPUs on the Windows platform. You will join the team in Oregon, California or another location, where you will be part of a highly collaborative cross-geo cross-functional team that analyzes AAA games, including pre-release titles, for optimization opportunities in both shipping and pre-production hardware. We then optimize our driver and shader performance for graphics rendering to improve user experience. Additionally, we drive industry leading features to deployment. As part of this effort, we also developing internal tools and analysis capabilities.

title: Senior AI Systems Architect/Researcher
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About Central Engineering Group — Networking Architecture

The CEG Networking Architecture Group defines next-generation networking silicon and platform architecture for hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, and AI workloads. The team focuses on IPU/DPU platforms, advanced packet processing, programmable networking, and the data-movement technologies that enable modern distributed computing systems to scale efficiently.

Position Overview

This role is for a senior AI systems architect who can translate the communication, memory, and orchestration bottlenecks of large-scale AI into networking architecture, IP, and platform direction. The successful candidate will work across research, architecture, silicon, software, and product teams to shape the next generation of distributed AI infrastructure.

As a Senior AI Architect/Researcher, you will help define how AI systems communicate and move data at scale across xPUs, DPUs, IPUs, NICs, memory, and heterogeneous storage. In this pathfinding and research role, you will advance new architectural approaches and translate research insights into network architecture and software capabilities that can influence N+1 to N+3 product roadmap.

The ideal candidate thinks in systems rather than components, understands the memory wall and scale-out serving bottlenecks, and can reason across interconnect, memory hierarchy, software runtime, and compute to unlock the next order of magnitude in AI efficiency. You will help set technical direction and influence silicon and software roadmaps. The candidate is expected to maintain substantial knowledge of state-of-the-art principles and theories, contribute regularly to scientific literature and the research community-at-large, and may participate in the development of Intellectual Property.

Key Responsibilities

Turn Workload Analysis into New IP

• Analyze real AI serving and training workloads, identify communication and memory bottlenecks, and translate those findings into new IP, offload engines, platform features, and architecture requirements

• Drive hardware-software co-design across compute, DPU/IPU, NIC, SoC fabric, and AI serving runtimes, ensuring that networking and data-movement capabilities are reflected in modern inference and training frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others

Architect AI-Scale Networking and Interconnect

• Define the architectural direction for how AI systems and infrastructure move data at scale across xPU-to-xPU, xPU-to-storage, and cross-node paths spanning IPU/DPU platforms, NICs, and heterogeneous storage

• Shape next-generation packet processing, RDMA-class transport, and programmable networking IP that forms the backbone of hyperscale AI inference and training

Attack the Memory Wall and System-Level Bottlenecks

• Investigate the fundamental data-movement bottlenecks in large-scale AI and Agentic inference and training, including KV-cache transfer, disaggregated prefill/decode, model and tensor parallelism, and communication collectives, and translate them into concrete architectural requirements

• Reason across the full memory hierarchy and interconnect to minimize copies, latency, and bandwidth overhead, balancing latency-sensitive control paths against bandwidth-intensive data-paths

Set Roadmap and Lead Across Teams

• Shape multi-generation compute, memory, and interconnect roadmaps across IPU/DPU product lines by defining scaling strategies, migration paths, and architecture requirements that connect research insights to product execution

• Align architecture across networking, SoC fabric, firmware/OS/drivers, and performance modeling teams

What We're Looking For

To be successful in this role, you should demonstrate the following professional traits:

• Architectural vision — defines long-term strategy across AI systems, networking, memory, and software domains

• Influence without authority — drives alignment across multiple teams and disciplines

• Systems thinking — understands interactions across compute, memory, network, and software

• Decision-making under ambiguity — makes sound tradeoffs with incomplete data

• Collaboration — builds strong cross-functional relationships

• Customer-oriented mindset — translates workload needs into architectural innovations

• Ownership and accountability — drives initiatives end-to-end

• Continuous learning — stays current with evolving AI systems, inference runtimes, interconnects, memory technologies, and cloud infrastructure trends

A strong candidate will have enough depth to reason from first principles, enough practical experience to understand implementation constraints, and enough leadership range to align research, architecture, software, and silicon teams around a coherent direction.


Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

• Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 5+ years of relevant experience; or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM field with 2+ years of relevant experience

The experience must include:

• Experience with modern AI training and/or inference systems, including model architecture internals, hardware algorithm code design, serving runtimes, and the memory and data-movement bottlenecks that govern large-scale performance

• Hands-on experience with modern inference and training serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and others, with practical understanding of disaggregated prefill/decode, model parallelism, tensor parallelism, and the communication patterns they create

• Experience in computer architecture and system-level design, with a focus on networking, interconnect, or memory subsystems

• Proficiency in C/C++ and/or Python


Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with memory hierarchy and system bottleneck analysis, including caches, memory controllers, bandwidth/latency tradeoffs, and the memory wall as it applies to data-intensive workloads

• High-performance networking and data-movement technologies such as RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, or equivalent transport and interconnect

• Experience with IPU/DPU/SmartNIC or accelerator-centric SoCs, particularly in cloud and hyperscale environments

• Familiarity with PCIe, CXL, and memory semantics for high-performance IO

• Experience defining architecture from concept through silicon, platform software, or shipping product, including translating workload analysis into architecture requirements and new IP

• Track record of cross-team technical leadership and influencing architecture and roadmap at a senior level

title: AI System Performance Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role
We are looking for a talented and motivated AI System Performance Architect. The role owns the end-to-end understanding of AI training and inference systems, sitting where serving strategy, parallelism, collective communication, and interconnect behavior come together. Through analytical modelling and multi-GPU simulation, the candidate translates SLA and deployment targets into concrete architectural guidance for Intel's future AI platforms. Strong analytical skills and the ability to present performance findings and configuration recommendations to engineering and leadership teams are essential.

Key Responsibilities
• Own end-to-end understanding of the AI training/inference system and build analytical models and multi-GPU simulation - including MPI/collective communication (allgather, allreduce, all-to-all) and interconnect contention - to project performance, expose architectural bottlenecks, and recommend optimal Intel system configurations.
• Model inferencing strategies - static batching, continuous batching, disaggregated serving, and chunked prefill - across frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang, covering agentic inferencing, prefix caching, and multi-turn flows.
• Cover data, pipeline, tensor, and expert parallelism and their communication patterns.
• Drive studies against SLA targets - batch size, TTFT, TPOT, ISL/OSL, and TPS.
• Analyse regression run traces and find patterns in utilization counters across SLA operating points to identify architectural bottlenecks.
• Perform what-if analysis by sweeping core count, memory/cache capacity and bandwidth, fabric bandwidth, GPU interconnect, and deployment options; deliver optimization and optimal architecture recommendations.
• Scout whitepapers, blogs, and conferences; keep self and team updated on AI innovations applicable to Intel's end-to-end system.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's, master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Bachelors with 8+ yrs, master’s with 6+ years and Ph.D. with 3+ years of experience in system performance modelling, AI workload analysis, or hardware architecture.
• Strong proficiency in Python, with the ability to build modular, maintainable analytical models and simulation frameworks.
• Solid understanding of LLM inference and training mechanics: prefill vs. decode, KV cache, batching policies, and quantization.
• Working knowledge of distributed parallelism strategies and their communication patterns.
• Familiarity with multi-GPU interconnect architectures (NVLink, PCIe, CXL, or equivalent).
• Understanding of SoC and platform fundamentals: core count scaling, cache/memory capacity and bandwidth, and fabric behavior.

Good-to-Have Skills
• Experience building discrete-event simulators for multi-node or multi-accelerator systems.
• Familiarity with performance profiling tools (e.g., Intel VTune, NVIDIA Nsight, or similar).
• Prior experience in a semiconductor or hardware company working on AI accelerator or platform products.

title: GPU Software Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

As a GPU Software Development Engineer, you will play a critical role in designing and developing software solutions that enable Intel's GPUs, ranging from firmware and device drivers to APIs and application layers. You will work on cutting-edge kernel-level features that drive functionality, power management, and performance optimization for integrated and discrete graphics products. Your contributions will directly shape immersive visual experiences for millions of users, ensuring Intel's leadership in graphics technologies.

Business Group

We are the Windows Kernel Mode Driver Team within Intel's Client Graphics IP group of DCG. Our primary objective is the development and deployment of robust and performant Windows kernel GPU drivers.  These drivers are instrumental in unleashing the full potential of Intel's integrated and discrete GPU hardware for user-space clients, games, and applications.

Our focus lies in managing critical low-level functions, including device activation, reset and power state transitions, workload submission, power conservation, and scheduling, as well as collaboration with System-on-Chip (SOC) Intellectual Properties (IPs). With this charter, we conceive, create, and verify software solutions that serve as the link between user-space applications and the underlying GPU and SOC.  If you thrive in an environment that involves working on system-level software, with regular exposure to diverse domains such as graphics rendering, firmware, SOC, and power management, then a role on our Kernel Mode Driver Team is where you should be.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop, validate, and optimize GPU kernel-mode drivers for Windows operating systems.
  • Collaborate on implementing low-level features, including device activation, power management, and workload scheduling for integrated and discrete GPUs.
  • Design and debug firmware and software features related to GPU hardware and accompanying System-on-Chip (SOC) components.
  • Analyze telemetry and resolve complex issues across layers of driver stacks, domains, and IP integration.
  • Contribute to the creation of test frameworks, workload automation, and validation methodologies to ensure high-quality code delivery.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related STEM field.

title: GPU Architecture and AI Performance Simulation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role
We are looking for a talented and motivated GPU Architecture and AI Performance Simulation Engineer. The role sits at the intersection of AI workloads and next-generation GPU hardware - analyzing, modeling, and optimizing AI workload performance on GPU and SoC architectures to shape architectural decisions across current and future silicon. The candidate will guide the team in fine-tuning workload, SoC, and system models, propose data-backed architectural enhancements, and track the AI GPU market to inform Intel's future accelerator roadmap. Strong analytical skills, the ability to present performance findings and trade-offs to engineering and leadership teams, and a willingness to mentor peers are essential.

Key Responsibilities
• Analyze AI workload behavior on GPU architectures - distinguishing compute-bound, memory-bound, and cache-bound behavior to identify performance bottlenecks and optimization opportunities.
• Build and maintain roofline analytical models and cycle-accurate performance models to support hardware what-if studies and guide micro-architectural decisions.
• Analyze AI workloads built on Transformer and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, inference and training, and assess the hardware-utilization impact of kernel-level optimizations such as Flash Attention, Flash Decode, Sparse Attention, and Causal Masking.
• Model and analyze multi-GPU and at-scale AI systems - workload distribution, synchronization overhead, and communication-compute overlap.
• Drive workload and architectural bottleneck analysis for the early architecture definition phases of Intel's future AI GPU accelerator roadmap products.
• Guide and mentor the team in delivering analytical models and end-to-end system-level performance projections; review modeling methodology and drive consistency across studies.
• Propose new architectural enhancement ideas, backed by quantitative modeling data and workload evidence.
• Maintain a forward-looking view of the AI GPU and accelerator market - tracking competitive roadmaps, whitepapers, and conferences - and translate those trends into architectural requirements while keeping the team updated on applicable AI innovations.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's with 10+ yrs, master’s with 8+ years and Ph.D with 5+ years of experience in System/GPU/SoC performance engineering, AI workload analysis, or hardware architecture.
• Deep knowledge of GPU microarchitecture (NVIDIA SM/CUDA cores, Intel Xe cores, or equivalent), GPU execution pipelines, and cache hierarchy design (L1/L2/L3).
• Familiarity with SoC design principles, on-chip fabric, memory subsystems, and interconnects.
• Experience with multi-GPU system architectures (NVLink, PCIe, CXL, or equivalent) and scaling AI workloads across multiple devices.
• Good understanding of distributed training/inference techniques: Tensor Parallel, Data Parallel, Pipeline Parallel, Expert Parallel, and Model Split methodologies.


Good-to-Have Skills
• Experience with cycle-accurate simulators or hardware performance emulation platforms.
• Familiarity with AI framework internals (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow) and kernel-level optimization (CUDA, SYCL, HIP, Triton).
• Exposure to LLM inference optimization techniques (quantization, KV-cache management, speculative decoding).
• Experience with performance profiling tools (e.g., NVIDIA Nsight, Intel VTune, AMD ROCProfiler, or similar).
• Publications or patents in GPU architecture, AI systems performance, or related areas.

We're looking for talented individuals excited to solve complex challenges and shape the future of platform architecture. If you're ready to make an impact and contribute to Intel's success, we encourage you to apply today.

descriptionHtml:

Intel’s Data Center Platform Engineering hardware team develops and supports platform solutions for leading cloud service providers and internet companies. These solutions integrate Intel data center products—including CPUs, GPUs, and NICs—across servers, storage systems, hardware accelerators, and infrastructure processing platforms. We are looking for a high-potential hardware engineer to help bring next-generation data center technologies to market while building a rewarding career.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Intel's Foundry Automation (IFA) group is seeking an experienced Infrastructure Systems Engineer to join our team.


In this role, you will lead the architecture, deployment, optimization, automation, and lifecycle management of enterprise Windows Server platforms, with, supporting engineering, manufacturing, cloud, virtualization, and application infrastructure environments. You will be responsible for delivering secure, highly available, and scalable infrastructure services while driving platform modernization initiatives across physical, virtual, and cloud-enabled environments.


This role is central to designing, implementing, maintaining, and scaling Microsoft-based infrastructure that supports Intel Foundry's critical manufacturing and engineering operations. While the environment is primarily Windows-focused, the role also provides operational support for Linux platforms, particularly Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), within hybrid infrastructure environments. You will collaborate closely with platform engineering, cloud, virtualization, network, security, storage, and software engineering teams to build reliable, automated, and highly available infrastructure services.


The ideal candidate combines strong Windows systems expertise with automation, infrastructure engineering, and operational excellence. Experience administering Linux systems is desirable, but deep knowledge of enterprise Windows technologies, identity services, security, and automation is the primary focus of this role.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the lifecycle management of Windows Server 2019, Windows Server 2022, and future Windows Server platforms, including deployment, configuration, patching, hardening, upgrades, and decommissioning.
  • Design, implement, and support core Microsoft infrastructure services including:
    • Active Directory
    • Group Policy
    • DNS and DHCP
    • PKI and Certificate Services
    • IIS and .NET application hosting
    • Windows Failover Clustering
    • Microsoft SQL Server infrastructure
  • Develop and maintain automation solutions using PowerShell, Python, and Bash to streamline infrastructure provisioning, compliance, patch management, monitoring, and operational workflows.
  • Implement and maintain Windows security controls, including vulnerability remediation, endpoint protection, privileged access management, system hardening, and compliance requirements.
  • Support Windows-based workloads running on VMware, OpenShift Virtualization, and cloud-hosted environments.
  • Provide operational administration and support for Linux systems, including RHEL deployment, patching, troubleshooting, security maintenance, and lifecycle management.
  • Monitor infrastructure health, perform performance tuning, troubleshoot complex operating system and platform issues, and drive root-cause analysis for production incidents.
  • Collaborate with network, storage, security, and platform engineering teams to deliver resilient enterprise infrastructure solutions.
  • Develop and maintain operational documentation, architecture standards, implementation procedures, and troubleshooting guides.

The Ideal Candidate Must Demonstrate:

  • Strong hands-on experience administering Windows Server 2019, Windows Server 2022, and enterprise Microsoft infrastructure environments.
  • Deep knowledge of Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, PKI, IIS, Windows authentication, and Microsoft security technologies.
  • Strong PowerShell scripting and automation experience, with familiarity in Python and Bash.
  • Experience supporting highly available, large-scale Windows environments in virtualized and hybrid infrastructure deployments.
  • Working knowledge of Linux administration, preferably Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL).
  • Knowledge of Windows security, patch management, system hardening, identity management, and compliance best practices.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

This position requires regular onsite presence at our Chandler, Arizona facility.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
Intel's Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) team is the backbone of our 24x7 manufacturing and foundry operations, ensuring the seamless automated delivery and storage of materials across our state-of-the-art fabrication facilities. We are looking for a motivated and skilled AMHS Equipment Technician to join our dedicated team of technicians, engineers, and managers in Rio Rancho, NM. In this role, you will play a critical part in keeping Intel's manufacturing operations running at peak performance by maintaining, troubleshooting, and optimizing our AMHS infrastructure.

Business Group
The Intel Foundry business group focuses on delivering cutting-edge manufacturing solutions, enabling Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry. This group drives innovation and ensures operational excellence in Intel's state-of-the-art facilities. Joining this team means becoming part of a global network that collaborates to deliver reliable and scalable solutions foundational to Intel's commitment to technology advancement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor AMHS operations in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, proactively detecting and responding to system issues to ensure continuous manufacturing flow
  • Perform timely electrical and mechanical troubleshooting to diagnose and resolve issues in electromechanical equipment
  • Execute preventive and corrective maintenance on all AMHS equipment and sub-assemblies, including setup and calibration
  • Log system problems and errors accurately in designated databases, maintaining detailed and precise records
  • Respond to escalations in partnership with Manufacturing Service Desks, Equipment Engineering teams, and other key stakeholders
  • Dismantle, adjust, repair, and reassemble equipment in accordance with layout plans, blueprints, operating manuals, and technical drawings
  • Provide project support for AMHS installation and modification projects as required
  • Collaborate with AMHS hardware engineers and product owners to escalate and resolve complex technical challenges
  • Serve as a buddy, trainer, and/or certifier for team members, contributing to the development of training materials
  • Achieve and maintain L3 and advanced equipment certification milestones through established training processes
  • Uphold Intel's Safety and Quality Culture standards, acting as a role model for work ethics and results
  • Demonstrate flexibility to rotate across shifts to support staffing and organizational needs

  • Adaptable - You embrace change and thrive in dynamic, evolving environments
  • Detail-oriented - You take pride in precision and accuracy in everything you do
  • A team player - You foster collaboration, support your colleagues, and contribute to a positive team culture

title: Senior Platform Hardware Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Position Overview As a Platform Hardware Design Engineer, you will provide technical leadership for the architecture, design, integration, bring-up, and validation of complex platform hardware. You will drive hardware development end-to-end, translating high level system requirements into detailed circuit and component specifications and leading designs from architecture and schematic development through PCB implementation, board power-on, debugging, validation, and delivery. You will be expected to make platform level technical decisions, resolve complex and ambiguous multidisciplinary problems, lead critical design reviews, drive cross-functional alignment, mentor engineers, and influence hardware development practices across projects. Our Business Group You will be joining the Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE), an organization at Intel committed to advancing Intel's mission of delivering world-class silicon and platform solutions. The group focuses on developing integrated systems that align with customer needs and support Intel's broader goals of leadership in technology innovation. SPE collaborates across diverse domains to ensure Intel platforms meet performance, reliability, and scalability requirements. Our work sits at the intersection of silicon, board hardware, firmware, validation, signal and power integrity, mechanical and thermal engineering, PCB technology, manufacturing, and system integration. Our senior hardware engineers have a broader responsibility than executing an individual design. They help establish platform architecture, guide implementation, identify and qualify appropriate hardware solutions, provide technical leadership during board power-on and debug, and lead resolution of schematic, layout, SI/PI, and hardware issues. Key Responsibilities Platform Architecture and End-to-End Technical Ownership • Own complex platform-board designs from requirements and architecture through deployment. • Translate high level platform and silicon requirements into system architecture, circuit level requirements, component specifications, and PCB implementation requirements. • Define and drive critical platform architecture decisions encompassing high speed interfaces, memory, power delivery, clocking, resets, sequencing, control, management, and validation functionality. • Lead design trade-offs across electrical performance, SI/PI, thermal and mechanical constraints, board complexity, reliability, manufacturability, component availability, cost, schedule, and system compatibility. • Establish clear technical direction where platform requirements or implementation approaches are initially ambiguous. Advanced Board Design and Technical Leadership • Lead development of complex high density, multilayer PCBs incorporating advanced digital, analog, mixed signal, and power circuitry. • Own or provide technical leadership for schematic design, component selection, interface definition, PCB implementation, and design verification. • Establish PCB stack-up, placement, routing, impedance, power distribution, and critical interface requirements in collaboration with layout and analysis teams. • Lead schematic, layout, and technical design reviews and ensure critical findings are driven to closure. • Guide engineers and layout teams in resolving challenging schematic, PCB, layout, and design-for-X issues. • Identify and qualify new hardware solutions and reusable design approaches where appropriate. High-Speed Design and SI/PI • Apply deep understanding of signal integrity, power integrity, transmission-line behavior, high-speed interfaces, and platform power delivery to architecture and implementation decisions. • Partner with SI/PI engineers to establish design constraints and evaluate critical interfaces and power delivery networks. • Review PCB implementations for stack-up, placement, routing, return path continuity, high speed performance, and advanced SI/PI considerations. • Use modeling, simulation, measurement, and hardware correlation to guide technical decisions as appropriate. Power Architecture and Power Delivery • Define and review platform power delivery architecture, voltage regulation, sequencing, power budgeting, and power distribution networks. • Evaluate board and system power delivery tradeoffs, considering electrical performance, transient behavior, PCB implementation, and platform requirements. • Work with power integrity specialists to assess PDN behavior and drive required design improvements. • Apply simulation and hardware measurement to correlate power delivery behavior and resolve platform issues. Board Bring-up, System Integration and Debug • Define and lead power-on, bring up, validation, characterization, and debug strategy for complex platform hardware. • Lead resolution of difficult issues spanning board hardware, silicon, firmware, high-speed interfaces, power delivery, and system integration. • Use disciplined root cause analysis to diagnose failures and define corrective actions. • Provide hands-on technical leadership in the lab during critical power-on, bring up, and debug activities. • Apply appropriate measurement techniques and laboratory equipment for high speed, low speed, clock, power, and digital/analog circuitry. • Drive problems across engineering boundaries until technical closure. Program and Cross-functional Leadership • Serve as a senior technical interface across silicon, firmware, validation, SI/PI, mechanical, thermal, PCB layout, manufacturing, suppliers, and program teams. • Lead technical discussions and design reviews and communicate risks, tradeoffs, recommendations, and design decisions clearly to stakeholders. • Identify technical and execution risks early and drive mitigation plans. • Own technical readiness for critical hardware milestones, including design release, fabrication, assembly, power-on, and validation. • Develop and improve reusable architectures, review methodologies, design checklists, development flows, and engineering practices. • Mentor engineers through architecture development, schematic and PCB reviews, bring-up, debug, and technical problem solving. • Influence technical decisions and engineering practices beyond an individual board or project.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.
• 6+ years significant hands-on industry experience in complex platform hardware, PCB development, or system hardware engineering.
• Demonstrated experience leading complex board designs from architecture and requirements through schematic design, PCB implementation, bring-up, debug, and validation.
• Deep understanding of digital and analog board design, electrical interfaces, mixed-signal fundamentals, and system architecture.
• Strong knowledge of high speed interfaces, transmission line behavior, signal integrity, power integrity, memory, clocking, reset, sequencing, and power delivery.
• Proven experience with PCB technologies and layout techniques, including stack-up, placement, routing, and advanced SI/PI considerations.

• Strong hands-on laboratory experience and demonstrated ability to diagnose complex board level problems, determine root cause, and drive corrective actions.
• Demonstrated ability to analyze board/system level design tradeoffs and make sound technical decisions.
• Ability to independently lead complex technical development activities and drive issues across multiple engineering functions.
• Strong technical documentation, presentation, written communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
• Demonstrated technical leadership and mentoring capability.

title: Platform Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About Central Engineering Group

The Central Engineering Group (CEG) is Intel's hub for driving innovation and excellence in silicon development. Focused on engineering solutions that power Intel's flagship products, CEG architects, designs, and validates IP foundational to Intel's broader technology portfolio. By joining this team, you will be part of a collaborative, inclusive environment driving advancements to strengthen Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry.

Position Overview

As an IP Logic Design Engineer at Intel, you will play a pivotal role in developing high-quality IP blocks and subsystems for integration into full chip designs. You'll be responsible for creating cutting-edge logic designs, optimizing power, performance, and area, and ensuring seamless integration with the broader system. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver next-generation silicon solutions with speed, efficiency, and reliability.


Key Responsibilities

• Develop logic designs, register transfer level (RTL) coding, and simulation for IP blocks and subsystems for integration into full chip designs

• Define architecture and microarchitecture features and ensure their implementation in the design

• Optimize design logic to meet power, performance, area, and timing goals while maintaining physical implementation integrity

• Review verification plans and address RTL test failures to ensure accurate validation of design features

• Collaborate with physical design teams to address floorplan limitations and integrate designs seamlessly

• Drive quality assurance compliance to enable smooth IP-to-SoC handoff


What We're Looking For

title: Senior Azure DevOps Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Senior Azure DevOps Engineer - Full-Stack and Hybrid Cloud Systems
Bangalore, India ' Full-Time
About the Role
We are looking for an experienced, versatile Azure DevOps Engineer to join our team and become a genuine part of what we are building.
This is not a straightforward DevOps role. Our system spans a full-stack web application, a rich and deliberately complex Azure cloud environment, and on-premises Linux lab infrastructure that talks directly to FPGA hardware. The person who thrives here will be someone who gets energized by that kind of variety, not overwhelmed by it.
Just as importantly, we are looking for someone who communicates well, enjoys working closely with developers and customers, and takes real pride in the quality and reliability of what they build and maintain. Technical depth matters, but so does being someone the team genuinely enjoys working with.
The Environment You Will Be Working In
The Application
We build and operate a full-stack web application with a Node.js server, TypeScript services, and a React.js client. The application connects to on-premises Linux lab environments where a Python-based layer orchestrates and controls FPGA hardware. The cloud and the physical lab need to talk to each other reliably, securely, and continuously.
The Internal Azure Subscription
This environment is mature, fully operational, and genuinely complex. Containerized workloads run on Kubernetes. We use the right database for the right job: relational databases for structured data, a document store for flexibility, in-memory caching for performance, distributed file storage for shared access, and large-scale telemetry and analytics through Azure Data Explorer. Identity and access management spans SSO, Active Directory, Kerberos, and Microsoft Entra ID, because our permission model is real-world complex, not textbook simple. We also run an internal HPC-grade job scheduling system that manages compute resource allocation and permissions across lab infrastructure.
The External Azure Subscription
This subscription is starting now and will serve customers outside our organization. Security, network architecture, compliance, and performance are the foundation here, not afterthoughts. You will be building this alongside our network and cybersecurity teams with genuine ownership of getting it right.
What You Will Be Doing
CI/CD and Developer Support
Design, maintain, and continuously improve pipelines covering the full delivery lifecycle for our Node.js, TypeScript, and React codebase. When something breaks in a pipeline or a release goes sideways, the development team will come to you, and you will be the person who unblocks them calmly and effectively. Beyond day-to-day support, you will raise the quality bar by embedding good practices into the workflow: automated testing, regression coverage, reproducible builds, and documentation that people actually use.
Automation and AI-Driven Operations
We want a platform that monitors itself, detects problems, and recovers on its own wherever possible. When it cannot, it should tell us clearly and give us what we need to act fast. We want you to use AI tools actively and creatively to get there, whether that means intelligent alerting, automated remediation, generated runbooks, or things we have not thought of yet. Every repeated manual task is a candidate for automation.
Platform and Infrastructure Engineering
Own the day-to-day health and long-term evolution of our internal Azure environment: Kubernetes workloads, data services, storage, networking, and identity systems. Maintain the bridge between cloud and lab, keeping our Linux hosts and hardware systems connected and operational as the platform grows.
Security and the External-Facing Cloud
Work closely with our network and cybersecurity teams to design and harden the external subscription before customers ever touch it. Zero-trust access, network segmentation, secrets management, private endpoints, and audit logging need to be built in from the start. We need someone who thinks about security architecturally, not just operationally.
Required Qualifications
Why Join Us
The work is technically rich and varied in a way that is hard to find. You will not be executing tickets. You will be shaping how the platform evolves, with real ownership and real impact on both the team that builds the product and the customers who use it. We are a collaborative group that values good judgment, welcomes new ideas, and tries hard to be a team people are glad to be part of.

Qualifications:

4+ years of hands-on experience with Azure DevOps and cloud infrastructure, including ownership of production environments.
Azure DevOps and CI/CD: Strong experience with YAML pipelines, Repos, Artifacts, self-hosted build agents, Git workflows, and release management, including deployment across development, test, and production environments, versioning, and rollback.
Kubernetes and AKS: Practical experience deploying, operating, and troubleshooting production workloads using Docker and Helm, including configuration, networking, storage, scaling, and upgrades.
Azure infrastructure and networking: Experience managing compute, storage, virtual networks, DNS, firewalls, and connectivity between cloud and on-premises environments.
Infrastructure as Code: Experience creating repeatable infrastructure deployments using Terraform, Bicep, or equivalent tools.
Linux administration: Strong troubleshooting skills across services, processes, permissions, networking, storage, and shared file systems such as NFS.
Scripting and automation: Ability to write maintainable automation using Python, Bash, PowerShell, or similar languages to reduce manual work and improve reliability.
Application delivery: Experience building CI/CD pipelines for JavaScript and TypeScript applications, particularly React frontends, Node.js backends, and containerized microservices.
Identity and cloud security: Practical understanding of Microsoft Entra ID, authentication and authorization, role-based access control, service and workload identities, secrets and certificate management, least privilege, and network isolation.
Database operations: Working knowledge of relational databases, particularly Microsoft SQL Server, and familiarity with NoSQL systems. Ability to manage deployment, connectivity, access permissions, monitoring, backup and recovery, and operational troubleshooting.
Monitoring and incident resolution: Experience with centralized logs, metrics, dashboards, and alerts using Azure Monitor, Application Insights, or equivalent tools, with the ability to investigate failures across applications and infrastructure.
Technical ownership and collaboration: Ability to drive infrastructure improvements from design through production, document decisions, and work effectively with developers, IT, and security teams.
Advantages
Experience securing and operating customer-facing or external-user cloud environments.
Experience with hybrid platforms connecting cloud services to physical hardware, lab systems, or FPGA environments.
Experience managing both Linux and Windows build agents and their dependencies.
Practical use of AI-assisted engineering or AIOps tools for automation, troubleshooting, incident analysis, or operational improvement.

title: PnP System Validation and Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The PnP SV (Power and Performance System Validation) group is responsible for the functional (logical) integrity of the processor, from the first silicon stage through to mass production.

In the period before the first silicon, the group is responsible for defining the processor testing methodology and its environment, defining test plans, and developing some of the software and hardware tools required to perform the tests.

In the period between the first silicon and readiness for mass production, the group focuses on running the defined tests and performs DEBUG of failures in order to ensure that all logical bugs have been found. After approval for mass production, problems and bugs that were missed (from customers) arrive, and work is done on them (as each processor has many derivatives).

The work in the department involves collaboration with additional groups – logic design, architecture, software groups for tool and simulator development, and more.

A complete project lasts between two to four years, with each phase taking approximately half of that period.

Job Description

  • Taking an active part in performance and power measurement and improvement tests for Intel's flagship processors and various platforms.
  • Defining and executing test plans, debugging in highly complex environments using advanced equipment and innovative methods.
  • Participating in setting goals, plans, and work methodologies. Working closely with product architects, the design group, software, and Validation teams in Israel and abroad.

Qualifications:

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science
  • 3-6 years of experience working with processor architecture or at the system/platform level of a processor and operating system, preferably in the field of Silicon/Platform Validation – mandatory
  • Programming knowledge in Python – mandatory
  • Programming knowledge in C++ – advantage

title: Senior Analog and Mixed Signal Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Group

Intel's Advanced Design Foundational IP Organization (AD-FIP) within Design Technology Platform (DTP) drives pathfinding and development of the analog/mixed-signal and high-speed I/O IP that defines what Intel's leading-edge process technologies can deliver. The High-Speed I/O team develops SerDes and die-to-die interface reference designs and test chips that co-optimize Intel process technology with next-generation wireline standards, including high-speed PAM4 electrical links, PCIe, UCIe, and HBM.

The Role

We are seeking a senior technical expert in high-speed SerDes circuit design and SerDes system architecture. You will own SerDes link architecture on Intel's leading technology test chips, from link budget and equalization strategy down to transistor-level design of the critical analog front-end and clocking blocks. You will also translate link requirements into device, interconnect, and design-rule requirements that shape future Intel process nodes. This is a senior individual-contributor role with technical leadership across design, layout, and measurement engineers.

Responsibilities

  • Define SerDes link architecture for next-generation interfaces (224G/448G-class PAM4 electrical links, PCIe Gen7/Gen8, UCIe): channel analysis, link budget, jitter and noise budgeting, and equalization partitioning across TX FFE, RX CTLE, DFE, and ADC/DSP-based receivers.
  • Build and maintain system-level link models (statistical and time-domain, in MATLAB or Python; COM and IBIS-AMI based) and use them to derive block-level specifications for TX, RX, ADC, and clocking circuits.
  • Lead transistor-level design of critical SerDes blocks: TX drivers (SST/CML) with FFE, RX AFE (CTLE, VGA, termination, T-coil and ESD co-design), DFE and slicers, time-interleaved ADC front ends, CDR and phase interpolators, LC and ring PLLs, and clock distribution.
  • Drive test-chip definition, integration, tapeout readiness, and silicon bring-up; correlate measured BER, eye, jitter, and power against models, and lead root-cause analysis of silicon-to-model gaps.
  • Translate SerDes requirements into process and PDK requirements (device fT/fmax and parasitics, BEOL RC, inductor Q, matching, ESD capacitance budget, reliability and aging) and drive design-technology co-optimization with process, PDK, and template-library teams.
  • Provide technical leadership: mentor engineers, lead design reviews, and represent Intel Foundry in technical engagements with IP partners and foundry customers.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelors Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical and Computer Engineering with 6+ years of industry experience in high-speed wireline SerDes circuit design experience -OR- Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical and Computer Engineering with 4+ years of industry experience in high-speed wireline SerDes circuit design, -OR-  Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Electrical and Computer Engineering with 2+ years of industry experience in high-speed wireline SerDes circuit design.
  • Experience in Transistor-level design of SerDes TX, RX, or clocking circuits in at least one silicon-proven design at 28 Gb/s per lane or higher.
  • Experience in at least one of the following:
    • SerDes link architecture: channel and link-budget analysis or equalization trade-off studies used to set block-level specifications.
    • Lab validation of high-speed links: BER, eye, or jitter measurement and correlation to simulation.
    • Behavioral or statistical link modeling in MATLAB or Python.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Silicon-proven designs at 56 Gb/s PAM4 or higher, in FinFET or GAA CMOS; multiple tape-outs with block ownership.
  • Experience across all three areas above (architecture, lab validation, and link modeling).
  • Experience in ADC/DSP-based receivers at 112 Gb/s PAM4 or higher, including time-interleaved ADC design. - 224 Gb/s-class link development (IEEE 802.3dj, OIF CEI-224G). - PCIe Gen6/Gen7 PHY or UCIe die-to-die PHY development.
  • Design experience on 5nm-class or more advanced nodes, with design-technology co-optimization experience with process teams.
  • Experience in package and channel co-design: package/PCB channel modeling, signal and power integrity, crosstalk.
  • Experience with first-author publications at ISSCC, VLSI Symposium, CICC, or JSSC; patents in SerDes circuits or architecture.
  • Technical leadership of a multi-engineer SerDes design team through a full PHY delivery.

title: APTM Yield Analysis/Device Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet. By joining the Advanced Packaging Technology and Manufacturing (APTM) Yield Group, you will be part of a team tasked with the critical objective of driving yield and defect improvement across our entire advanced packaging portfolio. We solve highly complex physical and electrical problems to ensure our latest packaging technologies successfully transition from development into high-volume manufacturing.

We are seeking a APTM Yield Analysis/Device Engineer to drive technology development, transfers, and manufacturing ramps in Rio Rancho, New Mexico. In this role, you will analyze massive, multi-dimensional datasets to identify where manufacturing processes, test content, and inline metrologies must be optimized. Acting as a strategic technical advisor, you will set clear engineering priorities, lead cross-functional problem-solving initiatives, and directly influence our technology yield roadmap.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Data Synthesis & Insight Extraction: Extract insights from structured and unstructured factory datasets using statistical methods, machine learning, and tools like JMP or Python.
  • Failure Correlation: Correlate electrical and physical failure mechanisms by utilizing deep knowledge of Failure Analysis (FIFA), Design for Test (DFT), Sort/Test, and Integration/Process flows.
  • Defect System Optimization: Manage inline defect metrologies, evaluate detection capabilities, and drive inline defect reduction programs across the factory.
  • Technical Program Leadership: Lead a small group of engineers (direct or indirect) to execute experiments, resolve nonstandard yield events, and ensure smooth technology transfers to High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM).
  • Stakeholder Reporting & Collaboration: Deliver detailed technical reports summarizing yield and device health to upstream and downstream partners, establishing clear action plans to achieve best-in-class yield levels.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence: Instills a high-performing team culture with a willingness to lead, guide, and collaborate across diverse organizational boundaries.
  • Tolerance for Ambiguity & Flexibility: Adapts rapidly to changing priorities, new technical fields of study, and fluctuating business demands.
  • Strategic Prioritization & Autonomy: Works with minimal direct oversight to prioritize critical path items and resolve complex, unstructured technical issues.
  • Executive Communication: Delivers concise, high-impact technical presentations to influence decision-making among diverse groups at all levels.

Apply today to join Intel New Mexico's APTM Yield Group and lead the technical breakthroughs that power global computing. Let's build the future together.

technology priorities. The role requires exceptional writing, sound executive judgment, and the ability to deliver in a complex, fast-moving environment.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description:

You will help maintain quality excellence while contributing to APCC's mission of delivering standardized, high-quality execution at scale. Your primary focus will be the accurate classification of defects captured by multiple inspection systems. Through precise defect classification, you will play a vital role in minimizing defect noise, driving systematic defect reduction initiatives, and maintaining the optimal balance between quality control and manufacturing efficiency.

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to
Defect Classification and Analysis:
• Review and Analyze defect images captured by diverse metrology tools.
• Accurately classify defects based on documented defect specification.
• Distinguish between true defects requiring disposition action and false positives or nuisance defects.
• Maintain proficiency across multiple inspection platforms and adapt classification criteria to different tool capabilities and imaging conditions

Defect Validation:
• Verify defect classifications against established criteria and specifications
• Partner with Layer Owner to ensure consistent defect categorization approaches
• Prevent over-rejection scenarios by accurately identifying non-critical defects and cosmetic variations that do not impact product performance.
• Avoid under-rejection situations by ensuring killed defects are properly identified and flagged for disposition.

Hold Lot Disposition:
• Ensure strict compliance in review and disposition of hold lots based on documented Out-of-Control Action Plans (OCAP)
• Ensure proper documentation and traceability of all disposition decisions.
• Collaborate with Layer Owner to update and refine OCAP procedures based on emerging defect patterns

title: CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Performs physical design implementation of CPU designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing. Conducts all aspects of the CPU physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis. Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking. Analyzes results and makes recommendations to improve current and future CPU microarchitectures closely collaborating with logic, circuit, architecture, and design automation teams. Possesses CPU specific expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, structured placement, routing, synthesis, and DFT. Works intimately with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a highspeed, low power synthesizable CPU. Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area. Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.

Qualifications:

As a CPU Physical Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in implementing high-performance, low-power CPU designs from RTL to GDSII. You will focus on detailed processes such as synthesis, placement, routing, timing analysis, and power optimization, enabling designs that meet stringent performance and efficiency targets. Your work will directly influence the success of Intel's next-generation CPUs and their manufacturing readiness, contributing to innovative advancements in computing technology.

You will join a dynamic team dedicated to designing Intel's latest high-performance CPUs using cutting-edge technologies. title: Deep Learning Hardware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Intel's Client AI Architecture team is seeking an Deep Learning Hardware Engineer to help shape future generations of Intel's Neural Processing Unit (NPU) architecture for AI PCs, Edge AI, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and multimodal foundation models.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of AI, computer architecture, and hardware-software co-design to optimize AI workloads and drive innovations in next-generation AI acceleration technologies. You will collaborate with architecture, software, compiler, and machine learning teams to develop high-performance, power-efficient AI solutions for Intel client platforms.

The ideal candidate has experience developing, optimizing, or deploying AI workloads on NPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, or related computing architectures. Experience with Intel NPUs, OpenVINO, AI software stacks, compiler technologies, AI inference optimization, and hardware-software co-design is highly desirable.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Contribute to the design and optimization of neural compute and AI accelerator architectures.
  • Develop and evaluate RTL implementations of hardware features supporting machine learning workloads.

title: Compiler Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Compiler Engineering team in Data Center Group at Intel has an opportunity available for a Compiler Engineer.

At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. You will contribute to an ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.

The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models.

As a Compiler Engineer, you will play a critical role in advancing compiler technologies that deliver exceptional performance and scalability across Intel architectures.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Designing, developing, testing, debugging, and maintaining advanced compiler technologies and software components.
• Driving the implementation of new compiler features and resolving software defects.
• Analyzing real-world applications, workloads, and benchmarks to identify optimization opportunities.
• Improving the performance and efficiency of compiler-generated code for Intel CPU architectures.
• Conducting functional, performance, scalability, and stress testing to ensure product quality and reliability.
• Partnering with hardware architects and platform teams to enable new processor capabilities.
• Collaborating across global engineering, validation, and performance teams to deliver high-quality products.

The Compiler Engineering team in Intel's Data Center Group is looking for talented and passionate compiler engineers.

At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. descriptionHtml:

Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing in building the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing factories across the globe. The future is what we build.

Our enterprise manages a portfolio of capital projects on-site with a large contractor workforce that encompasses outsourced general contractors, A/E firms, and key trade companies in the Semiconductor Construction Industry.

The Quality Assurance/Quality Control Manager will be responsible for the Intel site construction quality assurance program and project quality systems to support all areas of semiconductor construction projects. The Quality QA/QC manager will also provide oversight to Intel's direct contracted 3rd party inspection firms (geotechnical, civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, and process).

  • Develop a 3rd party resource plan to include QAR firm, high purity analytical test firm, Exhaust Test and Balance firm, Special Inspection Agencies, Gas and Chem system technician team, Life Safety system startup and test team
