title: CBS E2E Finance Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Overview:

The E2E Finance Architect will own the enterprise Finance solution architecture across SAP Financial Accounting and Controlling (FICO), subledger accounting, product costing, fixed assets, Project Accounting, SAP Profitability and Performance Management (PaPM), and SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) for Financial Planning and Analysis (FP and A).

This role will provide architecture leadership for the current IAO transformation and maintain long-term ownership of the Finance technology roadmap after implementation. The architect will partner with Accounting, Manufacturing Finance, FP and A, business process owners, IT, and implementation partners to deliver integrated, scalable, and controlled Finance solutions.

Key Responsibilities:

End-to-end solution architecture ownership: Define and govern the Finance target architecture, solution designs, integration patterns, and architectural standards. Resolve cross-functional design issues and ensure consistency across accounting, costing, profitability, planning, and reporting.

Accounting and subledgers: Lead solution architecture across general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, intercompany accounting, bank accounting, financial close, and subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation. Ensure consistent financial data, reporting dimensions, and auditability.

  • Product costing and manufacturing finance: Solution Architect standard and actual costing, Material Ledger, inventory valuation, work in process, overhead allocation, production variances, and profitability analysis. Address semiconductor requirements across wafer fabrication, assembly and test, yield and scrap impacts, and internal or outsourced manufacturing.
  • Fixed assets and Project Accounting: Own solution architecture for asset acquisition, assets under construction, capitalization, depreciation, transfers, and retirement. Integrate project structures, budgeting, commitments, cost collection, and settlement with fixed assets and financial accounting.
  • SAP PaPM: Define solution architecture for cost allocations, profitability models, business-driver calculations, and scenario analysis. Ensure transparent calculation logic, traceable results, and reconciliation with financial source systems.
  • SAC for FP and A: Lead solution architecture for budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, and management reporting, including operating expenses, capital expenditures, workforce costs, and integrated financial statements. Connect planning models with actuals and operational drivers.
  • Treasury: Lead solution architecture for cash and liquidity management, bank account management, payments and bank connectivity, cash forecasting, and treasury risk management. Ensure integration with financial accounting, banking platforms, and FP and A to support accurate cash visibility, treasury accounting, and financial controls.
  • Tax with ONE SOURCE: Own solution architecture and integration between SAP and Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE for indirect tax determination, calculation, and compliance reporting, including sales and use tax, VAT, and GST. title: Senior PDK Physical Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Shape the Future of Advanced Semiconductor Technology at Intel


Join Intel's Design Technology Platform (DTP) organization and become part of a world-class team enabling the next generation of semiconductor innovation. In this highly visible role, you will develop and deploy advanced density fill methodologies and Process Design Kit (PDK) solutions that directly impact Intel's most advanced technology nodes and product designs.


Working at the intersection of process technology, physical verification, and design automation, you will collaborate with leading engineers across Intel and the EDA ecosystem to solve complex manufacturability challenges, improve design productivity, and enable breakthrough technologies. Your contributions will influence how future products are designed and manufactured, helping Intel maintain technology leadership in an increasingly competitive industry.


What You'll Do

  • Lead the development, implementation, and validation of density fill solutions within advanced Process Design Kits (PDKs).
  • Develop algorithmic solutions using industry-leading physical verification platforms, including Calibre, Synopsys ICV, and Cadence Pegasus, to ensure density compliance and manufacturability across advanced process technologies.
  • Collaborate with process integration teams, design rule owners, product design engineers, and customers to define requirements and deliver state-of-the-art solutions.
  • Drive automation initiatives that improve engineering efficiency, solution scalability, and deployment across multiple design environments.
  • Design and develop robust validation frameworks, test suites, and qualification methodologies to ensure high-quality tool and rule deck releases.
  • Advance innovative physical verification methodologies to address emerging challenges associated with technology scaling.
  • Partner closely with external EDA vendors to influence and deploy next-generation tool capabilities and methodologies.
  • Develop technical documentation, training materials, and best practices that enable successful adoption across Intel's design community.
  • Serve as a technical expert and contribute to strategic initiatives that shape Intel's design enablement roadmap.

Ideal Candidate Background

We are particularly interested in candidates who have developed physical verification methodologies, density-fill solutions, or PDK technologies within:

  • Semiconductor Foundries.
  • Integrated Device Manufacturers (IDMs).
  • Advanced Packaging and OSAT Organizations.
  • EDA Software Companies.
  • Design Enablement or CAD Teams supporting advanced-node development.

Core Competencies

  • Excellent communication and technical presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable solutions.
  • Strong problem-solving, debugging, and analytical skills.
  • Strong understanding of technology scaling challenges and their impact on physical verification and design rule development.

Qualifications:

The Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.  Minimum qualifications listed below would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experience and / or schoolwork/classes/research. The preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field with 6+ years of relevant experience;
    • OR - Master's degree with 5+ years of experience.
    • OR - PhD with 2+ years of experience.
  • 4+ years of hands-on experience with at least one industry-standard physical verification platform such as Calibre, ICV, or Pegasus, including methodology development, rule deck debugging, validation, or production deployment.
  • 3+ years of experience developing, maintaining, or debugging physical verification rule decks using SVRF, TVF, PXL, PVL, or Tcl-based verification environments.
  • Experience with semiconductor process technology, device physics, design rules, and manufacturability requirements.
  • Experience developing algorithmic solutions for physical design and manufacturing challenges at advanced technology nodes.
  • Experience with with Unix/Linux operating systems and engineering computing environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 4+ years of direct experience developing, deploying, or supporting density fill methodologies for advanced semiconductor technologies at 16nm and below.
  • Proven expertise in fill rule implementation, density optimization, and manufacturing-driven design methodologies.
  • Deep experience with physical verification flows, including DRC, density analysis, fill verification, and process-aware design enablement.
  • Experience supporting or developing solutions for leading foundry, IDM, or advanced process technologies.
  • Familiarity with custom layout environments such as Cadence Virtuoso or Synopsys Custom Designer.
  • Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary engineering teams and external partners to deliver innovative solutions.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives, driving process improvements, or influencing product and methodology roadmaps.
  • Prior experience with semiconductor foundries, IDMs, OSATs, or EDA vendors developing physical verification methodologies, density-fill solutions, PDKs, or design-for-manufacturing technologies is highly desirable.

Why Intel?

This role offers a rare opportunity to work on technology challenges that influence the future of semiconductor manufacturing. You'll collaborate with experts across process technology, CAD, physical design, and EDA while helping define methodologies used across Intel's most advanced products. If you are passionate about solving complex physical verification and manufacturability problems at scale, this role offers both significant technical depth and broad organizational impact. Join Intel and make a direct impact on the next generation of semiconductor innovation.

At Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD), we have continued to extend Moore's law to be world leaders in computing technology. To achieve the necessary scaling of our semiconductor manufacturing process, we have led the industry in developing enhancements such as strained silicon for carrier transport enhancement, high-k metal gates, FinFETs, and next-generation Gate-All-Around architectures. LTD has been at the center of every new development that has kept Moore's Law moving forward.


Defect Metrology plays a key role in the development of every new silicon process technology. Our analysis builds the plan that allows LTD to take technology from the research phase to the high-volume manufacturing phase while maintaining high-quality standards. In the Manufacturing Integration Engineering (MIE) organization, we engineer world-class yields on advanced processes by driving defects down to Best-in-Class targets.


As a Defect Metrology Engineer, you will be responsible for identifying all defects that impact yield and performance in an advanced silicon process technology. You will characterize the process using cutting-edge metrology tools. With this characterization, you will be responsible for investigating the root cause owners and developing defect reduction roadmaps to achieve program milestone commitments to our customers. You will then work directly with the process modules and integration teams to drive that roadmap by developing and qualifying process fixes through Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS). You will also respond to defect baseline shifts to isolate the root cause and implement preventative actions consistent with 8D methodology. This role provides an opportunity to influence Intel's future process technologies that will keep Moore's Law moving forward.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Owning a segment of the process to ensure adequate metrology is placed to detect and respond to all yield-limiting defects prior to reaching end-of-line sort.
  • Investigate and respond to exclusionary baseline shifts to ensure segment defect health is restored to capable, demonstrated baseline.
  • Develop new recipes and RFCs as part of New Product Introduction (NPI).
  • Provide navigation and leadership to meet Intel's yield objectives, utilizing state-of-the-art metrology tools and test vehicles (QTM, Short Loop, etc.).
  • Organizing and presenting defect summaries to F25, LTD, MDCE engineering teams.
  • Partnering with Intel Integration, Yield, and failure analysis labs to provide root cause for all defect issues.
  • Hold the team and collaborators accountable for quality through Integrated Module Team (IMT) and Focus Team (FT) forums.
  • Work collaboratively as a part of the overall LTD Defect metrology group.
  • Role-model and establish a team culture of trust, collaboration, safety, accountability, and sustaining excellence.
  • Build strong relationships with other LTD teams based on mutual trust and respect.

The Ideal Candidate Must Demonstrate:

  • Strong data analysis and problem debug skills.
  • Team player with flexibility and adaptability to changing business needs.
  • Strong ownership mindset and driving closure-see the problem, own the problem.
  • Excellent communication and navigation skills to larger audiences.
  • Understand and adhere to Intel cultural values such as Customer First, Fearless Innovation, Results Driven, One Intel, Integrity, Quality, Inclusion.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research, and relevant previous job and internship experience.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Must possess a Master's degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Nuclear Engineering, Optics, Chemistry, or Computer Science.
  • Hands-on experimental research experience: designing and conducting experiments, operating laboratory equipment (characterization, fabrication, or synthesis), and analyzing statistical data.

Preferred qualifications:

Demonstrated academic research, coursework, laboratory, or internship experience with one or more of the following:

  • Materials characterization (SEM, TEM, AFM, etc.), materials fabrication, synthesis, metrology, statistical or data analysis (MATLAB, Excel, JMP, Python, etc.).
  • Semiconductor processing fundamentals (lithography, wet and/or dry etch, chemical mechanical polishing, thin films), semiconductor and/or transistor device physics, and Design of Experiments (DOE).
  • Defect metrology, defect inspection/improvement, yield analysis, or process integration.
  • Demonstrated application of Statistical Process Control (SPC) or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles.
  • Complex problem-solving methodologies: root cause analysis, Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS), 5 Why, Fishbone diagrams, or 8D frameworks.
  • Understanding of semiconductor physics or semiconductor processing cleanroom unit operations.
  • Understanding of defect metrology tools such as brightfield, darkfield, or voltage contrast (VC).

We welcome motivated professionals to bring their expertise and enthusiasm to Intel, where you will have the opportunity to grow your career while helping to shape the future of technology in a collaborative and forward-thinking environment. title: Memory Electrical Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, innovation starts with you. We are pushing the limits of silicon, AI, and edge-to-cloud architecture to power breakthrough technologies worldwide. Here, your skills will drive meaningful impact, solving real-world challenges and defining the next era of tech. Join our team and lead the future of engineering.
Join Intel's Memory Validation Team as a Memory Electrical Validation Engineer, where you will serve as a technical expert and lead validator for cutting-edge memory technologies embedded in mobile and desktop CPU products.
In this role, you will be responsible for leading the electrical validation strategy, signal integrity compliance, and system margin analysis for Intel's memory interfaces. You will drive complex post-silicon debug, refine Memory Reference Code (MRC) requirements, and collaborate closely with cross-functional design, architecture, and firmware teams to ensure robust product quality, high-volume production readiness, and optimal silicon performance.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Electrical Validation Strategy Execution
    Lead Validation Execution: Define, own, and execute comprehensive electrical validation (EV) test strategies and plans for high-speed memory I/O interfaces to achieve aggressive performance, quality, and production goals.
  • Signal Integrity /System Margin: Validate analog circuit performance, signal integrity compliance (SIV/SMV), and system-level electrical margins across temperature, voltage, and process corners to ensure stable operation.
  • Test Infrastructure / Automation: Design, execute, and continuously optimize validation procedures, specialized test automation frameworks, and system margin analysis tooling.
  • Post-Silicon Debug / Design Collaboration
    Complex Failure Triage: Drive deep-dive debug for electrical design features, identifying root causes for functional, parametric, and triage failures.
  • Lead DOEs: Formulate and execute multi-variable Design of Experiments (DOEs) in close collaboration with circuit design, logic, and pre-silicon teams to drive silicon issues to resolution.
  • I/O Interaction Testing: Characterize complex interactions between electrical design elements, board-level environments, and silicon features using post-silicon validation infrastructure.
  • Firmware Optimization/Cross-Functional Alignment
    MRC Analysis / Tuning: Analyze, refine, and optimize Memory Reference Code (MRC) steps, calibration values, and firmware algorithms for margin, power, and quality improvements.
  • Cross-Team Integration: Collaborate directly with architecture, circuit design, pre-silicon verification, and system integration teams to ensure robust validation coverage across the entire memory subsystem.
  • Technical Guidance: Provide technical direction and mentorship to junior validation engineers on validation methodologies and debug techniques.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
Education / Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 6+ years of industry experience, OR
  • Master's degree with 4+ years of industry experience, OR
  • PhD with 2+ years of industry experience.

Core Technical Experience (Must meet all):

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience in memory electrical validation, including Signal Integrity Validation (SIV) and Signal Margin Validation (SMV).
  • 4+ years of experience in analog/mixed-signal circuit fundamentals, electrical calibration methodologies, and post-silicon memory validation/debug processes.
  • Solid functional knowledge of Memory Reference Code (MRC) firmware execution paths, parameters, and debug flows for root-cause analysis.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience in high-speed mixed-signal IP electrical validation, high-speed I/O characterization, or signal integrity (SI/PI) analysis.
  • Deep domain experience with modern high-speed memory technologies (e.g., DDR5, LPDDR5/5X, LPDDR6) and JEDEC interface specifications.
  • Proven track record of leading complex root-cause debug investigations (DOEs) across multidisciplinary teams (Design, Logic, FW).
  • Proficiency with high-speed lab equipment (oscilloscopes, BERTs, logic analyzers) and scripting languages (Python, C/C++) for test automation and data analysis.

title: Intel Foundry/PCC Semiconductor Manufacturing Student Technician – ICE Program
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Why Intel Foundry? 

Every technological breakthrough starts with a spark of curiosity and hands-on determination. At Intel Foundry, we design, develop, and manufacture the cutting-edge semiconductor chips that power the world—from AI-driven supercomputers and autonomous vehicles to global cloud networks and everyday smart devices. 


As a Manufacturing Student Technician Intern, you won’t just read about semiconductor innovation, you will be inside one of the world’s most advanced cleanroom environments, operating multi-million-dollar toolsets and driving real-time wafer production. This 2-year part-time program is specifically designed for college students pursuing associate degrees, offering competitive pay, practical training, flexible scheduling around your classes, and an express ramp into high-tech manufacturing careers. 


What You Will Gain 

  • World-Class Cleanroom & Tool Experience: Develop hands-on operational and maintenance mastery over state-of-the-art semiconductor fabrication equipment. 
  • Direct Technical Mentorship: Collaborate alongside seasoned process engineers, module technicians, and factory leaders invested in your growth and success. 
  • Academic Flexibility & Total Rewards: Work compressed work-week shifts structured around your academic schedule, backed by industry-leading pay, performance bonuses, and benefits. 

Key Responsibilities & Day-to-Day Impact 

  • Drive Wafer Production & Operations: Oversee automated wafer fabrication and movement processes within the Oregon Fab network, maintaining strict adherence to quality benchmarks, output targets, and operational discipline. 
  • Hands-On Maintenance & Troubleshooting: Diagnose equipment anomalies, conduct preventative maintenance (PM), and utilize precision hand tools and diagnostic fixtures to maximize equipment availability and yield. 
  • Execute Technical Procedures: Interpret and execute instructions from comprehensive engineering drawings, schematics, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and technical specifications. 
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Deliver crisp, concise shift pass-downs to incoming teams and partner closely with module teams to sustain continuous factory flow. 
  • Uphold Safety & Cleanroom Standards: Serve as a safety champion by adhering strictly to fab safety protocols, chemical safety standards, and cleanroom contamination controls. 

Work Schedule & Program Structure 

  • Program Duration: 2-Year Cohort Internship Program. 
  • Term-Time Hours: 20 to 32 hours per week during active school terms. 
  • Break/Summer Hours: Up to 40 hours per week during academic breaks and summer sessions. 

Compressed Workweek (CWW) Shifts (12-Hour Day Schedules): 

  • Shift 5 (Day): Sunday through Tuesday (and alternating Wednesdays) | 7:30 AM – 8:00 PM 
  • Shift 7 (Day): Thursday through Saturday (and alternating Wednesdays) | 7:30 AM – 8:00 PM 
  • Additional schedule options available for AMHS Area
  • Shift8 (Day/Night) AMHS FH Sunday Through Tuesday (alternating Wednesday) | 12:00 PM – 00:00 AM  
  • Shift8 (Day/Night) AMHS BH Thursday Through Saturday (alternating Wednesday) | 12:00 PM – 00:00 AM    

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Relevant experience can be obtained through schoolwork, classes and project work, certifications, apprenticeships, internships, military training, and/or work experience.


Minimum Requirements:

  • Active Student Status: Currently enrolled in good standing at a locally accredited community college, trade school, or university pursuing an Associate’s degree in Microelectronics, Automation STEM, or applicable technical trade. 
  • Applicable fields include Microelectronics, Robotics, Electrical/Electronic Engineering Tech, Mechanical Technology, Automotive/Diesel Systems, Aviation Maintenance, HVAC, Machining, Life Safety Systems, Industrial Automation, Welding, and Precision Manufacturing.

title: Module Development Engineer (Ph.D.) - Intel Foundry
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Intel Logic Technology Development (LTD) designs and scales the advanced semiconductor process technologies that power future generations of Intel architecture.


As a Module Development Engineer, you will drive the development, optimization, characterization, and high-volume manufacturing (HVM) transfer of leading-edge semiconductor processes.

  • Patterning & Removal: Lithography, Overlay, Wet Etch, Dry/Plasma Etch, Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP).
  • Thin Films & Doping: Epitaxy (EPI), Thin-Film Deposition (ALD/CVD/PVD), Diffusion, Ion Implantation, Metals/Metallization, Dielectrics.
  • Metrology, Yield & Integration: In-line Metrology, FEOL/BEOL Process Integration, Defect Reduction, Yield Analysis, Electrical Characterization.

Key Responsibilities ("What You Will Do")

  • Process & Hardware Engineering: Design, execute, and optimize experimental runs to advance semiconductor processes, equipment hardware, and new material capabilities.
  • Process Control & Data Analytics: Apply statistical modeling, Design of Experiments (DOE), and control systems (SPC, APC, Run-to-Run) to reduce variability, mitigate defects, and drive yield enhancement.
  • Cross-Functional & Vendor Collaboration: Partner with external tool/material suppliers and internal integration teams to co-develop cutting-edge equipment and process methodologies.
  • HVM Technology Transfer: Resolve equipment, process, and yield excursion root causes to ensure smooth, robust technology transfer from development into high-volume manufacturing.
  • Documentation & Technical Reporting: Document experimental findings, operating procedures, and technical recommendations through engineering reports and presentations.

Qualifications:

Candidates must meet the following criteria (relevant experience may be gained through academic coursework, laboratory research, thesis work, internships, post doc, or publications):


Minimum Qualifications 

  • Education: Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Physics, Mechanical, Chemistry, or a related STEM field (expected completion prior to start date).
  • Hands-on Experience: 6+ months of experience with semiconductor fabrication, process development, device research, materials research, or related semiconductor technology, including one or more of the following: lithography (Litho)/overlay, epitaxy (EPI), wet etch, dry etch, thin-film deposition, diffusion, ion implantation, CMP/planarization, metals/metallization, dielectrics, metrology, process integration, yield, or electrical characterization. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Environment & Tooling: 6+ months in a cleanroom or semiconductor research lab working directly with fabrication or analytical instrumentation (e.g., ALD, CVD, PVD, plasma etch, CD-SEM, TEM, AFM, spectroscopic ellipsometry). 
  • Data Science & Automation: 6+ months utilizing statistical methodologies (DOE, SPC) and engineering software/scripting languages (Python, MATLAB, JMP, C#, or equivalents) for data analysis and automation. 
  • Device Physics & Integration: Academic or research specialization in transistor architecture, advanced semiconductor materials, or FEOL/BEOL process integration. 
  • Technical Dissemination: Proven track record of presenting technical findings through dissertations, peer-reviewed publications, conference proceedings, patents, or white papers.

title: Senior Manager, Data Center Portfolio & Demand Management
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Intel's Global IT organization is seeking a strategic and results-oriented leader to drive demand management, portfolio governance, and investment planning across Data Center and Infrastructure programs. This role leads a team responsible for evaluating technology demand, prioritizing investments, managing portfolio performance, and ensuring execution aligns with business and technology strategies.

As a senior leader, you will partner across business, engineering, infrastructure, operations, finance, and executive stakeholders to establish governance frameworks, optimize resource allocation, and provide visibility into portfolio health, risks, and outcomes. Success in this role requires strategic thinking, business acumen, strong leadership, and the ability to influence decisions across a complex global organization.

This position offers the opportunity to shape how infrastructure and data center investments are planned, prioritized, governed, and delivered to support Intel's long-term business objectives.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team responsible for demand management, portfolio governance, strategic planning, and investment prioritization.
  • Partner with business and technology leaders to evaluate demand, align priorities, and ensure investment decisions support organizational objectives.
  • Establish and continuously improve portfolio governance frameworks, prioritization processes, and executive decision-making mechanisms.
  • Oversee portfolio intake, resource planning, prioritization, and execution tracking across data center and infrastructure initiatives.
  • Provide executive-level reporting, portfolio insights, and actionable recommendations to support strategic business decisions.
  • Drive visibility into portfolio performance, investment outcomes, resource utilization, risks, dependencies, and capacity constraints.
  • Facilitate investment trade-off discussions and enable data-driven prioritization across competing business needs.
  • Build strong partnerships across infrastructure, cloud, engineering, operations, and finance organizations to ensure successful execution of strategic initiatives.
  • Lead process improvement efforts that increase efficiency, transparency, accountability, and operational excellence.
  • Foster an inclusive, collaborative culture focused on continuous improvement, innovation, and measurable business impact.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Strategic Mindset: Connects investments, priorities, and resources to long-term business objectives.
  • Executive Influence: Builds alignment and drives decisions across senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Business Acumen & Prioritization: Translates complex and ambiguous business needs into clear requirements, priorities, decisions, and accountable execution plans.
  • Executive Communication: Communicates effectively with executives and influences stakeholders across business, technology, facilities, finance, sourcing, and delivery organizations.
  • Results Orientation: Uses data to prioritize effectively, manage trade-offs, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
  • Change Leadership: Leads through ambiguity and drives organizational improvement and transformation.

title: Firewall Network Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.

Who we Are:
Intel's Information Security organization enables Intel to provide secure products, solutions, and services which meet U.S. regulatory requirements. The Information Security organization supports the unique IT information Security and Compliance requirements for Intel federal projects that deliver products and/or services to the US Government (USG). As part of this team, you will help us grow our secure solution suite to meet U.S. Government requirements.

The Intel Information Security organization is seeking a Firewall Network Security Engineer. The candidate chosen for this role will assist senior engineers with design, architecture, and build of secure classified network products to support USG operations.

Primary duties and Responsibilities:
• Assist with architecting network and network security products in secured enclaves, including product testing, validation, and selection.
• Assist with design and long-term roadmap planning for new and future scalability in secure enclaves.

Job Description:

As a Module Development Engineer within Intel's Advanced Packaging Technology Development (APTD) Metrology Group, you will contribute to the development, optimization, and implementation of advanced metrology capabilities supporting Intel's next-generation semiconductor packaging technologies.

Your work will combine hands-on equipment and process development, equipment qualification, manufacturing process optimization, and technology development initiatives. The APTD Metrology Group at Intel supports critical semiconductor technology development programs by enabling advanced measurement and inspection capabilities.

The group works closely with engineering, manufacturing, and technology development teams to introduce innovative measurement solutions and support Intel's next-generation semiconductor technologies.

title: SoC Validation Engineer – Power Management
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


The Role and Impact:
Intel is seeking a motivated and experienced SoC Validation Engineer to join our Power Management Validation team. In this role, you will be responsible for validating power management architectures and features that enable Intel's next-generation products. You will play a critical role in ensuring design quality, functionality, and power efficiency by developing innovative validation strategies, executing comprehensive test plans, and driving debug activities across complex SoC designs.

As a SoC Power Management Validation Engineer, you will work closely with architecture, design, and verification teams to validate key power management features including Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), power gating, clock gating, reset flows, low-power states, thermal management, and telemetry. You will contribute to the development of advanced validation environments, uncover design issues early in the development cycle, and drive solutions that improve product quality and readiness. This position offers an opportunity to influence future Intel products while expanding your technical leadership and validation expertise.

Business group:
You will be joining Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), a global leader in designing and delivering cutting-edge technologies that drive data center innovation and transformation. The group specializes in developing high-performance solutions to accelerate computing, storage, and networking capabilities, supporting Intel's mission to power the world's digital infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities:
- Develop and execute comprehensive validation plans to ensure power management features meet architectural and functional specifications.
- Design, develop, and maintain validation environments, automated test content, and debug infrastructure for power management validation.
- Validate critical power management features including: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), Power Gating and Clock Gating, Low-Power States and Power State Transitions, Reset and Power Sequencing, Thermal Management Features, Telemetry and Monitoring Logic.
- Develop validation content and infrastructure using industry-standard methodologies and tools such as SystemVerilog, UVM, simulation, and emulation platforms.
- Execute simulation and emulation workloads to validate design functionality and identify issues early in the product development cycle.
- Analyze validation results, coverage metrics, and performance data to improve design quality and validation effectiveness.
- Drive root cause analysis, debug, and resolution of complex design issues in collaboration with architecture, RTL design, and verification teams.
- Develop and maintain automation frameworks, regression environments, dashboards, and data analysis tools to improve validation efficiency and coverage.
- Review architecture specifications and design changes to assess validation impact and ensure comprehensive feature coverage.
- Contribute to validation methodology improvements and best practices across multiple product generations.
- Mentor junior engineers and provide technical leadership on complex validation and debug challenges.
- Continuously explore new technologies, automation techniques, and AI-assisted solutions to improve execution and outcomes.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your degree, research and or relevant previous job and or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications:
- Bachelors & 6+ years or Masters & 4+ years or PhD & 2+ years degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

- 10+ years of experience in pre-silicon validation, functional validation, design verification, or silicon validation.

- Strong understanding of digital design fundamentals, computer architecture, and SoC design concepts.

- Strong knowledge of SystemVerilog and UVM-based validation methodologies.

- Experience with simulation or emulation environments, debugging and root-cause analysis skills.

- Knowledge in Python or Perl or Shell, or similar scripting languages.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

- Experience validating power management architecture and features in complex SoC designs, such as: Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), Power Gating, Clock Gating, Low-Power State Management, Reset and Power Sequencing, Thermal Management Features.

- Experience developing validation plans, test content, and coverage-driven validation strategies.

- Experience in one or more of the following areas: Functional Validation, Design Verification, Coverage-Driven Verification, Emulation-Based Validation, Low-Power Verification Methodologies, Reset Validation, Power State Validation, Telemetry Feature Validation.

- Familiarity with assertion-based verification, formal verification, and advanced validation automation techniques.

- Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives and mentor engineers.

- Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively across architecture, design, and validation teams.

- Experience leveraging AI and advanced analytics to improve validation productivity and quality.

- Passion for innovation, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.

- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are seeking a transformative, results-driven leader to serve as Senior Director of Competitive and Solutions Marketing. You will architect and guide our centralized intelligence ecosystem, establishing an enterprise-wide source of truth for market conditions, competitive dynamics, growth opportunities, and market response. You will help shape the company's understanding of market opportunities, competition, emerging technology shifts, and investment priorities[WA4.1][RM4.2]. The role will deliver independent, fact-based market perspectives that influence enterprise planning, resource allocation, and strategic decision-making.

This is not a traditional reporting or analytics role. You will lead the evolution of market intelligence, shifting our capability from static, reactive dashboards to an AI-enabled strategic advisory and market response engine.
In this role, you will combine deep human judgment with AI capabilities. You will partner closely with IT to define the business architecture and product requirements for the intelligence system. You will also cultivate a collaborative Intelligence Community that breaks down information silos across departments. By using agentic tools for first-draft synthesis and continuous signal sensing, you will free the team to focus on strategic counsel, objective stress-testing of proposals, and faster, higher-value contributions to decisions across planning cycles.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead ongoing market and competitive analysis, including positioning, market sizing, forecasting, and emerging industry trends; clarify complex market shifts and identify forward-looking opportunities.

  • Define and lead Intel's vision for AI-enabled market intelligence, using agentic workflows, automated synthesis, predictive modeling, and decision-support systems to increase the speed, scale, and impact of intelligence across the enterprise. Partner with business stakeholders, IT, and external providers to define requirements.
  • Develop market responses that position and differentiate Intel's products and solutions. Establish simple mechanisms for sharing customer and partner feedback and equip teams to use AI to analyze information and communicate findings clearly.
  • Lead, mentor, and evolve a high-caliber team of data scientists and technical marketers, shifting traditional data-gathering and report-building roles toward higher-value strategic consulting, scenario modeling, and intelligence systems design.

Core Competencies

  • Systems Thinking: Ability to connect disparate macro, competitive, and customer signals into an integrated, actionable framework for corporate investment.
  • Intellectual Courage: Willingness to provide unvarnished, objective truth and actively challenge internal assumptions, even when they run counter to the prevailing consensus.
  • Collaborative Stewardship: High emotional intelligence (EQ) to champion a "One Intel" mindset, unifying siloed teams around common objectives and shared data assets.

  • Strategic AI and Product Acumen: Demonstrated experience serving as the business or product owner for data and AI initiatives, including defining functional requirements for automated data ingestion, NLP/LLM workflows, predictive models, or advanced analytics platforms.

Demonstrated success challenging conventional thinking and driving alignment among senior leaders in highly matrixed organizations and executive leadership
  • Cross-Functional Orchestration: Exceptional ability to build communities of practice, align matrixed stakeholders across diverse business units, and drive cross-functional consensus without formal hierarchical authority.
  • Independent Judgment: Demonstrated willingness to provide candid, fact -based perspectives that challenge prevailing assumptions and ensure decisions are grounded in market realities rather than organizational preferences.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

As a Module Engineer, you will play a critical role in optimizing high-volume manufacturing equipment and processes to enable the production of cutting-edge integrated circuits. Your daily responsibilities will involve conducting tests and measurements to ensure control over critical dimensions and defectivity, recommending process modifications to enhance efficiency and quality, and ensuring seamless technology transfer across global manufacturing sites. This position offers the opportunity to make a direct impact on Intel's semiconductor manufacturing leadership while fostering technical growth in a dynamic, innovative environment.


This is an onsite manufacturing role supporting a 24/7 factory environment. The position requires working on a rotating shift schedule, including day and night shifts, with weekly shift rotations to support continuous manufacturing operations and business needs.

Business Group
This role is part of Intel's Assembly and Test Manufacturing (ATM) organization, a key component of Intel's back-end manufacturing ecosystem. ATM supports Intel's diverse product portfolio, including client, automotive, server, and connectivity segments. The team focuses on delivering advanced packaging and testing solutions while driving manufacturing excellence and supporting global technology initiatives, aligning with Intel's IDM 2.0 strategy.

title: Server Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


The Role and Impact
As a CPU Architect, you will define, model, and drive the development of cutting-edge CPU architectures tailored to meet performance, power, frequency, and area targets across diverse applications, from high-performance computing to low-power devices. You will evaluate tradeoffs, innovate architectural solutions, and optimize designs to address future workload demands. Your contributions will shape Intel's advancements in CPU technology, influencing transformative innovation for the industry.

Business group
Intel's Data Center Group (DCG) focuses on delivering world-class solutions that power data-driven computing at scale. This group plays a crucial role in advancing Intel's capabilities, enabling breakthrough innovations in performance, scalability, and efficiency across diverse computing segments. By joining, you'll be part of a dynamic organization driving technology leadership and supporting Intel's broader mission to create world-changing advancements.

Key Responsibilities
- Define and document CPU architecture specifications to ensure modularity, scalability, and alignment with hardware and software requirements.
- Develop novel architectural solutions and features to achieve performance, power, and area optimization targets.
- Conduct feasibility studies and tradeoff analyses for CPU requirements and new instruction sets supporting emerging workloads.
- Model CPU performance and power, analyze bottlenecks, and propose architectural refinements based on workload predictions.

title: TD Memory Quality and Reliability PhD Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team 

The Technology Development (TD) Quality and Reliability organization plays a critical role in enabling the successful deployment of next-generation semiconductor technologies through silicon-based quality, reliability, and technology readiness assessments. 

The Memory Quality and Reliability team works closely with Design, Device Engineering, Product Development Engineering (PDE), and Yield organizations to develop, characterize, and certify SRAM, Register File (RF), and Fuse technologies for advanced process nodes. The team supports key technology certification and PDK release milestones through memory characterization, silicon data analysis, predictive modeling, and risk assessment. 

Role Overview 

As a TD Memory Quality and Reliability Intern, you will collaborate with experienced engineers to evaluate advanced memory technologies and help drive technology readiness for future Intel Foundry process nodes. This role offers hands-on experience in memory characterization, silicon data analytics, statistical modeling, and semiconductor technology development. 

You will contribute to projects that support technology certification decisions by analyzing silicon data, developing predictive models, and assessing memory performance across various operating conditions. 

Responsibilities 

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: 

  • Analyze silicon characterization data from SRAM, Register File (RF), and Fuse memory test structures to identify performance trends, variability, and potential risks. 
  • Support memory characterization activities across voltage, temperature, and process conditions. 
  • Perform data analysis, visualization, and reporting using Python, JMP, or similar analytical tools. 
  • Develop and enhance statistical models for Vmin/Vmax prediction and technology readiness assessments. 
  • Support Silicon-to-Simulation (Sil2Sim) correlation studies and memory characterization methodologies. 
  • Generate technical reports and contribute to technology certification reviews. 
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Design, Device Engineering, Process Integration, Product Development Engineering, and Yield Engineering. 
  • Assist with risk assessment activities and technology certification milestones. 
  • Present data-driven findings and recommendations to engineering teams and project stakeholders. 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications 

  • Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or a related field. 
  • Basic knowledge of semiconductor devices, microelectronics, or integrated circuit design. 
  • Programming or scripting experience using Python or similar languages. 
  • Experience analyzing technical, scientific, or research data through academic projects, research activities, or previous internships. 
  • Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher required.

Preferred Qualifications 

Coursework, research, or experience in one or more of the following areas: 

  • SRAM or memory technologies 
  • Semiconductor device physics 
  • VLSI design 
  • Statistics, machine learning, or data science 
  • Semiconductor process technology 

Experience with: 

  • Python, Pandas, and NumPy 
  • JMP or other statistical analysis tools 
  • Data visualization and statistical modeling techniques 
  • Large-scale data analysis and predictive modeling 

Additional experience in memory architectures, silicon characterization, reliability assessment, or semiconductor test methodologies is highly desirable. 

What You Will Learn 

During this internship, you will gain exposure to: 

  • Advanced SRAM, RF, and Fuse memory technologies 
  • Memory characterization and certification methodologies 
  • Silicon data analytics and statistical modeling techniques 
  • Vmin/Vmax evaluation and predictive model development 
  • Technology qualification and certification processes 
  • Cross-functional semiconductor technology development workflows 
  • Silicon-based decision making for technology readiness and risk assessment

title: CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Are you interested in building the next generation of high-performance, power-efficient CPUs?

Join Intel as a CPU Physical Design Engineer and begin your career working on advanced processor technology. In this early-career role, you will work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to the physical design and verification of CPU designs from RTL to GDSII.

You will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard EDA tools and develop expertise across physical design areas including synthesis, floorplanning, place and route, clock implementation, static timing analysis, power optimization, and physical verification.

As part of the CPU Physical Design team, you will collaborate with engineers across logic design, architecture, circuits, and design automation while developing the technical expertise required to solve increasingly complex CPU design challenges.

What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Implement physical design and verification flows for custom CPU designs, ranging from RTL synthesis to GDS generation, custom and memory designs.
  • Perform verification and signoff processes such as formal equivalence verification, layout verification, reliability verification, and timing/power integrity analysis.
  • Collaborate with logic, architecture, circuit, and design automation teams to identify opportunities for design improvements and optimize product-level parameters such as power, frequency, and area.
  • Build and refine physical design methodologies and automation workflows to streamline the design process.
  • Work closely with EDA vendors to enhance tool capabilities for high-speed, low-power CPU design.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Learning agility and curiosity: Eager to learn new technologies, tools, and CPU physical design methodologies.
  • Problem solving: Approaches technical challenges analytically and works through problems in a structured manner.

Job Description: 

This is an exceptionally exciting moment to enter the semiconductor manufacturing industry. Global demand for advanced computing-driven by AI, automation, cloud infrastructure, and digital transformation-is fueling the largest period of growth and reinvestment the sector has seen in decades. Semiconductors are now recognized as critical to economic resilience, national security, and technological leadership leading to unprecedented expansion in manufacturing capacity and innovation. For professionals in the field, this translates to rare opportunities to shape breakthrough technologies, contribute to globally significant projects, and be part of arguably the most rapidly evolving and impactful industry ever.


Intel's Global Construction Engineering (GCE) organization is responsible for the design and engineering of Intel's major manufacturing and cleanroom facilities worldwide. Our organization consists of highly specialized, in house architects and engineers working in a deeply collaborative environment. Together with our factory, operations, and supply chain partners, we deliver some of the most technically complex construction programs in the industry-projects that demand precision, speed, and disciplined cost management.
Our vision is to be the world leader in semiconductor foundry construction engineering, and we are expanding our team to support the acceleration of Intel Foundry's manufacturing roadmap. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet. Join Intel's Substrate Packaging Technology Development (SPTD) organization, a global leader in developing advanced substrate and packaging solutions. Our team is dedicated to enabling Intel's roadmap of innovative packaging technologies, focusing on materials development, process optimization and simulation, and process equipment advancements. SPTD supports Intel's mission of delivering high-performance, cost-effective products that power the future of computing.

We are seeking a Senior Packaging Module Development Engineer to join our team in Chandler, Arizona. In this role, you will play a key part in advancing Intel's IC substrate and packaging technologies. You will develop, optimize, and implement innovative processes, materials, and equipment configurations to enable next-generation packaging solutions. Combining physical experimentation with statistical data analytics and process modeling, your work will directly impact manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and reliability across Intel's advanced packaging portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Process & Material Optimization: Develop and refine packaging processes and materials to meet stringent quality, reliability, yield, and cost targets.
  • Workflow & Equipment Definition: Define and establish equipment configurations, process parameters, and integrated workflows for advanced IC substrate and packaging technologies.
  • Experimental Characterization (DOE): Design and execute experimental plans using Design of Experiments (DOE) principles to characterize process windows and analyze complex material and equipment interactions.
  • Data Analytics & Process Modeling: Apply statistical methods, deep data analytics, and engineering scripting tools to optimize manufacturing processes, drive material enhancements, and resolve IC substrate development challenges.
  • Continuous Improvement: Implement continuous process improvements to enhance tool stability, product quality, and manufacturing productivity.
  • Cross-Functional Problem Solving: Partner with cross-functional engineering, materials, and equipment teams to drive process development and root-cause troubleshooting initiatives.
  • Technical Documentation & Transfer: Author technical documentation, including white papers and process specifications, to enable seamless technology transfer and knowledge sharing across global teams.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Technical Leadership & Influence: Strong leadership skills to guide cross-functional engineering efforts and drive technical alignment across diverse teams.
  • Analytical Problem Solving: Deep analytical mindset with a passion for combining empirical data and theoretical modeling to solve complex materials and processing challenges.
  • Clear Technical Communication: Concise written and verbal communication style to author specifications, publish internal white papers, and present findings to stakeholders.
  • Adaptability & Ownership: Self-directed engineer who thrives in a dynamic R&D environment and takes full accountability for project milestones.

Apply today to join Intel Arizona's Substrate Packaging Technology Development team. Take ownership of next-generation materials and processes, collaborate with world-class scientists, and build a rewarding engineering career.

Intel is transforming its backend manufacturing network operations toward autonomous, lights-out manufacturing. title: Intel Mask Operations Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

The Role and Impact: As a Module Development Engineer within Intel's Mask Operations team, you will play a critical role in the development and production of photolithography masks for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Working onsite in a dynamic and collaborative environment, you will leverage your expertise to troubleshoot sophisticated manufacturing processes and equipment, optimize process stability, and drive innovation that supports Intel's cutting-edge silicon manufacturing solutions.

Business Group: Intel Mask Operations (IMO) is part of Intel's Logic Technology Development group, which is focused on pioneering advanced semiconductor technologies to deliver innovative manufacturing solutions. The team operates at the forefront of technology, ensuring the development and production of critical components that enable Intel's industry-leading products and position the company for continued growth in the semiconductor industry.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead process equipment installation, development, and optimization.
  • Perform equipment maintenance, troubleshoot technical issues, and manage defect analysis and reduction activities.
  • Drive improvements in quality, reliability, yield, cost, productivity, and safety/ergonomics.
  • Plan and conduct experiments to fully characterize processes throughout development cycles.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to resolve technical process and defect issues.
  • Establish control systems to optimize and sustain production performance.
  • Develop strategies to address complex problems and implement systems to prevent recurrence.
  • Stay updated on industry trends, contributing to roadmaps for future manufacturing technologies.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of relevant post-doc research and industry experience.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Candidate must possess a PhD degree in STEM related Science or Engineering fields
  • 5+ years of experience in advanced semiconductor or photomask manufacturing and process flow with strong hands-on equipment experience in process development and optimization.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Working knowledge of photolithography mask manufacturing and process technologies.
  • Proficiency in data analysis tools such as JMP or SQL.
  • Familiarity and experience with Statistical Process Control (SPC), Design of Experiments (DOE), and engineering analysis principles.
  • Experience photomask inspection, metrology and process equipment and in using scientific equipment, such as SEM or TEM, for materials and device characterization.
  • Advanced understanding of semiconductor processing fundamentals, such as lithography, etch, film deposition, and chemical-mechanical planarization.
  • Ability to construct clear, data-driven problem statements and solutions.

Join us in shaping the future of semiconductor technology through innovative engineering and cutting-edge advancements in manufacturing. Your contributions will drive impactful solutions that will transform industries and power the future.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization delivers the latest process technology innovations to drive Intel's amazing product roadmap. Look at Life Inside Intel here.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Intel is seeking an experienced Principal Engineer with deep expertise in lithography scanner technology and broad experience in logic technology development, enhancement, and customization. In this role, you will lead scanner technology development and improvement for high-volume manufacturing, with a focus on advancing scanner performance and enabling Intel’s next-generation process technologies.

title: Graduate Talent (CPU-SoC Silicon Design)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

In this position, you will be involving in the training, design and development of next generation SOC/CPU for wide range of Intel products. Your responsibilities will include some of the following but not limited to:

  • Assist design unit owner in Register Transfer Level RTL model functional validation. Use CAD tool extensively to simulate logic behavior and circuit performance and direction of physical design for next generation, deep sub-micron embedded circuit solutions. Verify the circuit behavior against the original simulation model and first silicon.
  • Define VLSI Structural Design methodology and developing design flows. Implement structural physical designs, such as synthesis, floor planning, power-grid and clock tree designs, timing budgeting and closure, place and route, RC-extraction and integration. Verify structural physical designs, such as functional equivalency, timing/performance, noise, layout design rules, reliability and power.
  • Develop Analog IP on next generation deep submicron process for the Intel's SOC, perform tasks related to Very-large-scale integration VLSI complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor CMOS IC design, Solid state physics and physical layout. Such tasks may include: Circuit design of high speed clocking related circuits [phase-locked loop PLL, delay-locked loop DLL, bandgap] or high voltage input/output IO [double data rate DDR/LPDDR, General-purpose input/output GPIO, OPIO].
  • Responsible for Integration of Third party IPs -- Synthesis, functional and/or timing convergence, and pre and post-si debug of IPs developed by various external vendors as well as within the company. Handling of signals crossing power planes and clock domains, industry standard protocols including hardware and software details dealing with Memory LPDDR, storage eMMC, SATA, UFS, peripherals PCIe, USB, and MIPI interfaces in SOC devices. System integration dealing with Si/ Platform/ FW/ MW/ drivers/ OS/ Apps on Android Windows-based tablets and phones.

Qualifications:

You must possess a Bachelor of Engineering degree or a Master of Science degree in Electronic, Electrical or Computer Engineering.

Additional qualifications include:

  • Familiarity with Very Large Scale Integration VLSI Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor CMOS logic circuit design
  • Well versed in UNIX, C programming and relevant Computer Aided Design CAD tools.

title: GPU Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As a GPU Validation Engineer, you will play a critical role in ensuring the functional accuracy, performance, and reliability of Intel's cutting-edge GPUs. You will define, develop, and execute robust validation methodologies to test interactions between GPU features across hardware and software layers. Your work will directly impact the quality and performance of Intel GPUs, enabling seamless integration into diverse systems and driving innovation in graphics and compute technologies.

Business group :
You will be part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), which leads the development of technologies that power the world's data-centric infrastructure. This group focuses on shaping the future of cloud computing, AI, and high-performance computing by delivering solutions that advance Intel's leadership in data processing and connectivity. Joining DCG offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking products that support Intel's broader mission of enabling global progress through technology.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute functional validation plans for GPUs, ensuring comprehensive test coverage across hardware and software components.
  • Analyze and debug silicon issues to identify root causes, resolve failures, and optimize GPU designs.
  • Test and validate system-level interactions between GPU features using advanced validation infrastructure.
  • Collaborate with architecture, design, verification, and manufacturing teams to refine validation methodologies and processes.
  • Review proposed design changes to assess their impact on validation timelines, tasks, and performance goals.
  • Design and implement post-silicon validation infrastructure, including behavioral checkers, performance monitors, and coverage tools.
  • Publish detailed validation reports summarizing key findings, results, and recommendations.
  • Maintain and improve validation strategies to support product specifications and enhance overall GPU functionality.
  • Defines, develops, and performs functional validation for GPUs, focusing on validation of interaction of GPUs, media, display and system level features. Applies various hardware and software level tools and techniques to ensure validation coverage and that performance, power, and area goals are met.
  • Reviews proposed design changes to assess impact on validation plans, tasks, and timelines.
  • Develops GPU validation methodologies, executes validation plans, and collaborates with other engineers for design optimization, troubleshooting, and failure analysis.
  • Performs silicon debug to identify root causes and resolves all functional and triage failures for GPU issues. Tests interactions between various GPU features using validation infrastructure.
  • Develops post silicon validation infrastructure (e.g., performance monitors, behavioral checkers, state space coverage) and test environment used in validation testing.
  • Publishes GPU validation reports summarizing all validation activities performed, reviews results, and communicates to relevant teams.
  • Works with architecture, design, verification, board, platform, and manufacturing teams to maintain and improve debug, validation test strategy, methodologies, and processes for graphics interfaces and to meet desired product specifications.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field and 9+ years of experience, or a Master's degree with 6+ years, or a Ph.D. with 4+ years working in GPU validation, silicon debugging, or related domains.
  • Proficiency in validation tools and techniques, including hardware validation infrastructure and software-based testing methodologies.
  • Experience with silicon debug processes, triage failure analysis, and system-level validation.
  • Strong technical expertise in GPU architecture, media, and display technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute validation plans aligned with design and performance goals.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Proven experience collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams to drive design optimizations and resolve technical challenges.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a focus on continuous improvement in validation processes.
  • Effective communication skills to present findings and recommendations through clear and concise reports.
  • Passion for innovation and a proactive mindset to contribute to advancements in GPU technologies.
  • Proven experience in platform validation, low power flow management, memory expertise and ( GDDR/LPDDR ) debugging, and test content development, with a focus on reset/boot/low power functionalities.
  • Strong understanding of server architectures, hardware components, and operating systems.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python) for test automation, debugging, and test content development.
  • Experience with validation, debugging, and test content development tools and frameworks (e.g., Jenkins, GDB, WinDbg).
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git) and issue tracking tools (e.g., JIRA).
  • Knowledge of industry standards and best practices related to server reset, platform validation, debugging, and test content development.

Your work will help define the future of graphics processing technology, creating opportunities to grow, develop, and make a lasting impact through meaningful contributions to Intel's product excellence and innovation.

title: APCC Shift Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Advanced Packaging Command Center (APCC) Shift Group Leader is a people manager responsible for leading a shift-based operations team that provides remote manufacturing and technical support to factory operations. This role ensures safe, reliable, disciplined and consistent execution of APCC services while maintaining strong partnership with supported factory teams and global stakeholders. The Shift Group Leader is accountable for people leadership, shift execution, operational performance, service quality, escalation management, capability development and continuous improvement. The role requires sound decision-making in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where priorities change rapidly, supported by a solid understanding of the semiconductor manufacturing flow to lead defect-related operational response and drive cross-functional problem solving across APCC and supported factories. Key Responsibilities People and Shift Leadership - Lead, supervise and develop APCC Technicians, Commanders and Runners supporting remote factory operations across assigned sites, technologies and service areas. - Own core people-management responsibilities, including onboarding, goal setting, performance management, recognition and handling of employee relations matters. - Ensure effective 24/7 shift operations, including staffing, attendance, overtime management, workload balancing, shift coverage and task prioritization. - Provide clear leadership and direction during rapidly changing manufacturing situations, balancing operational priorities, technical risk and service commitments. - Ensure team members complete required training and certification (e.g., L1O/L2O) and that training materials remain current with the latest specs and processes. - Build team capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, technical development and disciplined execution of standard work. - Establish an environment of safety, accountability, teamwork, continuous learning and effective cross-functional collaboration. Operational Execution and Escalation Management - Ensure timely response, acknowledgement, disposition and escalation of manufacturing or technical events in accordance with established procedures and service expectations. - Enforce compliance with the operating spec, escalation timelines and follow-up expectations. - Coordinate work across APCC, factory operations, engineering, equipment, automation, manufacturing and other stakeholder organizations, including global sites across time zones, to ensure issues are properly owned and resolved. - Serve as the primary shift leadership escalation point for operational abnormalities, high-impact events, staffing constraints, service disruptions and issues requiring management intervention. - Maintain effective shift-to-shift handover, ensuring significant events, open actions, risks and escalation status are clearly communicated. - Provide shift reports and operations review inputs and communicate significant events to management and site stakeholders. - Ensure compliance with EHS, information security, access control and data integrity requirements. Technical Leadership - Provide shift leadership for quality/Yield-related manufacturing events, ensuring appropriate initial assessment, containment, escalation, ownership and follow-through in partnership with manufacturing, process, yield, quality and engineering teams. - Apply knowledge of the semiconductor manufacturing flow to understand how upstream process conditions in wafer fabrication, wafer-level packaging and sort/test may appear as downstream defect or yield signals. - Use problem solving methodology and technical data to guide problem definition, challenge defect classification and disposition where needed, and route issues to the appropriate engineering owners. - Distinguish immediate operational containment needs from issues requiring deeper engineering investigation,and ensure repeat or systematic defects have clear ownership for root cause, corrective action and follow-up. Operational Performance and Continuous Improvement - Monitor operational data, KPIs, dashboards and trends to identify execution gaps, recurring issues and improvement opportunities. - Drive disciplined adoption of standard work, operational governance and continuous-improvement practices. - Partner with technical and operational stakeholders to improve execution consistency, responsiveness and service quality. - Ensure lessons learnt from manufacturing events, defect excursions and operational gaps are incorporated into team capability development and standard work where appropriate. - Drive follow-through on recurring operational or technical issues until sustainable corrective actions and ownership are established.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Science or a related technical discipline. - 3+ years of experience as a people manager, shift leader or team leader of a factory/technical team of five or more employees, with responsibility for technical or operational deliverables. - Understanding of the end-to-end semiconductor manufacturing flow, with working knowledge of at least one of the following: wafer fabrication, wafer-level packaging or sort/test. - Ability to understand technical data and use it to support problem definition, operational decision-making and appropriate engineering escalation. - Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple priorities, managing escalations and delivering results in a time-sensitive operating environment. - Demonstrated ability to coach and develop team members and to make sound decisions under pressure. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including with global stakeholders and senior leaders. - Strong interpersonal skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively in a diverse and cross-functional team environment. - Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous situations and maintain commitment to operational deliverables. - Willingness and ability to work in a compressed work week and shift-based operating model, including coordination with stakeholders across time zones. Preferred Qualifications - 6+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, engineering, operations or technical support, including 3+ years leading teams. - Proven track record leading a team in a 24/7 high-volume manufacturing, command center, remote operations or factory support environment. - Working knowledge of semiconductor defect methodology and the ability to relate process conditions, defect signals and yield/quality excursions across the manufacturing flow. - Hands-on or leadership experience with wafer fabrication, wafer-level packaging and/or sort/test manufacturing operations. - Experience supporting semiconductor defect, yield or quality excursions. - Experience interpreting defect maps/images, defect Pareto/trend information, process data and equipment signals to support defect investigation and escalation. - Knowledge of structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, root-cause analysis, containment and corrective/preventive action. - Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, equipment support, process control, operational escalation and factory execution systems. - Knowledge of, or demonstrated aptitude for learning, manufacturing systems, automation platforms, dashboards and operational tools. - Experience using operational data, KPIs, dashboards and trend analysis to drive performance improvements. - Experience implementing standard work, operational governance, continuous improvement or quality management practices. - Experience collaborating across process, yield, equipment, manufacturing and quality engineering organizations to resolve complex manufacturing issues. We invite you to bring your experience and leadership skills to Intel and join us in driving innovation, optimizing operations, and empowering our teams to achieve their full potential.
