title: Senior Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

We are seeking a full-time Senior Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineer to play a pivotal role in our high-volume fabrication facility. In this position, you will provide tactical and strategic operational support to ensure the successful development and ramp of a high-volume or technology development fabrication facility. Define and drive the development and implementation of manufacturing decision-support tools and methodologies and maintain standards for operation sequences and processes. Analyze key factory metrics and drive improvements while providing direction that will improve overall factory performance. Develop, enhance and troubleshoot factory reporting systems and work with automation groups to develop business systems and processes that monitor factory performance. Your expertise will directly contribute to sustaining production activities, improving manufacturing systems and reports, and delivering high-quality outputs that meet customer and business needs.

Business group

As part of New Mexico's Wafer Packaging Production Department, you will join a collaborative team dedicated to advancing semiconductor manufacturing. The organization focuses on optimizing factory operations and supporting Intel's broader objectives in delivering innovative technologies. Working within this group, you will help shape manufacturing strategies to drive efficiency and support Intel's leadership in the semiconductor industry.

Key Responsibilities

- Provide tactical and strategic operational support for high-volume fab development, ramp, and sustaining activities as a senior production engineer, ensuring manufacturing readiness across the full product lifecycle including New Product Introduction (NPI) builds.

- Define and drive global manufacturing decision-support tools, methodologies, and standards for multiple processes and products, partnering with the Decision Support Team to design and develop linear optimization models that reduce changeovers, optimize output, and improve cycle time.

- Analyze current manufacturing and business processes to identify improvement opportunities, set operations targets, and drive data-driven decisions that optimize output, reduce cost, improve cycle time, and enhance overall factory performance and efficiency.

- Develop, enhance, and troubleshoot factory reporting systems and dashboards to provide real-time visibility into factory health, capacity, and performance metrics.

- Collaborate with the Industrial Engineering department to evaluate and align factory capacity and equipment availability against current and future product demand, proactively surfacing bottlenecks and capacity gaps to ensure 100 percent on-time delivery, customer commitment attainment, and cycle time target achievement.

- Own end-to-end lot-level customer order management within the production line, applying structured foundry prioritization methods to proactively detect delivery risks, drive timely corrective actions, and consistently achieve on-time customer commit attainment ahead of due dates while balancing competing priorities across multiple customer product lines simultaneously.

- Collaborate with global foundry operations, planning teams, and business partners to solve problems impacting factory operations, capacity, and factory health driven by enterprise planning and scheduling systems.

- Drive continuous process improvements by partnering with the production and Industrial Engineering departments to optimize foundry operations, eliminate flow disruptions, and ensure all products move through the line without delays.

- Define and drive requirements for manufacturing automation systems supporting key product roadmaps to deliver 100 percent of sales orders on time.

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:

·       Strong communication and leadership skills with the ability to translate complex manufacturing challenges into clear operational actions, manage customer-facing delivery commitments, and influence cross-functional teams at all levels of the organization.

This role requires on-site presence to fulfill essential job responsibilities.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline with 4+ years of relevant experience; OR
  • Master’s degree in one of the above fields or a related engineering discipline with 3+ years of relevant experience; OR
  • PhD in one of the above fields or a related engineering discipline with 1+ years of relevant experience.

Relevant experience should include a combination of the following:

  • Semiconductor manufacturing, foundry operations, production management, or a related technical environment.
  • Cross-functional collaboration with operations, industrial engineering, and production planning teams within a semiconductor fab or foundry environment.

This position is not eligible for Intel Immigration Sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting manufacturing operations, factory analytics, or decision-support systems in a high-volume semiconductor production environment
  • Demonstrated ability to solve complex multi-product optimization problems, analyze data, identify root causes using model-based problem solving, and drive corrective actions in a semiconductor manufacturing environment.
  • Experience managing customer sales orders and tracking lot-level production in a multi-customer foundry environment, with a proven ability to proactively identify delivery risks and drive corrective actions to meet customer delivery commitments.
  • 10+ years of experience in semiconductor foundry operations, high-volume fab manufacturing, or production engineering in a wafer fabrication or advanced packaging environment.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of Factory Physics principles and manufacturing science fundamentals, including variability management, Little's Law, WIP optimization, and capacity modeling, with a proven track record of applying these concepts hands-on to drive measurable improvements in cycle time, output, and factory utilization in a high-volume semiconductor or foundry environment.
  • Proven track record of bringing structured foundry methodologies to high-volume manufacturing environments, including lot-level order management, customer commit tracking, WIP prioritization, and multi-customer scheduling in a shared fab environment.

Apply today and become an integral part of our mission to lead in semiconductor innovation while driving scalable, world-class manufacturing solutions.

title: Packaging Module Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is a global technology pioneer, designing and manufacturing the crucial silicon foundations that power the world’s digital infrastructure. You will join Intel's highly collaborative Advanced Packaging and Assembly team—a critical group focused on driving breakthrough packaging innovations. Our mission is to enhance production efficiency, optimize next-generation assembly processes, and deliver world-class semiconductor packaging solutions to customers globally.


We are seeking a detail-oriented and collaborative Packaging Module Engineering Technician to support advanced packaging technology development in Arizona. Operating in a state-of-the-art laboratory environment, this fully on-site role focuses on preparing samples, running analytical testing, and evaluating materials. You will work side-by-side with research engineers to generate high-quality analytical data that directly influences semiconductor process optimization, quality control, and failure analysis.

Key Responsibilities:

• Perform materials characterization and analysis using microscopy, imaging, acoustic inspection, and other analytical techniques.
• Prepare samples and coupons for testing through cross-sectioning, polishing, etching, ion milling, spin coating, and related preparation methods.
• Operate characterization and test equipment including SEM/EDS, CSAM/TSAM, optical microscopy, elemental analysis, and mechanical testing systems.
• Support material evaluations, process development activities, and failure analysis investigations.
• Collect, analyze, document, and communicate characterization results and technical findings.
• Maintain laboratory equipment through routine maintenance, calibration, and basic troubleshooting.
• Ensure compliance with laboratory safety, quality, and documentation standards.
• Collaborate with engineers and cross-functional teams to execute experiments and deliver timely analytical support.
• Perform chemical handling, wet processing, and experiments in accordance with laboratory safety protocols and environmental health and safety (EHS) requirements.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Analytical & Solution-Oriented: A natural curiosity and logical approach to resolving nonstandard process, testing, and equipment issues.
  • Collaborative Communicator: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to work effectively with cross-functional engineering and research teams.
  • Rigorous Attention to Detail: Outstanding precision, organization, and a steadfast commitment to laboratory quality and safety protocols.
  • Growth Mindset: An eagerness to master new characterization techniques and adapt to innovative semiconductor technologies.

Are you ready to accelerate your career at the forefront of semiconductor R&D and packaging innovation? Apply today to join Intel's Advanced Packaging team in Chandler, Arizona!

title: WPM Integration: Defect Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Wafer Packaging Manufacturing organization is a global team at the heart of Intel's advanced packaging technology and high-volume manufacturing. Our vision is clear: optimize advanced packaging HVM processes end-to-end to maximize yield, quality, and customer satisfaction. WPM spans a broad and critical portfolio - including EMIB and Foveros wafer processing, TSV reveal, C4 bumping, Die Prep, and Wafer Level Assembly - supporting Intel's most strategic technologies across multiple sites worldwide

As a WPM Advanced Packaging Defect Reduction Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in protecting yield and elevating defect performance across some of the world's most advanced semiconductor packaging processes. Partnering with module engineering, QNR, manufacturing operations, and yield teams across our global network, you will bring together HVM manufacturing expertise with the technical rigor of a development organization to deliver impactful, lasting solutions. At WPM, we are more than a team - we are an organization that learns, grows, and succeeds and fails together, fostering a culture of trust, continuous improvement, and shared accountability where every individual's contribution drives our collective success.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own assigned advanced packaging layer(s), ensuring all POR defect inspection, classification, and review operations are properly established with healthy inspection recipes and NPI procedures defined.
  • Drive ADC implementation to ensure accurate defect classifications and maintain defect classification specs and Defect Menagerie for all assigned layers.
  • Partner with metro tool owners to set up and maintain SPC charts for every defect mode and layer, create OCAPs for Metro MTs and module engineering to respond to OOC events and defect tracers.
  • Own process health and product quality for the WPM manufacturing line, including defect performance, yield trends, excursions, and baseline process changes.
  • Own defect excursions through resolution, including containment, wafer/lot risk assessment, disposition, root cause, downstream impact, quality events, and non-POR material.
  •  Drive systematic defect reduction and process improvement using process/metrology data, SORT data, DOEs, FRECLs, ATVs, and experiments with process modules.
  • Co-lead cross-functional defect health reviews, including IMTs, Focus Teams, and Task Forces covering tracers, trends, OOCs, wafers-at-risk, excursions, and corrective actions.
  •  Extract, analyze, and correlate data to improve defects, yields, and VF matching, identifying key toolsets driving defects through analysis, MBPS, and FA.
  • Quantify chronic defect gaps to goal, document roadmaps to close gaps, and ensure defect health dashboards are operational and incorporated into factory business processes.
  • Communicate defect metrics and findings to module and factory stakeholders through weekly summaries and strategic quarterly reviews, while providing defect training to technicians, peers, and module teams.

Behavioral traits:

  • Proven ability to lead problem-solving initiatives and process improvement projects.
  • Exceptional communication skills for effectively collaborating across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Passion for mentoring and fostering technical growth within teams.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum qualifications and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.  This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related field and 3+ years of experience OR Master's degree in engineering or a related field and 2+ years of experience OR PhD in engineering or a related field with no prior professional experience.
  • Experienced mentioned above should be a combination of the following areas:
    • Data extraction, synthesis, and analysis using tools such as SQL and Python.
    • Technology transfer and new product introduction (NPI) activities in semiconductor manufacturing.
    • Expertise in failure analysis and data mining techniques to identify trends and drive actionable improvements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong understanding of semiconductor process flow, equipment, and process characterization techniques.
  • Experience with design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control (SPC), and process capability analysis.

We are looking for motivated individuals eager to make a meaningful impact in shaping Intel's manufacturing leadership. If you are excited about driving innovation and delivering groundbreaking solutions, we encourage you to take the next step and join our team.

title: Senior Design Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

Intel is building something new. The Unified Intel Chassis (UIC) team is a new IP development team focused on chassis and interconnect technology and a configurable generator for SoCs and chiplets. As a Senior Design Verification Engineer, you will verify coherent, non-coherent, and I/O-coherent systems — including interactions among interconnects, caches, memory subsystems, and chassis functions such as clocking, power management, reset, debug, and trace.

This is a hands-on technical role spanning the full verification lifecycle: from clarifying requirements and building models and checkers through debugging and verification signoff. You will work closely with engineers across architecture, design, verification, and tooling to turn specifications into working, tested hardware. Simulation, formal verification, and AI-assisted development are part of how we work.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own verification plans for chassis and interconnect IP, prioritize functional and integration risks, and drive assigned features from initial bring-up through signoff
  • Build reusable environments, reference models, and checkers for data integrity, ordering, address translation, access permissions, interrupt routing and delivery, and forward progress under concurrent traffic and backpressure
  • Combine simulation, formal properties, and targeted experiments to find bugs; review assumptions, checker completeness, coverage gaps, and proof results rather than relying on passing regressions alone
  • Collaborate with design and verification engineers to define interface contracts, share VIP and assertions, and debug interactions across data paths, clock and power transitions, reset sequences, and debug and trace functions
  • Work with architecture, design, and tooling engineers to clarify specifications, evaluate tradeoffs, and contribute reviewed changes to models, RTL, and verification infrastructure
  • Develop configuration-driven regressions and AI-assisted workflows for coding, property development, and debug; validate generated work with independent checks and reproducible tests across supported configurations
  • Mentor engineers through code and testplan reviews, communicate remaining risks, and establish clear evidence for verification closure

What We're Looking For

You should demonstrate the following professional traits to be successful:

  • Demonstrated ownership of complex verification work through closure, including cross-block root-cause analysis and clear technical communication across engineering disciplines
  • A collaborative approach to working across architecture, design, and verification teams to define requirements, resolve ambiguity, and drive toward shared goals
  • A rigorous, evidence-driven mindset — one that questions assumptions, validates generated work independently, and communicates risk clearly rather than relying on surface-level indicators of completeness

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • BS/MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field with 10+ years of relevant experience in design verification; background in IP DV with significant experience in subsystem and SoC-level verification

The experience must include:

  • Hands-on experience verifying high-performance interconnects and memory subsystems, with an understanding of coherent, non-coherent, and I/O-coherent operation, cache coherency, memory consistency, transaction ordering, virtual memory, I/O Memory management units (IOMMUs), and interrupt controllers; experience with MESI/MOESI-based coherency mechanisms and protocols such as AMBA CHI, CXL, or comparable architectures
  • SystemVerilog/UVM and assertion-based verification skills, with practical experience applying formal verification alongside simulation and understanding the limits of each method
  • Programming and debugging skills in SystemVerilog and Python or C/C++; ability to read RTL, build independent reference models and checkers, and develop maintainable test automation

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with configurable interconnect generators, generated testbenches, and verification across topology, parameter, and multi-die configurations
  • Experience with formal abstraction and proof decomposition, or emulation-based validation of system workloads
  • Experience verifying clocking, power management, reset, debug, trace, RAS, security isolation, or QoS interactions at subsystem level
  • Knowledge of cache hierarchies, home nodes, duplicate-tag structures, snoop filters, memory controllers, and how their interactions affect correctness and performance
  • Experience building and evaluating AI-assisted engineering workflows, including checks for incorrect generated code, properties, or specification interpretations

title: Design Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team

Intel is building a configurable interconnect and chassis generator for SoCs and chiplets, and the Unified Intel Chassis (UIC) team is looking for an Entry Level Design Verification Engineer to be part of it. In this role, you will use simulation, formal verification, and AI-assisted development to check hardware behavior, find bugs, and build reusable verification code.

Working closely with architecture, design, and tooling engineers, you will help turn specifications into working, tested hardware. We value strong fundamentals, curiosity, and engineers who follow a problem through to a solution. You will learn by building, testing ideas, and reviewing work with experienced engineers — with room to contribute to models, RTL, and tools as your skills grow.

Prior industry experience is not required. Relevant experience may come from coursework, research, internships, or personal projects.

Please note: This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop simulation tests, formal properties, reference models, and checkers for interconnect and chassis IP; learn to select and combine methods for the problem being verified
  • Debug simulation failures and formal counterexamples, distinguish design issues from testbench or assumption errors, and work with the relevant owners to resolve them
  • Translate specifications into verification plans and checks; review assumptions, coverage gaps, and proof results with the team, and take well-scoped features from initial bring-up through verification closure

  • Build scripts and reusable tools for configuration generation, regression execution, and results analysis across generated designs

What We're Looking For

You should demonstrate the following professional traits to be successful:

  • Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to ask questions, incorporate feedback, and learn unfamiliar hardware and software concepts
  • A methodical approach to problem-solving — one that distinguishes between what is expected, what is observed, and what needs to be investigated further
  • A collaborative mindset with the ability to communicate clearly and work effectively with engineers across architecture, design, and verification disciplines

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field — with 6+ months of work or academic experience
  • Foundation in digital logic, sequential circuits, and computer architecture, with the ability to read and reason about RTL
  • Programming and algorithmic problem-solving skills, demonstrated in C/C++, Python, or an HDL through coursework, research, projects, or internships
  • Experience explaining expected behavior, devise tests, and investigate unexpected results
  • Hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools in coursework, research, or projects, including reviewing and testing the code they produce

All minimum qualifications may be satisfied through internships, academic projects, coursework, or other practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Coursework or project experience with RTL simulation, formal verification, SystemVerilog assertions, or UVM
  • Familiarity with interconnects, cache and memory hierarchies, or protocols such as AXI, CHI, or PCIe
  • Hands-on projects involving RTL design, FPGA implementation, hardware modeling, or hardware-software co-design
  • Experience with Linux, Git, scripting, and automated build or test flows
  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows for specification analysis, test or property generation, or debugging

Preferred qualifications may also be satisfied through internships, academic projects, coursework, or other practical experience.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description: 

About the Team

The Hard IP Development Group (HIPD) within Intel's Central Engineering Organization is responsible for developing leadership IPs that are power-winning products for Server, Client, and Networking SOCs, as well as Intel Foundry Customers. HIPD develops a broad portfolio of Serial and Parallel IO PHYs including PCIe, USB, TypeC, UCIe Die-to-Die, DDR/LPDDR, and Ethernet PHYs.

The Electrical Validation and Debug group within HIPD is a dynamic and versatile team of engineers who directly engage with both IP design teams and SOC customers in IP validation and debug for test chips and products. This position is exciting and challenging, offering the opportunity to exercise your mixed signal design, architecture, and post-silicon debug expertise across all HIPD IPs, Client, and Server SOC teams.

Position Overview

This role focuses on mixed signal high-speed PHY post-silicon validation and debug, spanning IP enabling, customer sighting resolution, and cross-functional collaboration with SOC teams.

Key Responsibilities

title: SOC Functional Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:


As a SoC Functional Validation Engineer, you will play an integral role in ensuring the quality and reliability of Intel's state-of-the-art System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions. In this position, you will define, develop, and execute validation plans for integrated SoCs, focusing on post-silicon validation, debugging, and optimization. Through collaboration with cross-functional teams, your contributions will directly impact the performance and functionality of Intel products, driving innovation and excellence in the industry.

Business Group:


The Data Center Group (DCG) is at the forefront of developing cutting-edge technologies that enable high-performance computing and data-driven solutions. DCG focuses on creating advanced products and systems that power cloud, enterprise, and AI applications. By joining our team, you will contribute to Intel's broader mission of providing world-class solutions that shape the future of technology and computing.

Key Responsibilities:


- Develop and execute post-silicon validation plans to ensure compliance with design specifications and requirements.
- Perform functional validation for integrated SoCs, focusing on IP integration, system-level features, and interaction between components.
- Collaborate with architects, RTL designers, firmware teams, and other engineering groups to understand system-level requirements and features.
- Design and implement directed and random test cases to validate hardware/software interactions and ensure functional coverage closure.
- Debug SoC failures, identify root causes, and implement solutions or workarounds as required.
- Utilize tools such as Python, C, or C++ for test development and automation scripting.
- Analyze and modify test results, adapt test codes, and address coverage gaps to improve validation accuracy.
- Prepare and track validation requirements in collaboration with firmware, hardware, and platform teams.
- Develop and optimize validation methodologies, tools, and automation frameworks to streamline testing processes.
- Participate in project meetings, provide regular status updates, and escalate critical issues to management and stakeholders.
- Contribute to the development of new validation tools and methodologies, offering feedback and technical inputs for improvement.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:


- Bachelor's degree in Electronics, Electrical, or Computer Engineering, or related field, with 0-1 years of relevant experience in validation, test development, or debugging. Alternatively, a Master's degree in the relevant field with no prior professional experience.
- Proficiency in Python, C, or C++ for test content creation and automation scripting.
- Strong understanding of computer architecture, microarchitecture, and operating system concepts.
- Experience with pre-silicon platforms such as emulators or Virtual Prototypes for test code development.
- Demonstrated ability to debug software and hardware issues, identify root causes, and provide effective solutions.
- Knowledge of system hardware/software validation techniques and methodologies.
- Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI) for reporting metrics and tracking progress.

Preferred Qualifications:


- Solid understanding of x86 architecture and its interactions with hardware and software components.
- Hands-on experience with silicon debug tools, failure analysis methods, or system-level validation infrastructure.
- Familiarity with AI-driven workflows or tools for test plan development and analysis.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a cross-functional team environment.
- Enthusiasm for innovation and advancing validation processes through new methodologies and tools.

Join us at Intel and contribute to shaping the future of semiconductor technology. Be part of a team that values innovation, collaboration, and excellence-apply today.

title: Power Thermal Validation and Power Management Engineer - SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation (Temporary position)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

As a SoC Power Thermal Performance Validation and Optimization Engineer, you will play an essential role in ensuring Intel's products achieve optimal power, thermal, and performance benchmarks at the system-on-chip (SoC) level.

In this position, you will develop and execute validation methodologies, optimize hardware/software solutions, and perform SoC-level debugging to address power, thermal, and performance challenges. Your contribution will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver competitive, high-performing products to market.


This is a Temporary position (12 months)


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute System-on-Chip (SoC)-level power, thermal, performance, and Power Management validation and optimization plans across Intel products.
  • Collaborate with architecture, design, firmware, and software teams to ensure power, thermal, performance, and Power Management meet competitive targets and specifications.
  • Establish and execute leakage, Dynamic Capacitance (Cdyn), Thermal Design Power (TDP), Digital Thermal Sensor (DTS), thermal protectors (Catastrophic Trip, Processor Hot), Inverse Temperature Dependence (ITD), thermal margin, System-to-- Tester (S2T) correlation, data collection for the Electrical Critical Path (ECP), and Power Management methodologies - CPU idle power States (C-states), Package C6 (pkgC6), link low-power states (L1, L0p), tunings (Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling, ring scalability, Power Virus Pattern, Running Average Power Limit, etc.), Fixed Frequency Performance (FFP) and Power Constrained Performance (PCP) recipes - to validate hardware/software optimizations and ensure alignment with business Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
  • Perform System-on-Chip (SoC)-level debug to identify root causes and resolve functional and triage failures related to power, thermal, Power Management, and performance.
  • Configure and set up data acquisition/loggers' equipment (e.g. Yokogawa) to collect and analyze power-thermal data.
  • Develop and maintain validation infrastructure, including power/performance monitors, behavioral checkers, and testing environments.
  • Produce comprehensive validation reports summarizing activities and results and communicates findings effectively to relevant teams.
  • Drive continuous improvements to validation strategies, methodologies, and processes.

The ideal candidate should show the following behavioral traits

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving aptitude.
  • Effective communication and documentation skills for cross-functional collaboration.
  • Willing to work across team in multi-faceted groups (architecture, design, verification, firmware, software, and platform teams.)

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelors in Electronics, Electrical, Computer Engineering, or related field.
  • 1+ years of experience in SoC power, thermal, performance, and/or power management validation.
  • 1+ years of experience developing and / or optimization of power/performance and power management KPI's.
  • Advanced English level.

Must have unrestricted, permanent right to work in Mexico (this role is not eligible for visa or immigration sponsorship).

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • A Master's degree in is preferred.
  • Debugging experience for SoC-level power, thermal, performance, and power management failures.
  • Knowledge of hardware/software optimizations for power, thermal, performance, and power management.
  • Experience with System (SoC) level debug using JTAG debuggers.
  • Familiarity with validation tools such as data acquisition/loggers (i.e. Yokogawa), behavioral checkers, and state space coverage techniques.
  • Familiar with system board design/debugging and usage of lab equipment like Oscilloscope and Logic analyzer.
  • Experience with power-thermal and performance modeling, benchmarking, and validation infrastructure setup.
  • Experience with Python Programming language.


Requirements may be met through a combination of relevant industry experience, internship experience, and/or academic work, coursework, or research. Candidates who have completed their degree and whose professional experience is limited to internships may also be considered.

title: Graduate Talent (Firmware Development)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we create world-changing technology that enriches the lives of every person on Earth. For more than 50 years, Intel innovations have powered the computing breakthroughs that shape how people live, work, and connect.

The Physical AI, Client and Edge (PACE) organization within the Client Computing & Physical AI Group (CCPG) is driving the next wave of intelligent computing by bringing Artificial Intelligence closer to where data is created and decisions are made. From intelligent edge devices and robotics to autonomous systems and AI-enabled industrial solutions, PACE develops technologies that enable the future of Physical AI.

As part of this mission, the Firmware & Functional Safety Technologies (FFST) organization develops critical platform firmware technologies that power Intel's next-generation products. Firmware is where hardware and software come together, enabling silicon features, platform reliability, security, performance, and functional safety capabilities.

As a Graduate Talent in the Boot Firmware Engineering (BFE) team, you will work alongside experienced firmware engineers to develop and validate low-level platform firmware for Intel reference platforms. You will gain hands-on experience in platform initialization, silicon enablement, system debugging, firmware automation, and AI-assisted engineering workflows while contributing to technologies that power millions of computing devices worldwide.

What You Will Do

  • Develop, integrate, and validate boot firmware components for Intel client and edge computing platforms.
  • Participate in firmware architecture discussions, feature design reviews, and requirement definition activities.
  • Design and execute unit tests, integration tests, and platform validation methodologies to ensure robust firmware quality.
  • Investigate, debug, and root-cause hardware, firmware, and system-level issues using industry-standard debugging tools and methodologies.
  • Develop automation scripts and engineering tools to improve development efficiency, test coverage, and product quality.
  • Collaborate closely with silicon architects, hardware designers, software engineers, validation teams, and platform integrators across Intel's global engineering network.
  • Apply Generative AI and Agentic AI solutions to accelerate code development, debugging, validation, knowledge discovery, test creation, and engineering productivity.
  • Explore new approaches to AI-powered firmware engineering by leveraging autonomous AI agents, intelligent workflow automation, and large language models (LLMs).
     

Qualifications:

We are seeking passionate graduates who enjoy understanding how systems work from silicon to software and are excited to build the technologies behind tomorrow's intelligent devices.

Successful candidates often demonstrate a strong curiosity for both hardware and software and enjoy building things beyond academic coursework.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in:
    • Computer Engineering
    • Electrical & Electronic Engineering
    • Computer Science
    • Embedded Systems
    • Mechatronics
    • Robotics
    • Related engineering disciplines
  • Strong programming skills in one or more of the following:
    • C
    • C++
    • Python
  • Understanding of computer architecture, embedded systems, operating systems, and software development fundamentals.
  • Strong analytical thinking, debugging skills, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.
  • Passion for learning emerging technologies and solving challenging technical problems.

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates will have an advantage if they possess hands-on experience through personal projects, hackathons, internships, university projects, or open-source contributions involving:

Embedded and Hardware Projects

  • Arduino, ESP32, STM32, RP2040, PIC, MSP430, or similar microcontroller platforms.
  • Raspberry Pi, Jetson Orin Nano, BeagleBone, or other embedded Linux platforms.
  • Robotics, IoT, sensor integration, autonomous systems, drones, or industrial automation projects.
  • Embedded Linux, RTOS, device drivers, or bare-metal firmware development.

AI and Intelligent Systems

  • Machine Learning or AI projects using TensorFlow, PyTorch, OpenVINO, ONNX, or similar frameworks.
  • Edge AI deployment on embedded devices.
  • Computer vision, speech AI, robotics AI, or autonomous systems projects.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI coding assistants.

Agentic AI and Engineering Productivity

  • Development of AI agents, autonomous workflows, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, or multi-agent applications.
  • Experience integrating LLMs into software applications or engineering workflows.
  • Building automation pipelines that leverage AI for testing, debugging, code generation, or data analysis.

Additional Differentiators

  • Active GitHub portfolio showcasing personal technical projects.
  • Participation in hackathons, maker communities, robotics competitions, engineering clubs, or open-source initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to take an idea from concept to working prototype.

We're especially interested in builders and makers. If you've spent your free time creating projects with Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, robotics kits, autonomous vehicles, smart home systems, AI-powered devices, or other embedded platforms, we'd love to hear about them. We value candidates who are curious, hands-on, and passionate about understanding how hardware and software work together to create intelligent systems. Experience using AI tools to accelerate development and solve complex engineering problems is highly desirable.

title: Director, Government Affairs - Korea
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role


Join Intel and help build a better tomorrow. Intel is in the midst of an exciting transformation, with a vision to create and extend computing technology that connects and enriches the lives of every person on Earth. Join us and help create the next generation of technologies that will shape the future for decades to come.
Intel's International Government Affairs team is seeking a dynamic and experienced leader to join our Korea team as Director of Government Affairs.


In this role, you will work closely with Intel Korea, the Director for Korea International Government Affairs ( IGA) and the Vice President of International Government Affairs to develop and execute a comprehensive government relations strategy that supports a favorable semiconductor policy and regulatory environment for Intel's growth and operations.


The Director will also be responsible for maintaining excellent relationships and networks with key government stakeholders at the national, prefectural, and local levels. This leader will play an important role in positively positioning Intel, building a sound reputation and position of influence for the company, and establishing Intel as a trusted and influential partner in Korea.


Key Responsibilities


The Director of Korea Government Affairs will:


  • Represent Intel on legislative and regulatory matters with relevant government bodies and support the implementation of all phases of regulatory strategy to help secure necessary approvals for company products and services.
  • Provide strategic policy direction and coordinate Intel's efforts to engage with government, both directly and through key opinion leaders, industry associations, foreign diplomatic missions, business chambers, media, and public-private partnerships.
  • Develop and implement programs that increase awareness and appreciation of Intel's value proposition and strengthen the company's reputation in Korea.
  • Oversee Intel's lobbying activities in Korea and provide strategic direction and oversight to lobbyists, consultants, industry associations, and other external organizations engaged by Intel.
  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with external partners, industry organizations, business chambers, regulators, policymakers, and key opinion leaders.
  • Work closely with the Government of Korea, including METI, MEXT, MIC, the Cabinet Office/Digital Agency, universities, national laboratories, and other relevant institutions to influence key decisions and position Intel as a trusted partner.
  • Monitor the industry and government for intelligence sensing of emerging issues, anticompetitive behavior, and related risks, and advise on necessary action.
  • Partner closely with Intel Korea and internal stakeholders, including Sales and Marketing, Bus and the Digital Readiness program to identify key engagement opportunities and develop coordinated government engagement strategies that support Intel's business objectives and long-term success.
  • Serve as an active member of the broader business community by participating in relevant activities and initiatives, including leadership and engagement with business chambers, industry associations, and other external organizations.

Qualifications


The successful candidate must have detailed knowledge of how the Government of Korea functions, including its structure and legislative processes at the national, prefectural, and local levels.


Additional qualifications include:

  • Native-level Korean language skills and proficiency in business English.
  • Strong understanding of the issues affecting multinational businesses operating in Korea, as well as policies impacting the semiconductor and technology industries.
  • Exceptional diplomatic and negotiation skills, complemented by strong presentation, writing, and verbal communication capabilities.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and evaluating government affairs and public policy strategies.
  • Strong business savvy with the ability to link government functions to overall company objectives and generate significant accomplishments with minimal supervision.
  • Working knowledge and understanding of computing technologies.
  • A positive, outgoing, and professional presence with the ability to effectively represent Intel in external forums and engage credibly with senior government and ministerial officials.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team in a multicultural environment.
  • Strong partnership and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish and maintain effective professional relationships with both internal and external stakeholders

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in International Relations, Public Policy, Government Relations, Political Science, Law, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of related experience in government relations, regulatory affairs, and/or public affairs within a multinational company, NGO, or government organization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree with 10+ years of related experience in government relations, regulatory affairs, and/or public affairs within a multinational company, NGO, or government organization.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Robotics Solution Architect to define and develop end-to-end technical solutions for humanoid robotics. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. title: Principal Engineer, Analog and Mixed-Signal DTCO
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Group:

Intel's Advanced Design Foundational IP Organization (AD-FIP) within Design Technology Platform (DTP) drives pathfinding and development of the analog/mixed-signal, RF, and high-speed I/O IP that defines what Intel Foundry's leading-edge process technologies can deliver. The AMS Design-Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) team sits at the intersection of process technology, design rules, PDK, EDA tools, and circuit design, making sure each new node delivers competitive analog, mixed-signal, and custom-design density, performance, and productivity.

The Role:

We are seeking a senior technical leader in DTCO to define and drive co-optimization of Intel Foundry's next-generation process technologies for analog, mixed-signal, and custom design. You will identify where technology definition limits design outcomes (density, drive, matching, high-voltage support, layout productivity), quantify the impact, and drive resolution across process, design-rule, PDK, EDA, and design teams. This is a senior individual-contributor role with technical leadership across multiple organizations and external EDA partners.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead AMS DTCO for future Intel Foundry nodes: evaluate device architecture, front-end and back-end design rules, metal stack, and patterning choices against analog, mixed-signal, and custom-design requirements.
  • Run a closed-loop DTCO process: sense issues from designers, partners, and test chips; prioritize by PPA and productivity impact; drive rule, PDK, or flow changes; and validate the result on silicon and in design.
  • Quantify technology impact on circuits through layout studies, parasitic-aware benchmarking, and area and performance scaling analysis of representative AMS building blocks.
  • Define and drive design-rule and PDK requirements with process, design-rule, OPC, and quality and reliability teams, including high-voltage device support, density and fill rules, metal width and spacing options, and layout-dependent effects.
  • Partner with EDA vendors on node enablement for custom and AMS flows: custom layout, analog placement and routing, physical verification, fill, and extraction; translate tool and flow feedback into technology decisions.
  • Represent Intel Foundry in technical engagements with EDA partners and foundry customers, and present DTCO findings and recommendations to technology and business leadership.
  • Mentor engineers and set technical direction for the DTCO team.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of DTCO experience for analog, mixed-signal, I/O, or custom design on FinFET or more advanced process nodes, at a foundry, an IDM technology-development organization, or an EDA vendor.
  • And experience in at least one of the following:
    • Design-rule definition for analog or custom layout, including layout-pattern studies, layout-dependent effects, and test-structure design to evaluate rule impact.
    • Circuit-level technology benchmarking of analog or mixed-signal building blocks: device-model and parasitic evaluation, matching, and area or performance scaling analysis.
    • EDA tool or flow enablement of analog and custom design for a new process node: custom layout, analog placement and routing, physical verification, fill, or extraction.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

  • Hands-on analog, mixed-signal, or RF circuit design experience (for example PLLs, data converters, regulators, high-speed I/O, LNAs, PAs, or mmWave front ends), with an understanding of how device and interconnect parameters drive circuit performance.
  • Analog and RF device and passive technology: precision resistors, MIM/MOM capacitors, inductors and transformers, varactors, analog and RF device flavors, and RF figures of merit such as fT, fmax, and noise figure.
  • Experience across two or more of the areas in the minimum qualifications, or across both foundry and EDA environments.
  • High-voltage or extended-voltage device integration on advanced CMOS nodes.
  • Analog or custom layout design experience.
  • Gate-all-around transistors, backside power delivery, or advanced multi-patterning (SALELE, EUV) technology definition as it affects analog and custom layout.
  • Automation of DTCO studies using Python, layout generators, or machine learning.
  • Customer-facing technical engagement with foundry customers or EDA partners.
  • Publications at IEDM, VLSI Symposium, CICC, ISSCC, or RFIC; patents in DTCO, design rules, design enablement, or AMS/RF circuits.
  • Technical leadership across process, design, and EDA organizations, including driving technology-definition decisions at node level.

Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or a related field
  • Industry experience in semiconductor technology development, design enablement, or circuit design
  • Master's degree with 15+ years of experience OR Ph.D. with 12+ years of experience.

Business Group

Join Intel Foundry Technology Development and help advance the next generation of patterning.

You will operate in a high impact space, partnering closely with cross functional teams (Process Integration, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Yield/Defect Engineering, and suppliers) to solve complex technical challenges and establish long term systems that sustain performance.   • Drive technology development for future technology and high-volume manufacturing, provide process integration and equipment solutions, and perform feasibility studies to meet desired device specifications.

title: Senior Principal Engineer, Device Design
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Group

Intel is transforming from an Integrated Device Manufacturer (IDM) to a leading global foundry service provider, offering world-class manufacturing capabilities to external customers worldwide. Our Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) organization is at the forefront of this transformation-focusing on technology customization, yield improvement, performance optimization, and exceptional customer delivery.


About the Role
We are seeking a highly accomplished Senior Principal Device Design Engineer with broad semiconductor industry expertise to drive the high-level architecture, definition, and optimization of next-generation and high-volume manufacturing (HVM) semiconductor technologies. In this strategic technical leadership role, you will apply a deep mastery of semiconductor device physics to define technical roadmaps and ensure world-class performance across a diverse range of applications-including advanced logic, SRAM, low-power mobile, analog, and mixed-signal designs.
Serving as a primary technical bridge between Process Integration, Yield, and Module Engineering, and collaborative product partners, you will establish the technical direction, target validations, and silicon-to-simulation accuracy across Intel's diverse technology portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Technical Strategy and Architecture Leadership: Lead cross-functional, multi-disciplinary teams in defining base and derivative semiconductor architectures-including advanced transistors, interconnects, and design rules-tailored for high-performance logic, low-power, memory, analog, and mixed-signal applications.
  • Technical Partner and Customer Engagement: Partner directly with external customers, product design teams, and internal engineering groups to understand complex product requirements, resolve circuit-level performance/reliability/leakage trade-offs, and translate product needs into tailored silicon solutions.
  • Technology Customization and Optimization: Drive the development and implementation of customized semiconductor features across logic and memory technologies, ensuring seamless integration with existing manufacturing processes and platforms to support specialized applications.
  • Silicon-to-Simulation Readiness: Set and govern device and interconnect performance targets, evaluating silicon-to-simulation health, model readiness, and design feasibility for large-volume manufacturing.
  • Cross-Functional Integration: Serve as the authoritative technical interface bridging Process Integration, Process Module, Device Physics, Yield Engineering, and Product Design to coordinate complex technology handoffs and resolve system-level constraints.
  • Design Rule and Waiver Governance: Direct the validation and strategic waiver management processes for advanced design rules, balancing strict manufacturing compliance and yield with product design flexibility.
  • Advanced Data Analytics: Guide the evaluation of electrical test (E-test) and yield data using advanced statistical methods and data analysis techniques to translate experimental silicon data into actionable process and design intelligence.
  • Mentorship and Industry Thought Leadership: Provide senior technical mentorship to engineers and researchers across the organization, stay ahead of emerging semiconductor industry trends, and foster a culture of technical excellence and customer-centric innovation.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • Progressive experience in the semiconductor industry with a strong focus on CMOS device physics, device design, and semiconductor technology development.
  • Leadership and Technology Integration: Demonstrated technical leadership within the semiconductor industry, specifically leading cross-functional teams to define, develop, and deliver advanced semiconductor technologies (covering logic, memory, or integrated architectures) and design rules into High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM).
  • Design Rule Governance: Deep proficiency in design rule development, validation, and waiver management processes, with a strong understanding of how layout constraints impact product yield.
  • Data and Analytical Mastery: Proven expertise in statistical data analysis, Design of Experiments (DOE), and data interpretation to evaluate test chip, E-test, and yield trends.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Advanced and Specialty Node Expertise: Architectural experience in advanced-node transistor design and scaling, with deep experience in specialized semiconductor customization for low-power, analog, mixed-signal, and memory technologies.
  • Physical Verification and Mask Flows: High-level familiarity with physical verification flows, Design Rule Checker (DRC) development, and mask generation concepts.
  • Manufacturing and SPC: Extensive experience in a High-Volume Manufacturing (HVM) environment with a focus on statistical process control (SPC) and yield monitoring.
  • Executive Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and guide collaborative partners through complex technical trade-offs.

Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Material Science, or a related field. PhD preferred
  • 15+ years of relevant semiconductor device and technology development experience.

title: C4 Bump Module Equipment Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel Malaysia's newest Advanced Packaging startup team in Penang and help shape the future of semiconductor manufacturing. As part of a factory ramp from the ground up, you will work with advanced wafer manufacturing and packaging technologies, collaborate with global engineering teams, and play a key role in bringing new capabilities into high-volume production. This unique opportunity offers unparalleled exposure to factory startup activities, rapid professional growth, and the chance to leave your mark on one of Intel's most significant manufacturing expansions.


Job Summary

  • The Equipment Technician plays a critical role in the startup, ramp, and sustained operation of advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment supporting high-volume Advanced Packaging production.
  • This position is responsible for maintaining equipment performance, reliability, and availability through troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, equipment recovery, and continuous improvement activities.
  • The Equipment Technician partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, and equipment suppliers to support manufacturing readiness, operational excellence, yield, quality, and factory output while ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and quality requirements.
  • Performs electrical, mechanical, electronic, and/or mechatronic troubleshooting to identify and resolve problems with semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
  • Performs equipment setup, calibration, preventive maintenance, repair, adjustment, component replacement, and equipment recovery in accordance with approved procedures, specifications, equipment manuals, drawings, and safety requirements.
  • Monitors and analyzes equipment performance and manufacturing data to identify abnormalities, equipment degradation, and conditions that may affect equipment availability, process stability, manufacturing output, yield, or product quality.
  • Responds to equipment alarms, equipment-related excursions, and manufacturing interruptions in accordance with established procedures to restore equipment to required operating conditions.
  • Collects relevant equipment data, performs authorized troubleshooting, and works with Equipment, Module, and Process Engineering teams to identify root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Performs routine equipment health monitoring and supports the early identification of equipment conditions or trends that could impact manufacturing performance, reliability, capacity, or manufacturing readiness.
  • Works with Engineering teams to execute approved experiments, equipment characterization, process qualifications, equipment configuration changes, and continuous improvement initiatives. Supports equipment troubleshooting through data analysis, root cause investigation, and controlled experimentation to maintain or improve equipment availability, reliability, performance, and manufacturing readiness.
  • Supports established Statistical Process Control (SPC), equipment monitoring, fault detection, and manufacturing control systems by responding to equipment-related abnormalities according to defined procedures and escalation requirements.
  • Utilizes equipment performance data and system indicators to proactively identify opportunities for improved equipment stability and operational performance.
  • Coordinates with OEMs, equipment suppliers, and technical support organizations for troubleshooting, repair, servicing, component replacement, equipment recovery, and reliability improvements when required.
  • Works closely with Equipment Engineering, Process Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, and other support teams to resolve equipment-related manufacturing issues and support production objectives.
  • Creates and maintains equipment failure reports, maintenance records, troubleshooting documentation, calibration records, qualification records, and other technical documentation supporting equipment performance, reliability, and compliance requirements.
  • During factory startup and ramp, supports equipment installation, acceptance, setup, conversion, qualification, and manufacturing readiness activities in accordance with approved designs, specifications, and procedures.
  • Contributes to the successful introduction of new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities supporting Advanced Packaging operations.
  • Drives a culture of safety, quality, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
  • Performs assigned work in accordance with applicable EHS, cleanroom, quality, contamination control, and manufacturing work-control requirements.

Qualifications:

Education

  • Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Experience

  • Fresh graduates with strong technical aptitude and an interest in semiconductor manufacturing are encouraged to apply.
  • Relevant experience in semiconductor manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, electronics manufacturing, equipment maintenance, equipment troubleshooting, automation, or other high-volume manufacturing environments is an advantage.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with semiconductor manufacturing equipment troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, repair, setup, calibration, and equipment recovery.
  • Familiarity with semiconductor wafer fabrication, Advanced Packaging, assembly, test, or other high-volume manufacturing processes and equipment.
  • Familiarity with equipment and process monitoring methodologies, including Statistical Process Control (SPC), equipment performance monitoring, excursion management, and data-driven problem solving.
  • Experience interpreting equipment alarms, diagnostic information, technical documentation, schematics, engineering drawings, specifications, maintenance procedures, and equipment manuals.
  • Familiarity with structured troubleshooting methodologies, failure analysis, root cause investigation, and implementation of corrective actions.
  • Experience supporting equipment installation, startup, qualification, manufacturing readiness, production ramp, or equipment conversion activities is an added advantage.
  • Familiarity with automated material handling systems (AMHS), robotics, wafer handling systems, process equipment, metrology tools, automation platforms, manufacturing execution systems (MES), and manufacturing control systems is an added advantage.
  • Experience working with OEMs, suppliers, or technical service organizations to support equipment troubleshooting and maintenance activities is an added advantage.

Other Requirements

  • Strong technical aptitude and systematic problem-solving skills.
  • Basic understanding of mechanical, electrical, electronic, automation, pneumatic, vacuum, and/or mechatronic systems.
  • Basic understanding of semiconductor manufacturing operations and the relationship between equipment condition, process stability, yield, manufacturing performance, and product quality.
  • Ability to interpret and follow technical documentation, equipment manuals, schematics, specifications, maintenance procedures, and work instructions.
  • Ability to identify abnormal equipment or manufacturing conditions and respond or escalate in accordance with established procedures.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills, including the ability to collaborate effectively with Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, OEMs, suppliers, and cross-functional support teams.
  • Demonstrated learning agility and the ability to quickly acquire proficiency on new equipment, manufacturing processes, automation systems, and technologies.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to safety, quality, equipment reliability, and operational excellence.
  • Willing and able to work in a semiconductor cleanroom environment while adhering to contamination control, safety, and quality requirements.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and willingness to support factory startup, equipment installation, qualification, production ramp, and evolving manufacturing requirements in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • This role requires regular onsite presence to fulfill essential job responsibilities.
  • Willing and able to work shift schedules, including rotating day and night shifts, as required to support manufacturing operations.
  • Able to support overtime, weekends, public holidays, factory startup, production ramp, and equipment recovery activities based on business and manufacturing requirements.

title: System Debug Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
